claims.text: SHANK3 protein is detectable in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and is markedly reduced in people with PMS compared with controls (mean -77%).
claims.n: 23 individuals with PMS, plus a control group of unstated size
claims.eff: mean -77% vs controls; dispersion not reported in the abstract
claims.limA: Described by the authors as a pilot study; they call for validation in larger paediatric longitudinal cohorts.
claims.limO: Control group size, age and sex distribution not stated in the abstract. A 77% reduction is larger than the ~50% expected from haploinsufficiency alone, which the abstract does not explain.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: SHANK3 protein in PBMCs

claims.text: Lower SHANK3 levels in peripheral blood mononuclear cells are associated with the presence of developmental regression in PMS.
claims.limA: Pilot study; authors position this as a target-engagement or monitoring marker, explicitly not a diagnostic screen.
claims.limO: An association within 23 individuals, with regression as a binary. No adjustment or subgroup size is reported in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: PBMC SHANK3 level against presence of developmental regression

claims.text: Plasma beta-synuclein is elevated in PMS and correlates positively with the severity of speech impairment.
claims.limA: Pilot study; validation requested in larger and paediatric longitudinal cohorts.
claims.limO: Beta-synuclein is a neuron-specific synaptic protein but is not specific to SHANK3 biology; specificity against other neurodevelopmental conditions is not addressed in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: plasma beta-synuclein against speech impairment severity

claims.text: In a Shank3 transgenic mouse model, beta-synuclein levels were normalised through modulation of the mGlu5 receptor.
claims.limO: The allele, the compound, the dose and the sample size are all absent from the abstract. This record is close to uninformative until the full text is read, and is kept chiefly because it is the only back-translation link between the human marker and an intervention.
claims.model: Shank3 transgenic; specific allele not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: beta-synuclein level

claims.text: The 40 Hz auditory steady-state response is reduced in siblings with a SHANK3 frameshift variant and preserved in their unaffected sibling.
claims.eff: statistically significant in the younger affected child; non-significant in the older affected sibling
claims.limA: Authors note reduced sensitivity in early adulthood and call for age-stratified normative control datasets before individual-level interpretation.
claims.limO: A single family, n=3. The within-family design controls background genetics well but cannot support generalisation.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: auditory steady-state response at 16, 27 and 40 Hz, EEG

claims.text: Sensitivity of the 40 Hz auditory steady-state response as a marker appears to decline with age, being significant in childhood and non-significant in early adulthood.
claims.limO: An age effect inferred from two individuals of different ages. Age and individual are completely confounded in this design.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: 40 Hz ASSR by age

claims.text: Reduced 40 Hz intertrial phase coherence discriminates people with PMS from typically developing controls (AUROC 0.83).
claims.n: 123 participants: 42 typically developing, 56 idiopathic ASD, 25 PMS
claims.limA: Classification of idiopathic ASD versus PMS performed poorly in the full sample.
claims.limO: Preprint, not peer reviewed. Leave-one-out cross-validation on 25 PMS participants gives an optimistic and unstable AUROC; no independent validation cohort.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: 40 Hz ASSR intertrial phase coherence, EEG, classified with XGBoost under leave-one-out cross-validation

claims.text: About 36% of people with idiopathic autism show a PMS-like gamma-band phase-locking profile.
claims.limO: The index is defined by a model trained on 25 PMS participants, so the 36% figure inherits that model's instability. Preprint.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Synchrony Atypicality Index derived from the PMS-versus-TD model

claims.text: Transient beta event rate on EEG is elevated in a majority of children with PMS relative to typically developing controls.
claims.limO: Preprint, not peer reviewed. No sample size, no effect size and no dispersion in the abstract. Elevation is also reported in Rett and SYNGAP1-related disorder, so the marker is not specific to PMS.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: transient beta event rate, EEG

claims.text: People with SHANK3 sequence variants show lower adaptive behaviour skills than people with 22q13 deletions, irrespective of deletion size.
claims.limO: Cross-sectional, 56 individuals, with the SHANK3-variant subgroup size not stated. The comparison that matters most to this project rests on an unreported subgroup n.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Third Edition; ADI-R

claims.text: Genomic parameters were largely unrelated to ADI-R autism scores in a cohort of 56 people with PMS.
claims.limO: A null result stated without the statistical test, the power or the confidence interval. Absence of an association in 56 people is weak evidence that none exists.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: ADI-R domain scores against deletion size and variant type

claims.text: Metabolic profiling distinguishes people with PMS from controls, and distinguishes those meeting the ADI-R autism cutoff from those who do not.
claims.n: 56 individuals with PMS, plus controls of unstated size
claims.limO: High-dimensional profiling in 56 individuals without a stated correction for multiple comparisons or an independent validation set.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Biolog Phenotype Mammalian MicroArray (PM-M) metabolic profiles

claims.text: A distinct metabolic profile for individuals with PMS showed a reduced ability to metabolize major energy sources and a higher metabolism of alternative energy sources.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: The abstract reports no effect sizes, no p values and no multiple-comparison handling for a profiling study that necessarily tests many substrates. Neither the biosample nor the assay platform is named, so the marker cannot be reproduced from this record. Controls are not characterised by age, sex or intellectual disability status, so a metabolic difference attributable to mobility, diet, medication or institutional setting cannot be separated from one attributable to SHANK3.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: metabolic profiling (energy-source utilisation); assay platform and biosample not stated in the abstract

claims.text: The analysis of the metabolic response to hGH or IGF-1 showed a major overlap between both high and low responders, suggesting that the two growth factors share many target pathways.
claims.n: subgroups formed from the top and bottom 25% of 48 individuals with PMS; subgroup sizes not reported
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: The authors treat the overlap between hGH and IGF-1 responders as 'validating the model', but this is internal consistency within one dataset, not validation: the subgroups were defined by response and then compared on response, with no independent sample, no held-out set and no cross-validation described. Taking the top and bottom 25% of a 48-person sample also maximises apparent separation and inflates any effect relative to the full distribution. Subgroup sizes, effect sizes and p values are all absent.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: metabolic response to hGH and to IGF-1, compared between high- and low-responder subgroups

claims.text: When the effect of hGH and IGF-1 on the metabolism of glucose was investigated, the correlation between the high-responder subgroups showed less similarity, whereas the low-responders were still relatively similar.
claims.n: top and bottom 25% responder subgroups of 48 individuals with PMS; subgroup sizes not reported
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: 'Less similarity' and 'relatively similar' are reported without correlation coefficients, confidence intervals or any test of the difference between the two correlations, so the asymmetry between high and low responders cannot be distinguished from sampling noise in subgroups of unstated and probably small size.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: correlation of glucose metabolism between hGH and IGF-1 responder subgroups

claims.text: The examined group was too small to conclude that the expression of SHANK1, SHANK2, SHANK3 and SHARPIN genes in peripheral blood mononuclear cells can be used as a biomarker facilitating diagnosis and treatment of autism spectrum disorder.
claims.limA: The authors state the examined group was too small to support a diagnostic conclusion, and that peripheral blood is accessible but not easily collected.
claims.limO: A null result with no sample size, no control group description, no effect estimate and no power calculation anywhere in the abstract, so the finding cannot be read as evidence of absence. The cohort is idiopathic ASD, not PMS: no participant is reported to carry a SHANK3 variant, so this says little about whether PBMC SHANK3 expression tracks SHANK3 dosage in PMS. Not peer reviewed. Direction is recorded as no_change to mean 'no usable discrimination reported', not a demonstrated equivalence.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: SHANK1, SHANK2, SHANK3 and SHARPIN gene expression in peripheral venous blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs)

claims.text: Individuals with Phelan-McDermid syndrome have significant sleep abnormalities on the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire when compared with unaffected siblings.
claims.n: 47 individuals with PMS (male 23, female 24) versus 61 unaffected siblings (male 25, female 36)
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: The PMS group spans 1-46 years while the sibling comparison group spans only 1-17 years, so the groups are not age-matched and the CSHQ is a paediatric instrument applied well outside its validated age range for part of the PMS sample. No effect size or p value is given in the abstract. The measure is parent-report, and parents of an affected child are not blind to group; no actigraphy or polysomnography is reported for the PMS group. Sleep disturbance is common across intellectual disability generally, so nothing here is specific to SHANK3.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: sleep disturbance, Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ), parent-report

claims.text: SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability shows greater severity of sleep disturbance than Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
claims.n: 47 individuals with PMS and 64 with SYNGAP1-ID (male 31, female 33), aged 1-64 years
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: A between-syndrome comparison with no reported adjustment for the very different age ranges or for severity of intellectual disability, either of which could account for the difference. No effect size or p value in the abstract. Direction is recorded relative to PMS, i.e. PMS is the less severely affected group.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: sleep disturbance severity, CSHQ, compared between two synaptopathy groups

claims.text: Sleep disturbances were more severe in individuals with PMS aged 11 years and older compared with those under 11 years old.
claims.n: subgroups of the 47 individuals with PMS; subgroup sizes not reported
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: A post-hoc age split of 47 people into two subgroups of unstated size, with no stated justification for the 11-year cut-point, no effect size and no correction for the fact that a second age threshold (10 years) was used in the preprint version of the same study (R-0110). Cross-sectional data cannot distinguish worsening with age from cohort effects.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: sleep disturbance severity, CSHQ, by age band

claims.text: Individuals with PMS or SYNGAP1-ID were more likely to use sleep aids than unaffected siblings.
claims.n: 47 PMS and 64 SYNGAP1-ID versus 61 unaffected siblings
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: Sleep-aid use is a treatment-seeking behaviour, not a sleep measure, and it confounds the CSHQ comparison in the same paper: individuals already medicated for sleep are included in the group whose sleep is being characterised, without any reported stratification by medication status. The two syndrome groups are pooled in the abstract, so the PMS-specific rate is not recoverable.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: reported use of sleep aids

claims.text: There was a statistically significant decrease in uncinate fasciculus fractional anisotropy and a statistically significant increase in uncinate fasciculus mean diffusivity in children with Phelan-McDermid syndrome versus age-matched controls, in both right and left tracts.
claims.n: 10 participants with PMS (50% male; 8 with autism), compared with age-matched controls of unstated number
claims.eff: P <= 0.024; no effect estimate or confidence interval reported
claims.limA: The authors state that these findings need to be replicated in a larger cohort.
claims.limO: n = 10, with four tract-by-metric comparisons reported and a p value at the threshold (0.024) with no stated correction for multiple comparisons. The number, age distribution and sex of the control group are not given, and controls were enrolled in a separate study under a different protocol and, presumably, a different scanner cohort; 'age-matched' is asserted but not evidenced in the abstract. 8 of 10 participants had autism, so autism and PMS cannot be separated. White-matter diffusivity changes are non-specific and are reported across many neurodevelopmental conditions.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity, diffusion tensor imaging tractography

claims.text: The study investigated trends between autism spectrum diagnosis and the integrity of the uncinate fasciculus and inferior longitudinal fasciculus, and reported a significant group difference only for the uncinate fasciculus.
claims.limA: The authors state the findings need to be replicated in a larger cohort.
claims.limO: This is a null recorded by omission: the abstract names the inferior longitudinal fasciculus in the title and aims but reports a significant result only for the uncinate fasciculus, and gives no statistics at all for the inferior longitudinal fasciculus or for the autism-diagnosis trend. With n = 10 and 8 of 10 autistic, the study has no usable power to detect either, so the absence of a reported difference is uninformative rather than negative. Recorded so that the silence is counted rather than lost.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity of the inferior longitudinal fasciculus, DTI tractography

claims.text: Sleep disturbances were more severe for both Phelan-McDermid syndrome and SYNGAP1-ID in individuals 10 years and older compared with those less than 10 years old, when compared with healthy controls.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: The preprint abstract reports no sample sizes at all, no effect sizes and no p values. It describes the comparison group as 'healthy controls' where the peer-reviewed version describes 'unaffected siblings', and it places the age threshold at 10 years where the published version places it at 11. Not peer reviewed.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: sleep disturbance severity, Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ), by age band

claims.text: Review of polysomnography studies for individuals with SYNGAP1-ID revealed significant reduction in REM sleep content and delayed REM latency, demonstrating abnormalities in sleep architecture.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: No polysomnography result is reported for the PMS group at all: the objective sleep-architecture data in this study cover SYNGAP1-ID only, so the one measure here that is not parent-report says nothing about PMS. A retrospective review of existing clinical polysomnograms, with no stated number of studies, no normative comparison group and no statistics. Not peer reviewed, and this finding does not appear in the abstract of the peer-reviewed version.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: REM sleep content and REM latency, polysomnography

claims.text: In a Shank3-transgenic mouse model, motor coordination and endurance were impaired while muscle strength was unchanged.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no effect sizes and no p values anywhere in the abstract, and no genetic background stated although background is known to modify Shank3 phenotypes. The allele is described only as 'Shank3-transgenic', which does not identify which isoforms are lost - the single most important determinant of phenotype in this literature. The dissociation between impaired endurance and unchanged strength is reported without power, so the null on strength cannot be interpreted. Muscular hypotonia is a core PMS feature, which makes an uninterpretable null on strength a material gap rather than an incidental one.
claims.model: Shank3-transgenic knockout, heterozygous and homozygous; targeted exons and affected isoforms not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: motor coordination, endurance and muscle strength; specific paradigms not named in the abstract

claims.text: The animals displayed only minor impairments in social behavior, but pronounced stereotypic and repetitive behaviors.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: The near-null on social behaviour is the most consequential result in this abstract, since social deficit is the phenotype Shank3 mouse models are most often used to represent, and it is reported with no n, no effect size and no power analysis - exactly the conditions under which a null is uninterpretable. The authors themselves flag it as 'surprising', which signals a discrepancy with prior Shank3 mouse work that the abstract does not reconcile.
claims.model: Shank3-transgenic knockout, heterozygous and homozygous; targeted exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: social interaction and repetitive/stereotypic behaviour; paradigms not named in the abstract

claims.text: Spatial learning and memory were unchanged in the Shank3 knockout animals, while cognitive flexibility was slightly impaired.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: A null on spatial learning reported without sample size or power, alongside a positive finding described only as 'slightly impaired' with no quantification. A 'slight' impairment stated without an effect size cannot be distinguished from noise, and the pairing of an unpowered null with an unquantified positive in the same sentence is not interpretable either way.
claims.model: Shank3-transgenic knockout; targeted exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: spatial learning and memory, and cognitive flexibility; paradigms not named in the abstract

claims.text: Female animals had abnormalities similar to males in avoidance, anxiety and cognition but were less pathological in motor function and repetitive behavior, and heterozygous Shank3 knockout animals had either no abnormal or a milder phenotype in all test paradigms.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: Sex and genotype are treated as separate stratifications of an unstated total sample, so each cell is smaller still and no interaction test is reported. The heterozygous result matters most for translation - almost all people with PMS are haploinsufficient, not homozygous null - and it is precisely the condition in which this model shows little or nothing, with no power analysis to say whether 'no abnormal phenotype' means absent or undetected.
claims.model: Shank3-transgenic, heterozygous versus homozygous knockout
claims.measure: battery of motor, social, repetitive, anxiety and cognitive paradigms, compared by sex and by genotype

claims.text: Shank3-deficient adult male rats showed a reduction in overall brain size and in the absolute volume of the neocortex, piriform cortex, thalamus, forebrain, inferior and superior colliculi, internal capsule and anterior commissure, with the superior colliculus also decreased in relative volume.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: Male animals only, so nothing can be said about females in a syndrome that affects both sexes. No sample size, no effect size and no p values in the abstract for a long list of regions, with no stated correction for testing many regions at once; only one region (superior colliculus) survives as a relative-volume difference, which raises the possibility that most of the list reflects a global reduction in brain size rather than regional specificity. Heterozygous and homozygous results are not separated in the abstract, although heterozygosity is the state relevant to PMS.
claims.model: heterozygous and homozygous Shank3-deficient rats versus wild-type littermates; targeted exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: regional and whole-brain volume, in vivo structural MRI

claims.text: Diffusion tensor imaging in Shank3-deficient rats showed reduced axial diffusion and fractional anisotropy in the external capsule and increased mean diffusion in the fornix.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: No sample size, effect size or p value in the abstract. The affected tracts in the rat (external capsule, fornix) are not the tracts reported as affected in children with PMS (uncinate fasciculus, R-0108), so the cross-species correspondence claimed by the authors holds at the level of 'white matter is abnormal' rather than at the level of a specific tract that could serve as a translatable endpoint. Males only.
claims.model: heterozygous and homozygous Shank3-deficient rats versus wild-type littermates
claims.measure: axial diffusion, fractional anisotropy and mean diffusion, diffusion tensor imaging

claims.text: Shank3-deficient rats replicate the reduced brain volume and altered white matter phenotypes present in PMS, and the altered brain regions represent potential cross-species structural biomarkers.
claims.limA: The authors note that brain structure had previously been assessed ex vivo in pups of this rat model but not in vivo or in adults.
claims.limO: The word 'replicate' is doing heavy work: the human comparator is described in the abstract as 'limited brain imaging studies', the specific regions do not match tract for tract, and no quantitative cross-species comparison is performed. Adult male rats are compared against a paediatric, mixed-sex human literature. A region reported as abnormal in both species is a hypothesis for a cross-species endpoint, not a validated one, and the authors say so.
claims.model: heterozygous and homozygous Shank3-deficient rats versus wild-type littermates
claims.measure: correspondence between rat structural MRI/DTI findings and reported human PMS neuroimaging phenotypes

claims.text: Both gray and white matter structures were smaller in Shank3-deficient rats, leading to an overall reduction in brain size compared with wild-type littermates, the largest affected region being the neocortex.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or p values. Unlike the peer-reviewed version, the preprint abstract does not state that only male animals were studied and does not state that the animals were adults, so a reader of the preprint alone would overestimate the generality of the finding. Not peer reviewed.
claims.model: haploinsufficient and homozygous Shank3-deficient rats versus wild-type littermates
claims.measure: regional and whole-brain volume, magnetic resonance imaging

claims.text: The microstructure of two white matter tracts, the external capsule and the fornix, was abnormal in Shank3-deficient rats.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: 'Abnormal' is stated without naming which diffusion metrics moved or in which direction, information the peer-reviewed version supplies; on its own the preprint claim is not specific enough to be compared against any human finding. No n, no statistics. Not peer reviewed.
claims.model: haploinsufficient and homozygous Shank3-deficient rats versus wild-type littermates
claims.measure: white matter microstructure, diffusion tensor imaging

claims.text: LASSO regression on coronary artery calcification transcriptomes identified five biomarker candidates - NRG1, PXDN, ACTL7A, ACSS3 and SHANK3 - of which PXDN, not SHANK3, showed the strongest diagnostic performance.
claims.n: discovery cohort 8 CAC and 8 controls; validation cohort 6 CAC and 6 controls
claims.eff: AUC reported for PXDN only (0.95 discovery, 0.83 validation); no direction, effect size or AUC reported for SHANK3
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: A whole-transcriptome LASSO screen run on 8 vs 8 and 6 vs 6 samples is a selection procedure that overfits at this sample size; the 'validation' cohort is a second small public dataset, not an independent prospective sample. SHANK3 is listed as an unranked candidate with no direction, no AUC and no in vivo confirmation (only PXDN was taken forward to the mouse model). The record is retained for this project solely because it shows SHANK3 transcript abundance varying in a non-neural human disease: any blood-based SHANK3 transcript marker proposed for PMS will have to demonstrate specificity against vascular and metabolic disease.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: transcript-level differential expression and LASSO-based biomarker screening in two public transcriptomic datasets

ref.venue: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

claims.text: In children with syndromic autism spectrum disorders, including Phelan-McDermid syndrome, the most severely impacted PedsQL dimension was physical functioning.
claims.n: 213 children with Phelan-McDermid syndrome, 148 with Rett syndrome, 30 with SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability (caregiver respondents)
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: Caregiver proxy report collected through an online survey, with no direct assessment of the child and no verification of the genetic diagnosis described in the abstract. No effect sizes, confidence intervals or p values are given for the dimension ranking. Recruitment through family associations is self-selecting. No deletion size or variant information, so nothing in the record can be related to SHANK3 dosage.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL 4.0), caregiver report, four dimensions

claims.text: Individuals with Rett syndrome had significantly worse physical functioning, emotional and school scores than individuals with Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
claims.n: 213 children with Phelan-McDermid syndrome, 148 with Rett syndrome
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: Between-syndrome comparison of caregiver-reported scores with no adjustment for age, sex or severity described in the abstract, and no effect size or p value quoted. The groups were recruited through different syndrome communities, so a reporting-threshold difference between caregiver populations cannot be separated from a true phenotype difference.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: PedsQL 4.0 dimension scores, Rett syndrome compared with Phelan-McDermid syndrome

claims.text: Syndromic autism, including Phelan-McDermid syndrome, results in worse quality of life than other chronic disorders, including idiopathic autism.
claims.n: 391 children in total (213 PMD, 148 RTT, 30 SYNGAP1-ID)
claims.limA: The authors attribute the reduced quality of life to the lack of targeted therapies, which the design cannot test.
claims.limO: No concurrently recruited comparison group: the contrast with 'other chronic disorders' and with idiopathic autism rests on published reference values for the instrument, measured in other samples, at other times, by other teams. The causal attribution in the conclusion is not supported by a cross-sectional survey.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: PedsQL 4.0 and Beach Center Family Quality of Life Scale, caregiver report

claims.text: Beagle dogs carrying mutations in Shank3 avoided human affective touch in a heterospecific affective touch paradigm.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: Preprint, not peer reviewed. No number of animals, no effect size, no p value and no sex distribution anywhere in the abstract, so the result cannot be weighed at all. The behavioural paradigm is newly designed and therefore unvalidated and without comparison data from another laboratory. Non-standard species for this literature: no independent Shank3 dog colony exists against which to replicate.
claims.model: Beagle dog carrying Shank3 mutations; allele, exons and zygosity not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: avoidance of human affective touch in a newly designed heterospecific affective touch paradigm

claims.text: Affective-touch-evoked oscillations in the dorsal medial prefrontal cortex were significantly altered and the number of neurons encoding affective touch was reduced in Shank3 mutant dogs.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: The direction of the oscillatory change is not stated ('significantly altered'), nor the frequency band, so the finding cannot be compared with the human EEG literature on PMS - which is the only reason a circuit marker would interest this project. No number of animals or units, no effect size, no statistics reported. Preprint.
claims.model: Beagle dog carrying Shank3 mutations; allele, exons and zygosity not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: in vivo single-unit recording: affective-touch-evoked oscillations and count of affective-touch-encoding neurons

claims.text: The aversion to affective touch and the altered neural processing in Shank3 mutant dogs were largely rescued by the GABA-A receptor antagonist pentylenetetrazole.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: 'Largely rescued' is unquantified, with no dose, route, timing, number of animals or statistics. Pentylenetetrazole is a convulsant; the seizure burden of PMS makes a GABA-A antagonist an implausible clinical candidate, so the result is a mechanistic probe and should not be carried forward as a therapeutic lead. No vehicle-control or wild-type-plus-drug arm is described in the abstract, so a non-specific arousal effect cannot be excluded. Preprint.
claims.model: Beagle dog carrying Shank3 mutations; allele, exons and zygosity not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: affective touch avoidance and dmPFC affective-touch-evoked neural responses after pentylenetetrazole

claims.text: A SHANK3 methylation marker (SHANK3-16286-1-5) measured in cervical scrapings discriminated endometrial cancer from benign endometrial thickening with a single-gene area under the curve of 0.782.
claims.n: 20 endometrial cancer patients and 20 benign endometrial thickening controls, split 6:4 into training and validation sets
claims.eff: single-gene AUC 0.782 for the SHANK3 marker; three-marker panel AUC 0.922 (sensitivity 85.0%, specificity 90.0%)
claims.limA: The authors state this is a single-centre exploratory study with a small sample size, requiring validation in large-scale, multi-centre independent cohorts.
claims.limO: The three markers were screened and the ROC curves computed inside the same set of 40 samples, with the 'validation' set a 40% split of that set rather than an independent cohort - the AUCs are therefore optimistic by construction. The direction of methylation at the SHANK3 CpG is not stated. Nothing links methylation of this CpG in cervical epithelium to neuronal SHANK3 expression or to PMS.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: methylated CpG tandem amplification and sequencing of cervical scrapings; single-gene ROC analysis

claims.text: Shank3 was among ten significantly up- or down-regulated genes identified by RNA sequencing in bone marrow cells of benzene-exposed CD1 mice and associated with the MAPK oxidative stress pathway.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: The abstract does not state whether Shank3 was up- or down-regulated, nor by how much, nor the number of animals. Shank3 is one of ten genes from an unreplicated discovery screen and is conspicuously absent from the eight genes the authors then confirmed by qRT-PCR and carried into human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, so the qRT-PCR stage appears not to have confirmed it; the abstract never says so explicitly. The authors' own conclusion names only Mapk11 and Fgf3 as candidate biomarkers.
claims.model: CD1 mice, benzene-induced bone marrow failure model; Shank3 measured as an outcome, not manipulated
claims.measure: differential gene expression in bone marrow cells, RNA-seq with KEGG pathway analysis

claims.text: Early-life oral exposure to polypropylene microplastics and/or DEHP downregulated expression of the ASD-risk genes Shank3 and Nlgn1 in immature mice, alongside social interaction deficits and synaptic damage in the prefrontal cortex.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: Male mice only, group sizes not reported, no doses given, and no effect size or p value for the Shank3 change. Exposure doses in microplastic studies are frequently far above realistic human intake, and the abstract gives no basis to judge. The design cannot establish that reduced Shank3 expression mediates the behavioural phenotype rather than accompanying it.
claims.model: wild-type ICR mice; Shank3 measured as an outcome, not manipulated
claims.measure: Shank3 and Nlgn1 expression, neurobehaviour, histopathology and brain proteomics

claims.text: Inhibiting the mTOR signalling pathway with rapamycin restored autophagic activity and ameliorated the ASD-relevant neurodevelopmental alterations induced by polypropylene microplastic and DEHP exposure.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: No dose, schedule, group size or statistics for the rescue arm, and no report of whether rapamycin was given to unexposed controls, so a non-specific behavioural effect cannot be excluded. Whether Shank3 expression itself was restored is not stated - which is precisely the link this project would need. The model is a toxicant exposure, not SHANK3 haploinsufficiency, so the rescue says nothing about PMS.
claims.model: wild-type ICR mice exposed to PP-MPs and/or DEHP
claims.measure: autophagic activity and ASD-relevant behavioural outcomes after rapamycin

claims.text: Streptococcus mutans translocated to the gut in both gavaged groups but did not achieve enhanced colonization in SHANK3 knockout mice compared with wild-type mice.
claims.n: 6 mice per group, four groups (WT control, WT gavaged, SHANK3-/- control, SHANK3-/- gavaged)
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: A null result reported without any power consideration: with 6 animals per group, an absent genotype effect on colonization is weak evidence of no effect. No quantitative abundance values, confidence intervals or equivalence testing are given, and 'did not achieve enhanced colonization' is not distinguished from 'was not significantly different'.
claims.model: SHANK3 knockout (SHANK3-/-) and wild-type mice; allele and targeted exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: faecal metagenomic sequencing; S. mutans relative abundance in the gut

claims.text: LEfSe analysis identified Parascardovia denticolens and Bacteroides heparinolyticus as specific biomarkers for the S. mutans-gavaged SHANK3 knockout group, whose microbial networks showed reduced stability.
claims.limA: not_reported
claims.limO: 'Biomarker' here means a taxon discriminating two mouse groups of six animals in a LEfSe run over hundreds of taxa, with no stated multiple-comparison control, no held-out set and no LDA scores quoted; this is hypothesis generation, not a marker. No behavioural, neural or inflammatory outcome was measured, so the oral-gut-brain conclusion rests entirely on predicted metagenomic function (butanoate metabolism, neuroinflammation pathways) rather than on any measured phenotype.
claims.model: SHANK3 knockout (SHANK3-/-) and wild-type mice; allele and targeted exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: faecal metagenomic sequencing with LEfSe discriminant analysis and microbial co-occurrence network stability

claims.text: Astaxanthin treatment significantly improved core ASD-like behaviours in Shank3b knockout mice, including social interaction deficits, motor incoordination and repetitive grooming.
claims.limA: The authors note that oxidative stress assays were not performed.
claims.limO: No group sizes, doses, route, treatment duration, effect sizes or p values in the abstract. Sex is not reported, which matters in Shank3b mice where phenotype severity differs between sexes. Direction is recorded as mixed because improvement means an increase in social interaction and a decrease in grooming. No independent replication; the same group previously reported a comparable result with N-acetylcysteine, so the two findings are not independent evidence.
claims.model: Shank3b-/- mice; exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: social interaction, motor coordination and repetitive grooming

claims.text: In the cerebellum of Shank3b knockout mice, astaxanthin reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines and counteracted microglial hyperactivation.
claims.limA: Oxidative stress assays were not performed, which the authors state as a limitation of a study about a redox-active compound.
claims.limO: Which cytokines, by what method and by how much are all absent from the abstract. Only the cerebellum is reported, with no other region as a comparator, so regional specificity cannot be judged. No group sizes or statistics.
claims.model: Shank3b-/- mice; exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: pro-inflammatory cytokine levels and microglial activation in the cerebellum

claims.text: Receiver operating characteristic analysis suggests that TNF and IFN-gamma expression in peripheral immune cells may be promising biomarkers of treatment response to astaxanthin in Shank3b knockout mice.
claims.limA: Oxidative stress assays were not performed.
claims.limO: No AUC, confidence interval or p value is reported for either marker, and the ROC analysis is performed in the same animals that generated the hypothesis, with no independent test set - the discrimination is optimistic by construction. TNF and IFN-gamma are generic inflammatory markers with no specificity to SHANK3 biology; peripheral cytokine levels in children are confounded by intercurrent infection, which is common in PMS. The direction of change in peripheral compartments is reported as opposite to that in the cerebellum, which the abstract calls 'immune rebalancing' but does not demonstrate.
claims.model: Shank3b-/- mice; exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: TNF and IFN-gamma expression in peripheral immune cells, ROC analysis against treatment response

claims.text: Knock-in mice carrying the ASD-associated Shank1 R882H missense mutation displayed social disability and repetitive behaviours without abnormal motor function or heightened anxiety.
claims.limO: Sample sizes, sex, background strain and effect sizes are all absent from the abstract. The gene is SHANK1, not SHANK3: the relevance to PMS rests on paralogy within the Shank family, and nothing in the abstract shows the two genes converge on the same measurable readouts in humans.
claims.model: Shank1 R882H knock-in, corresponding to the human SHANK1 c.2621G>A (p.R874H) missense variant; SHANK3 not manipulated
claims.measure: social behaviour and repetitive behaviour test batteries, plus motor and anxiety assays; specific tests not named in the abstract

claims.text: Shank1 R882H knock-in mice showed decreased spine size, reduced spine density, abnormal postsynaptic density morphology and impaired hippocampal long-term potentiation and basal excitatory transmission, together with downregulated mGluR1-IP3R1-calcium signalling in frontal cortex, hippocampus and cerebellar cortex.
claims.limO: Several heterogeneous readouts are compressed into one summary sentence with no quantities, no n and no statistics; none can be weighted individually from the abstract. The signalling axis reported here is mGluR1-IP3R1, not the SHANK3-Homer-mGluR5 axis usually invoked in PMS, so it cannot be read as support for mGluR5-based markers.
claims.model: Shank1 R882H knock-in
claims.measure: spine size and density, postsynaptic density morphology, hippocampal LTP and basal excitatory transmission, mGluR1-IP3R1 signalling and intracellular calcium release; structural MRI for brain structure

claims.text: In an exploratory analysis of DNA methylation before and after haemodialysis, SHANK3 was identified by protein-protein interaction network analysis as one of several critical hub genes among differentially methylated region-associated genes.
claims.eff: 93 genes with significant methylation alterations, 41 with changes exceeding 100%; no value given specifically for SHANK3
claims.limA: The authors state that sample size is an important limiting factor influencing the reliability of findings across molecular and clinical levels and that further investigation is needed.
claims.limO: The number of patients is never stated in the abstract. SHANK3 appears only as a node in a bioinformatic hub list with no gene-specific statistic, no validation and no replication, and the cohort has no relation to PMS or to neurodevelopment. This is a search false positive with no biomarker value for PMS; it is recorded so that the hit is traceable rather than silently dropped.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: genome-wide DNA methylation (bisulfite conversion, GenomeStudio), differentially methylated regions, STRING/Cytoscape hub-gene identification

claims.text: In children with ASD, fMRI analyses revealed a significant decrease in functional connectivity between the superior colliculus and the ventral tegmental area.
claims.limO: Cohort size, age range, sex distribution and the composition of the comparison group are absent from the abstract, as is any effect size. The clinical cohort is idiopathic ASD, not genetically defined PMS, so the human half of this translational pairing carries no SHANK3 genotype at all.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: SC-VTA functional connectivity, fMRI

claims.text: In Shank3 knockout mice, miniscope recordings identified a reduction in the frequency of calcium transients in superior colliculus neurons projecting to the ventral tegmental area, accompanied by changes in neuronal correlation and intrinsic cellular properties.
claims.limO: Which Shank3 allele was used is not stated, which matters because isoform-specific alleles give different phenotypes. Homozygous knockout does not model the heterozygous dosage of PMS. No n, no sex and no effect size are reported.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout (Shank3-/-); targeted exons and isoforms not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: frequency of calcium transients by miniscope imaging; neuronal correlation; intrinsic cellular properties

claims.text: Interneuronal correlation in Shank3 knockout mice and SC-to-VTA functional connectivity in children with ASD each correlated with the severity of social deficits, which the authors propose as supporting the SC-VTA pathway as a biomarker for ASD.
claims.limO: A brain-behaviour correlation reported without a coefficient, a confidence interval, a p value or a sample size, and with no statement of whether it survives correction for multiple comparisons. A cross-species parallel is asserted rather than tested in a common statistical frame. fMRI in young children with ASD requires sedation or extensive habituation, which the abstract does not address and which conditions whether this could ever be a repeatable trial endpoint.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: SC-VTA functional connectivity (fMRI) against severity of social deficits; in mice, interneuronal correlation against social orienting

claims.text: Random forest analysis of blood transcriptomic data selected SHANK3 among the ten key feature genes with the highest importance scores for autism prediction.
claims.n: not_reported; secondary analysis of the public dataset GSE18123
claims.eff: not_reported for SHANK3; the only AUC given is MGAT4C (AUC = 0.730)
claims.limO: Neither sample size nor the direction of SHANK3 expression change is stated. Feature selection and ROC evaluation appear to be performed on the same single public dataset with no external validation cohort, which inflates apparent discriminative performance. The cohort is idiopathic ASD, not PMS, so a SHANK3 signal here says nothing about SHANK3 dosage in PMS.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: differentially expressed genes from GSE18123, protein-protein interaction network, random forest feature importance

claims.text: ROC curve analysis indicated that most of the top selected genes had strong discriminatory power in differentiating ASD from controls, with MGAT4C reaching an AUC of 0.730.
claims.eff: AUC = 0.730 for MGAT4C; no confidence interval, and no AUC reported for SHANK3
claims.limO: An AUC of 0.730 is described as strong discriminatory power, which overstates it: that is modest classification performance, reported without a confidence interval and apparently without an independent test set. No AUC is given for SHANK3 itself, so this record does not establish SHANK3 as a classifier at all.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: receiver operating characteristic analysis of blood gene expression for ASD versus control classification

claims.text: In gene expression profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from hospitalised women, SHANK3 was identified as a differentially expressed gene unique to unipolar depression following pharmacological treatment.
claims.n: 24 women with unipolar depression and 32 women with bipolar depression
claims.eff: p = 0.001 for SHANK3; direction and fold change not stated in the abstract
claims.limO: No healthy control group is described; the comparison is unipolar versus bipolar depression before and after treatment. Treatment was uncontrolled and heterogeneous, so any expression change may reflect the drug rather than the disorder. The direction of the SHANK3 change is not given, and a microarray-wide p of 0.001 is reported with no indication of correction for multiple testing. Female-only sample; no relation to PMS.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: PBMC gene expression, SurePrint G3 microarray analysed with GeneSpring

claims.text: Two up-regulated genes, OPRM1 and CELF4, were significantly associated with treatment response in both unipolar and bipolar depression, while RASGRF1 was identified as a potential bipolar-specific marker.
claims.n: 24 women with unipolar depression and 32 women with bipolar depression
claims.eff: p = 0.013 for OPRM1 and CELF4; p = 0.010 for RASGRF1; fold change threshold applied was greater than 2
claims.limA: The authors describe the markers as potential and call for further studies.
claims.limO: Only treatment responders were profiled, so there is no non-responder comparison from which a predictive marker could be derived; the design supports association with improvement, not prediction of it. 56 participants across two diagnoses is small for transcriptome-wide discovery, and no replication cohort is described.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: PBMC gene expression against treatment response defined as a 50% reduction on the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale

claims.text: High levels of nitrosative stress biomarkers were found in both the Shank3 and the Cntnap2 ASD mouse models.
claims.limO: Neither the Shank3 allele nor the specific analytes are named, and no quantities, n or statistics are given. That the same elevation is seen in the Cntnap2 model is explicitly a demonstration that the marker is not specific to SHANK3 loss, which limits its use for target engagement in PMS even though it strengthens the convergence argument.
claims.model: Shank3 mouse model and Cntnap2 mouse model; alleles and targeted exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: nitrosative stress biomarkers and nitric oxide levels; specific analytes and assays not named in the abstract

claims.text: Pharmacological intervention with a neuronal nitric oxide synthase inhibitor reversed molecular, synaptic and behavioural ASD-associated phenotypes in both the Shank3 and the Cntnap2 mouse models.
claims.limO: A claim of reversal across three levels of phenotype with no compound named, no dose, no duration, no sample size and no statistics. Reversal of a battery of endpoints reported as a single result cannot be weighed endpoint by endpoint from the abstract, and no blinding or randomisation is described. Full-text retrieval is required before this is usable.
claims.model: Shank3 and Cntnap2 mouse models; alleles not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: molecular, synaptic and behavioural ASD-associated phenotypes; individual endpoints not specified in the abstract

claims.text: Treating iPSC-derived cortical neurons from patients with a SHANK3 mutation with the nNOS inhibitor showed therapeutic effects similar to those seen in the mouse models.
claims.limO: Number of patient lines, number of control lines and whether isogenic controls were used are all unstated, and iPSC work with one or two lines is routinely confounded by line-to-line variability. The outcome measured is not named. Similar therapeutic effects is a qualitative assertion with no quantity attached.
claims.model: iPSC-derived cortical neurons from patients carrying a SHANK3 mutation; variant not specified
claims.measure: not specified in the abstract beyond therapeutic effects similar to those in the mouse models

claims.text: A significant increase in nitrosative stress biomarkers was found in the plasma of low-functioning ASD patients.
claims.limO: No sample size, no control group description, no analyte named and no effect size. The patients are described only as low-functioning ASD, with no genotype, so it is not known whether any carried a SHANK3 variant. Nitrosative stress is a general cellular stress readout and is elevated in many conditions, so specificity for PMS is unaddressed.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: plasma nitrosative stress biomarkers; analytes and assay not named in the abstract

claims.text: In a randomised clinical trial, the incidence of perioperative neurocognitive disorder in the remote ischemic preconditioning group (44%) was comparable to that in the control group (44%).
claims.eff: 44% versus 44%, P = 0.982; no confidence interval reported
claims.limO: A null result with no power calculation reported in the abstract, so it is not possible to say whether 120 patients could have detected a clinically meaningful difference. No relation to PMS or SHANK3 beyond the exploratory variant analysis; recorded as a registered trial with a clearly reported null.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: incidence of perioperative neurocognitive disorder across six neurological tests before and after surgery

claims.text: Serum myeloid differentiation factor 2 and cystatin C did not differ significantly between patients with and without perioperative neurocognitive disorder and were unable to predict its occurrence.
claims.eff: not_reported; no p value, confidence interval or discrimination statistic given for either marker
claims.limO: A negative biomarker result presented with no statistics at all and no power analysis, which is exactly the pattern that makes null findings uninterpretable. Neither marker has a stated prior effect size that the study was designed to exclude.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: serum MD2 and cystatin C by ELISA against PND status

claims.text: Whole genome sequencing identified 3877 mutated genes exclusively in patients with perioperative neurocognitive disorder, enriched in synapse function and including a Shank3 variant (rs4824145), which the authors suggest may confer susceptibility.
claims.n: not_reported for the sequenced subset; 120 patients randomised in total
claims.eff: not_reported; no association statistic, odds ratio or p value given for rs4824145
claims.limO: Exclusively identified in PND patients is a presence-absence comparison in a very small sample, not an association test; with 3877 genes so classified, chance alone would produce many such exclusive variants. No allele frequency, no statistic and no correction for multiple testing are reported, and no replication cohort exists. The conclusion that carriers may be more susceptible is not supported by anything quantified in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: whole genome sequencing, variants exclusive to PND patients, KEGG pathway enrichment

claims.text: SHANK3 was among the top differentially methylated probes in cortex surrounding the epileptogenic zone in drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy, and its methylation status was verified by methylation-specific qPCR.
claims.n: 19 patients with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy and 10 postmortem non-epileptic controls
claims.eff: 3210 differentially methylated probes in SCEZ; no probe-level statistic reported for SHANK3
claims.limO: 19 cases against 10 postmortem controls, with surgical tissue compared against postmortem tissue, which differ in postmortem interval, agonal state and cell composition. The qPCR step verifies the array measurement, not the biological association, and is not an independent replication. Direction of SHANK3 methylation change is not stated, and no PMS or SHANK3-variant patients are involved.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: DNA methylation, Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChip, with technical verification by methylation-specific qPCR

claims.text: One hippocampal differentially methylated probe, cg26834418 in CHORDC1, showed a strong blood-brain correlation with BECon and IMAGE-CpG and is proposed as a potential surrogate peripheral biomarker of drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy.
claims.limO: Blood-brain concordance is taken from external reference databases rather than measured in these patients' own paired blood and brain samples, so the surrogacy is predicted, not demonstrated. Only 32 differentially methylated probes were found in the hippocampus, and selecting one of them as a candidate marker without replication is a single-cohort finding. The gene is CHORDC1, not SHANK3.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: methylation at cg26834418, with blood-brain concordance estimated from the BECon and IMAGE-CpG reference tools

claims.text: The SHANK3 promoter is hypermethylated in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of patients with first-episode schizophrenia.
claims.limO: The abstract reports no sample size for either patients or controls, no effect size and no p value for the hypermethylation itself. The population is first-episode schizophrenia, not PMS; nothing establishes that the same PBMC signal behaves this way in SHANK3 haploinsufficiency, where the expected direction of promoter methylation change is not predicted by the study. MeDIP-chip was genome-wide, so SHANK3 is one of an unstated number of tested loci and no multiple-testing correction is described in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: SHANK3 promoter DNA methylation in PBMCs, methylated DNA immunoprecipitation-chip (MeDIP-chip)

claims.text: SHANK3 promoter hypermethylation in PBMCs is negatively correlated with cortical surface area in the left inferior temporal cortex and positively correlated with negative symptom subscores in first-episode schizophrenia.
claims.limO: No correlation coefficients, confidence intervals, p values or sample sizes are given in the abstract, so the strength of the blood-to-brain link cannot be judged at all. A single cortical region is named without any statement of how many regions were tested. The design is cross-sectional and correlational; direction of causation is not addressed.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: PBMC SHANK3 promoter methylation against MRI cortical surface area and negative symptom subscores

claims.text: The transcription factor YBX1 binds the hypermethylated region of the SHANK3 promoter in iPSC-derived cortical interneurons but not in glutamatergic neurons, and shRNA knockdown confirms a direct positive regulatory effect of YBX1 on SHANK3 expression in cortical interneurons.
claims.limO: Whether the iPSC lines carry any SHANK3 variant, or come from patients at all, is not stated; without that the cell-type specificity cannot be anchored to any genotype. Number of lines, clones and differentiations is absent, so the result could rest on a single line. The cell-type contrast (interneurons yes, glutamatergic neurons no) is reported as a dichotomy with no quantification, which is the classic shape of an underpowered negative in the comparison arm.
claims.model: iPSC-derived cortical interneurons and glutamatergic neurons; donor genotype not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: YBX1 binding at the SHANK3 promoter and SHANK3 expression after YBX1 knockdown

claims.text: The 40-Hz auditory steady-state response was totally absent in a 15-year-old girl with a duplication of the first seven exons of SHANK3, significantly deviating from the response of typically developing children.
claims.n: 1 individual (SH01) compared with 32 typically developing children
claims.limA: Presented by the authors as a case report; they state that 40-Hz ASSR had not previously been studied in relation to SHANK3 functioning.
claims.limO: A single case against a comparison group, so no estimate of within-genotype variability exists and the statistical test is a single-subject deviation score with no effect size or p value reported in the abstract. The case is a duplication, not a deletion: the finding cannot be assumed to transfer to PMS, where SHANK3 dosage is reduced rather than increased. The comparison group is typically developing rather than intellectual-disability-matched, so absent ASSR could reflect intellectual disability or attention rather than SHANK3 dosage. ASSR abnormalities are reported in schizophrenia and other conditions and are not specific to SHANK3.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: 40-Hz auditory steady-state response, EEG during binaural 40-Hz click trains of 500 ms with 500-800 ms inter-trial intervals

claims.text: The same individual had a relatively preserved auditory event-related potential with only a slightly attenuated P1, despite the complete absence of the 40-Hz ASSR.
claims.n: 1 individual (SH01) compared with 32 typically developing children
claims.limO: A largely null result in a single case, reported without any power consideration: 'relatively preserved' and 'slightly attenuated' are not quantified, and no statistical test is cited for the ERP in the abstract. It is recorded because the dissociation it describes, intact transient ERP alongside absent steady-state response, is what would make ASSR informative rather than a generic sign of hearing or attention problems, and that dissociation rests here on one person.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: auditory event-related potential, including P1 amplitude

claims.text: The individual with the partial SHANK3 duplication was diagnosed with mild mental retardation and learning disabilities, dysgraphia, dyslexia, a smaller vocabulary than typically developing peers and microcephaly, with mild autistic symptoms below the threshold for an ASD diagnosis and no seizures or MRI abnormalities reported.
claims.limO: Single case; the authors state the phenotype resembles that of approximately 30 previously reported 22q13.33 microduplication patients, but no systematic comparison is given. Absence of seizures and of MRI abnormalities is reported, not tested, and the duration of EEG monitoring is not stated, so 'no seizures' is a clinical history rather than a negative investigation.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: clinical phenotyping, ICD coding (F70.88), MRI, seizure history

claims.text: Embryonic exposure of zebrafish to 100 nM mercury chloride suppressed shank3a gene expression, together with adsl, tsc1b and nrxn1a, alongside altered metabolites and impaired visual and social behaviour.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, fold changes or p values for any gene are given in the abstract, and the method used for expression measurement is not named. A single concentration was tested, so no dose-response exists. This is a toxicological study with no SHANK3 genetic manipulation and no PMS relevance beyond the fact that shank3a appears in the gene panel; the authors themselves single out tsc1b, not shank3a, as the gene best correlated with ASD. The metabolites proposed as biomarkers are markers of retinal impairment in fish, not of SHANK3 biology.
claims.model: wild-type zebrafish larvae; no SHANK3 genetic model
claims.measure: shank3a, adsl, tsc1b and nrxn1a gene expression; LC-MS metabolites; light-dark, social and colour-preference assays

claims.text: High levels of nitrosative stress biomarkers were measured in both the Shank3 and the Cntnap2 ASD mouse models.
claims.limO: Preprint, not peer reviewed. The Shank3 allele is not identified, which for this corpus is disqualifying detail rather than a minor omission, since Shank3 lines differ in isoform loss. Which analytes constitute the 'nitrosative stress biomarkers' is not stated, nor the tissue, nor n, nor any statistic. The marker is shared with Cntnap2 mice in the same study, so by the authors' own design it is not specific to SHANK3.
claims.model: Shank3 mouse model; allele, exons targeted and background not stated in the abstract. Cntnap2 mouse model used in parallel
claims.measure: nitrosative stress biomarkers; specific analytes not named in the abstract

claims.text: Treating the Shank3 and Cntnap2 mouse models with a selective neuronal nitric oxide synthase inhibitor led to a reversal of the molecular, synaptic and behavioural ASD phenotypes.
claims.limO: Preprint, not peer reviewed. 'Reversal of the molecular, synaptic and behavioral ASD phenotypes' is a global summary claim with no single named endpoint, no compound, no dose, no route, no duration, no n and no statistics; nothing in it is checkable from the abstract. Reversal in two unrelated genetic models by the same agent is as consistent with a non-specific effect on activity or arousal as with a shared pathway, and the abstract reports no wild-type treated control for the behavioural measures.
claims.model: Shank3 mouse model; allele not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: unspecified molecular, synaptic and behavioural ASD-relevant readouts

claims.text: Nitric oxide levels were significantly elevated in plasma from 19 low-functioning ASD patients compared with 20 typically developed volunteers.
claims.n: 19 low-functioning ASD patients and 20 typically developed volunteers
claims.limO: Preprint, not peer reviewed. Nineteen against twenty, with no effect size, no confidence interval and no p value in the abstract. The ASD cohort is not genotyped: no participant is stated to carry a SHANK3 variant, so this is not PMS evidence. Plasma NO is a highly non-specific analyte affected by diet, nitrate intake, inflammation, exercise and medication, none of which is said to have been controlled. The SNO-proteome enrichment analysis is exploratory and reported without correction.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: plasma nitric oxide levels; SNOTRAP mass spectrometry for the SNO-proteome

claims.text: Higher baseline plasma Shank3 levels predicted antidepressant response to a single subanesthetic ketamine infusion at days 1, 2 and 3 in subjects with bipolar depression.
claims.n: 29 subjects with bipolar depression received the infusion; the number for whom Shank3 levels were collected is not stated
claims.limA: The authors list the small sample size, the inability to assess the source of peripheral Shank3, and the lack of a placebo group for baseline Shank3 levels and for the comparative structural and functional neuroimaging.
claims.limO: All three p values sit between 0.02 and 0.05 with correlations around 0.4 in a sample of at most 29, and three time points are reported without correction for multiple comparisons; this is the profile of a result that is unlikely to survive replication. The number of subjects actually contributing Shank3 levels is never stated, so the denominator of these correlations is unknown. The population is bipolar depression, not PMS, and no participant is reported to carry a SHANK3 variant. The assay used to measure plasma Shank3 is not named in the abstract and the biological source of circulating Shank3 is unknown by the authors' own admission.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: baseline plasma Shank3 level against antidepressant response

claims.text: Higher baseline plasma Shank3 levels were associated with larger average amygdala volume and larger right amygdala volume in bipolar depression.
claims.eff: r=0.58, p=0.02 for average amygdala volume; r=0.65, p=0.009 for right amygdala volume
claims.limA: Small sample size and lack of a placebo comparison group for the neuroimaging, as stated by the authors.
claims.limO: Fifteen subjects. Correlations of 0.58 and 0.65 in n=15 have very wide confidence intervals, none of which is reported, and are highly sensitive to single data points. Laterality (right but not left stated) in a sample this size should be read as noise until replicated. No correction for the number of regions or the number of correlations tested across this paper is described.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: baseline plasma Shank3 level against amygdala volume on 3-Tesla MRI

claims.text: Greater baseline plasma Shank3 predicted increased glucose metabolism in the hippocampus and amygdala after ketamine in bipolar depression.
claims.eff: r=0.51, p=0.04 for hippocampus; r=0.58, p=0.02 for amygdala
claims.limA: Small sample size and no placebo group for comparative functional neuroimaging, as stated by the authors.
claims.limO: Seventeen subjects, two regions, p values of 0.04 and 0.02 uncorrected. There is no pre-ketamine PET comparison described, so 'increased' refers to a correlation with post-infusion metabolism rather than to a measured change. Overlapping subsets of the same 29 subjects contribute to the clinical, MRI and PET correlations, which compounds the multiplicity problem across the three records extracted from this paper.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: baseline plasma Shank3 level against post-ketamine [18F]-FDG PET glucose metabolism

claims.text: Shank3 was among 14 genes involved in neurite growth, neural development and synaptic plasticity identified as direct targets of differentially expressed long noncoding RNAs in the prefrontal cortex of mice after repeated social defeat stress.
claims.limO: The direction and magnitude of any Shank3 change are not stated in the abstract, so this record carries no quantitative information about Shank3 at all. Shank3 appears inside a list of 14 genes drawn from 1796 differentially expressed mRNAs and a predicted lncRNA-mRNA network, and the abstract says qRT-PCR confirmed only four of the differentially expressed transcripts without stating whether Shank3 was among them. The lncRNA-target relationships are bioinformatic predictions, not demonstrated regulation. No PMS or SHANK3 variant is involved.
claims.model: wild-type mice subjected to repeated social defeat stress; no SHANK3 genetic model
claims.measure: RNA-sequencing of lncRNAs and mRNAs with qRT-PCR confirmation and bioinformatic target prediction

claims.text: The reduction of parvalbumin-immunoreactive neurons observed in Shank3B-/- mice is due to a reduction in Pvalb mRNA and parvalbumin protein rather than to a loss of parvalbumin-expressing neurons.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, no fold changes, no p values and no age are given in the abstract, which matters here because parvalbumin expression is strongly developmentally and activity regulated. Three brain regions and four genotypes are summarised in a single sentence ('in all cases'), hiding any region- or genotype-specific variation. Genetic background is not stated, and SHANK3 phenotypes are known to be background-sensitive.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mice, studied alongside Shank1-/-, PV-/- and PV+/- mice
claims.measure: Pvalb mRNA by qRT-PCR and parvalbumin protein by Western blot, with stereological counts of PV-immunoreactive neurons

claims.text: The number of parvalbumin-expressing GABAergic interneurons, identified independently by Vicia Villosa Agglutinin staining, was unaltered in Shank3B-/- mice.
claims.limO: A null result reported without any power analysis, confidence interval or equivalence test, so 'unaltered' cannot be distinguished from 'not detected with the n used'. Stereology in three regions across four genotypes with no stated animal numbers is the weakest possible form in which to present a negative. VVA labels the perineuronal net rather than the neuron itself, and perineuronal net integrity is itself activity-dependent, so an unchanged VVA count is not a fully independent cell count.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mice, studied alongside Shank1-/-, PV-/- and PV+/- mice
claims.measure: stereological counts of VVA-positive neurons as a parvalbumin-independent marker of the Pvalb neuron subpopulation

claims.text: DNA methylation was significantly increased in three intragenic CpG islands of SHANK3 in postmortem brain tissue from 54 individuals with autism spectrum disorders compared with 43 controls.
claims.n: 54 ASD postmortem brain tissues and 43 controls
claims.limO: No methylation differences, confidence intervals or p values are given, and no correction across the five CpG islands tested is described. Brain region, postmortem interval, tissue pH, age and sex are all absent from the abstract, and every one of them influences measured methylation. The cohort is idiopathic ASD, not PMS: no participant is stated to carry a SHANK3 deletion or point mutation, so this cannot be read as evidence about PMS brain tissue. Postmortem brain is not a measurable biomarker in a living child.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: DNA methylation profiling of five CpG islands (CGI-1 to CGI-5) in SHANK3

claims.text: The increased methylation was clustered in CGI-2 and CGI-4 in approximately 15% of the ASD brain tissues.
claims.eff: approximately 15% of ASD brain tissues; denominator for the percentage and dispersion not reported in the abstract
claims.limO: Roughly 15% of 54 is about eight samples, so the subgroup driving the overall difference is very small and no threshold for calling a sample 'epimutated' is stated in the abstract. If the group difference in R-0416 rests on this subgroup, the finding is a minority phenomenon rather than a general property of ASD brain, and the abstract does not say whether the comparison was significant after excluding it.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: per-sample clustering of SHANK3 CGI-2 and CGI-4 methylation

claims.text: Altered expression and alternative splicing of SHANK3 isoforms were observed in the brain tissues with increased methylation of SHANK3 CpG islands.
claims.limO: Neither the direction nor the magnitude of the expression change is stated, and the abstract does not say how many samples were analysed for expression. The association between methylation and isoform expression is correlational within a small, selected subset of samples, which is the configuration most prone to regression to the mean. SHANK3 has at least five intragenic promoters and extensive splicing, so 'altered expression and alternative splicing' summarises many comparisons in one phrase.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: isoform-specific SHANK3 expression and alternative splicing of coding exons

claims.text: A DNA methylation inhibitor modified the methylation of SHANK3 CpG islands and altered the isoform-specific expression of SHANK3 in cultured cells.
claims.limO: The cell line, the compound, the concentration and the exposure time are all absent, and the direction of the expression change is not stated. DNA methylation inhibitors act genome-wide, so an effect on SHANK3 expression is not evidence of a SHANK3-specific mechanism. The cells are not neurons and not patient-derived as far as the abstract states.
claims.model: cultured cells; cell line not identified in the abstract
claims.measure: SHANK3 CpG island methylation and isoform-specific SHANK3 expression in cultured cells

claims.text: Shank3B null mutant mice displayed a dramatic resistance to pentylenetetrazol-induced seizure induction relative to wildtype littermates, and this finding replicated in two independently bred and tested cohorts.
claims.n: two full cohorts; animal numbers not reported in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors frame the study as a replication and robustness exercise and present the EEG phenotype as newly quantified in this model.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, PTZ dose, effect size or p value appear in the abstract, so 'dramatic' is unquantified. The replication is across two cohorts within the same collaborating group rather than by an independent laboratory, which is a weaker claim than the word 'replicable' in the title suggests. Direction is clinically counterintuitive: people with PMS have a raised rather than lowered seizure risk, so this phenotype runs opposite to the human condition and should not be read as a trial-ready target-engagement marker.
claims.model: Shank3B null mutant (Shank3B KO) mice with wildtype littermate controls
claims.measure: EEG recorded via wireless implanted telemeters; seizure threshold after PTZ challenge

claims.text: Shank3B null mutant mice showed an enhancement of gamma band oscillatory EEG activity indicative of enhanced inhibitory tone, replicated in two separate cohorts.
claims.n: two full cohorts; animal numbers not reported in the abstract
claims.limO: No power values, frequency bounds, animal numbers or statistics are given in the abstract. 'Indicative of enhanced inhibitory tone' is an interpretation of a spectral measure rather than a direct measurement of inhibition. The increase is in resting-state gamma power and is not the same measure as the absent 40-Hz auditory steady-state response reported in a human SHANK3 duplication case (R-0403), so the two must not be treated as the same marker pointing in opposite directions without full-text comparison of the methods.
claims.model: Shank3B null mutant (Shank3B KO) mice with wildtype littermate controls
claims.measure: gamma band power from wireless telemetric EEG over 7 days of baseline recording

claims.text: Shank3B null mutant mice exhibited repetitive grooming, deficits in aspects of reciprocal social interactions and vocalisations and reduced open field activity, with variable deficits in sensory responses, anxiety-related behaviours and learning and memory.
claims.n: two full cohorts; animal numbers not reported in the abstract
claims.limO: The word 'variable' covers the domains that did not replicate cleanly, and the abstract does not say which tests failed, in which cohort, or with what power; those non-replications are the most informative part of a replication study and are the part left unquantified here. Reduced open field activity is a motor confound for several of the other assays, including social interaction and grooming scores, and the abstract does not say whether it was adjusted for. Sex is not reported for any assay.
claims.model: Shank3B null mutant (Shank3B KO) mice with wildtype littermate controls
claims.measure: battery of established behavioural tests covering social, repetitive, cognitive, anxiety-related, sensory and motor domains, with two or more corroborative tests per domain

claims.text: A gradient-boosted machine-learning classifier trained on 40-Hz auditory steady-state response intertrial phase coherence features discriminated participants with PMS from typically developing participants with an AUROC of 0.83.
claims.n: 123 participants in total (42 typically developing aged 2-30, 56 idiopathic ASD aged 3-31, 25 PMS aged 2-26); the PMS vs TD model therefore rests on 67 participants
claims.eff: AUROC = 0.83, reported without confidence interval, without sensitivity/specificity and without calibration
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: Leave-one-out cross-validation reuses the same 67 participants that defined the feature set and the hyperparameters; there is no external or held-out cohort. The AUROC carries no confidence interval, which for 25 cases is a wide interval in practice. Feature selection appears to have been made across several families (time-series, ERSP, FOOOF, ITPC) and only the best-performing family is reported, which inflates the figure unless the selection was nested inside the cross-validation — the abstract does not say it was. Age range 2-26 in the PMS group spans a period of large developmental change in gamma-band responses. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: machine learning (XGBoost gradient-boosted trees) applied to EEG 40-Hz ASSR features — time-series, ERSP, FOOOF-derived spectral and intertrial phase coherence — with leave-one-out cross-validation; discrimination reported as AUROC

claims.text: When the PMS-trained phase-coherence model was applied to individuals with idiopathic autism, 35.7% showed an elevated Synchrony Atypicality Index, interpreted by the authors as a PMS-like gamma-band phase-locking profile.
claims.n: 56 individuals with idiopathic ASD, scored by a model fitted on 25 PMS and 42 typically developing participants
claims.eff: 35.7% of the idiopathic ASD group above the elevated-SAI threshold; the threshold, its derivation and any confidence interval are not reported in the abstract
claims.limO: The proportion depends entirely on a cut-off that the abstract never defines; a different cut-off gives a different headline number. The index is derived from a model fitted on the same typically developing comparison group, so the idiopathic ASD scores are not independent of it. There is no test of whether a comparable proportion of other neurodevelopmental conditions, or of typically developing participants, would exceed the same threshold — which is exactly the specificity question a PMS stratification marker has to answer. The unsupervised clustering is reported as concordant but no cluster statistics are given.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: transfer of a trained, age- and sex-adjusted ITPC classifier to a separate diagnostic group to yield a continuous Synchrony Atypicality Index (SAI); unsupervised clustering of high-dimensional ITPC features as a secondary analysis

claims.text: Classification of idiopathic ASD versus PMS performed poorly in the full sample, and improved only after individuals with a high Synchrony Atypicality Index had been removed from the idiopathic ASD group.
claims.n: 56 idiopathic ASD and 25 PMS participants before exclusion; the number remaining after exclusion is not stated
claims.eff: not_reported — no accuracy, AUROC or confidence interval is given for either the full-sample or the restricted comparison
claims.limO: This is the batch's clearest negative result and it is reported without a single number.
