The reported improvement is produced by removing, from one class, the cases that a previous model scored as resembling the other class; re-running the classification afterwards necessarily separates the groups better and cannot be read as an independent finding. Whether the heterogeneity interpretation or a simpler ceiling on what 40-Hz ITPC can distinguish explains the initial poor performance cannot be decided from the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: supervised machine-learning classification (idiopathic ASD vs PMS) on EEG ITPC features, before and after removing cases selected by the model-derived SAI

claims.text: Fifty-two genes have peripheral blood expression profiles that scale with 22q13.3 deletion size in people with PMS.
claims.eff: not_reported — the abstract gives the gene count but neither the direction nor the magnitude of the scaling, nor the multiple-testing threshold
claims.limO: The abstract does not state whether expression falls or rises with deletion size, so the record cannot be used for a dosage prediction as it stands. Blood is not brain, and nothing establishes that these genes behave the same way in neural tissue. Deletion size is strongly correlated with the number of deleted genes, so a scaling relationship is close to expected for genes inside the interval and the abstract does not separate cis from trans effects for this set of 52. Single cohort, no replication sample.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: differential expression analysis of the peripheral blood transcriptome against deletion size (platform not stated in the abstract)

claims.text: Two hundred and eight genes are underexpressed in PMS participants with large class II deletions but unchanged in class I, are not located in 22q13.3, and are enriched for glycosphingolipid metabolism, NCAM1 interactions and cytotoxic natural killer cell signatures.
claims.eff: not_reported — no fold changes, false discovery rate or enrichment statistics are given in the abstract
claims.limO: A gene list with enrichment terms is a hypothesis about biology, not a demonstration of it: none of the 208 genes is functionally validated here, and enrichment results depend on the annotation database and background gene set, neither of which is named in the abstract. Because these genes lie outside 22q13.3, the inference that the deletion causes their underexpression is correlational and could also reflect differences in blood cell composition between the two genotype classes — which the authors' own deconvolution result (R-0605) shows is present. Single cohort, no external replication.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: differential expression analysis between genotype classes, followed by gene-set / pathway enrichment analysis

claims.text: In silico deconvolution of the blood transcriptome predicted a reduced proportion of CD56+ CD16- natural killer cells in PMS participants with class II mutations, and the prediction was confirmed by mass cytometry.
claims.n: 76 individuals with PMS in the transcriptomic analysis; the number of samples used for the mass cytometry validation is not stated in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported — neither the predicted nor the measured NK cell proportions, nor their difference between genotype classes, are quantified in the abstract
claims.limO: This is the one computational prediction in the batch that was checked against an independent measurement, which is why it is graded more favourably than the rest — but the check was run in the same participants that generated the prediction, so it establishes that the deconvolution is internally accurate, not that the finding generalises to another PMS cohort. The deconvolution reference matrix and algorithm are not named in the abstract, and reference-based deconvolution inherits the biases of whatever reference it uses. No numbers are given for either measurement.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: in silico cell-type deconvolution of bulk blood transcriptome into immune cell proportions, with orthogonal experimental validation by mass cytometry time-of-flight (CyTOF)

claims.text: Twenty-four serum metabolites are significantly altered in PMS participants with class II mutations, with a general reduction in sphingolipid metabolism.
claims.n: 76 individuals with PMS (37 class I, 39 class II)
claims.eff: not_reported — the 24 metabolites are not named and no fold changes, p values or false discovery rate are given in the abstract
claims.limO: The convergence between the metabolomic sphingolipid signal and the transcriptomic glycosphingolipid enrichment comes from the same 76 participants and the same blood draws, so it is internal consistency rather than independent replication, and should not be cited as corroboration. Metabolomes are strongly affected by diet, medication, fasting state and age, none of which is reported as controlled in the abstract — all plausibly differ between people with large and small deletions, who differ in feeding difficulties and medication burden. Serum, not cerebrospinal fluid or brain.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: untargeted global metabolomics profiling of serum, with pathway-level interpretation

claims.text: A multiclass support vector machine trained on Social Communication Questionnaire profiles correctly classified 55% of individuals into one of thirteen genetic syndrome groups or an idiopathic autism group.
claims.n: over 1500 individuals across thirteen syndrome groups plus 254 autistic individuals without a known genetic syndrome; the Phelan-McDermid group is 35 individuals
claims.eff: 55% of individuals correctly classified; no confidence interval, no chance-level baseline and no per-class sensitivity or specificity are reported in the abstract
claims.limA: Cross-sectional design; reliance on a screening tool focused primarily on social communication skills; imbalanced sample sizes across syndrome groups.
claims.limO: An overall accuracy across fourteen very unequal classes is dominated by the large groups (fragile X n = 297, Prader-Willi n = 278) and says little about the small ones, which include PMS at n = 35. The abstract reports no comparison against a trivial baseline that always predicts the largest class, so 55% cannot be interpreted. No external validation cohort is mentioned and the cross-validation scheme is not described. The input is a 40-item screening questionnaire, not a direct observational assessment.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: supervised machine learning — multiclass support vector machine classification of Social Communication Questionnaire scores, with self-help skills as an additional predictor

claims.text: Phelan-McDermid syndrome showed less phenotypic specificity of autistic characteristics than Angelman, fragile X, Prader-Willi, Rubinstein-Taybi and Cornelia de Lange syndromes.
claims.n: 35 individuals with Phelan-McDermid syndrome within a sample of over 1500
claims.eff: not_reported — the abstract ranks the syndrome groups qualitatively and gives no per-class accuracy for Phelan-McDermid syndrome or for any other group
claims.limA: Cross-sectional design; screening instrument focused on social communication; imbalanced sample sizes across syndrome groups.
claims.limO: The groups said to show greater specificity are also among the largest (fragile X 297, Prader-Willi 278, Cornelia de Lange 199), and the groups said to show less specificity include several of the smallest (PMS 35, Sotos 40, Smith-Magenis 54). Classifier accuracy rises with class size, so the reported ordering is confounded with sample size and cannot be read as a statement about PMS biology. A screening questionnaire covering mainly social communication is also unlikely to capture what distinguishes PMS, in which severe language absence and motor impairment dominate. This record should not be cited as evidence that PMS lacks a characteristic autism profile.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: per-syndrome classification performance of a multiclass support vector machine on Social Communication Questionnaire profiles, read as an index of phenotypic specificity

claims.text: Adding an idiopathic autism reference group and self-help skills as a predictor did not change the accuracy of the classification model.
claims.n: over 1500 individuals with genetic syndromes plus 254 autistic individuals without a known genetic syndrome
claims.eff: not_reported — no accuracies are given for the compared model variants and no equivalence margin is defined
claims.limO: A null result stated without numbers: 'did not change' could cover anything from identical accuracy to a difference the study was not powered to detect. Adaptive or self-help measures are strongly correlated with overall intellectual disability, so their failure to add information may mean the questionnaire already encodes that variance rather than that adaptive function is uninformative.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: comparison of multiclass support vector machine accuracy with and without an idiopathic ASD class and with and without self-help skills as a predictor

claims.text: An in silico preselection of 30,000 compounds feeding a biochemical CLK2 assay screen identified a potent indazole CLK inhibitor series proposed as a therapeutic approach for Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
claims.n: 30,000 compounds screened; number of hits and of confirmed actives not stated in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported — no IC50, selectivity ratio or hit rate is given in the abstract
claims.limO: The in silico method is not named, so the virtual screen cannot be reproduced or assessed; 'an in silico approach' could be anything from a pharmacophore filter to docking. No prospective comparison against random library selection is reported, so the contribution of the computational step to the hit rate is unknown. Potency is asserted without numbers. CLK2 is several steps removed from SHANK3 itself.
claims.model: cell-free biochemical assay with recombinant CLK2; compound set of 30,000 chosen from a larger library by an unspecified in silico method
claims.measure: in silico virtual screening / compound preselection, followed by a biochemical CLK2 Caliper enzymatic assay

claims.text: High-resolution X-ray structures of all four CLK family kinases, including the first reported CLK4 structure, were solved bound to known CLK2 inhibitor tool compounds and reveal the basis of inhibitor selectivity within the family.
claims.eff: not_reported — resolutions, space groups and accession codes are not given in the abstract
claims.limO: Structures of a kinase bound to an inhibitor explain selectivity retrospectively; the abstract reports no prospective test that the structural insight predicted selectivity for a new compound. No Protein Data Bank accession is cited in the abstract, so the structures cannot be checked from it. SHANK3 is not present anywhere in this experiment.
claims.model: recombinant human CLK1, CLK2, CLK3 and CLK4 proteins in complex with tool inhibitors TG003 and CX-4945
claims.measure: X-ray crystallography of protein-inhibitor complexes (structure determination, not computational modelling)

claims.text: The efficacy of the new indazole-series CLK2 inhibitors was demonstrated in a mouse brain slice assay.
claims.limO: The readout, the concentrations, the number of slices and animals, and the comparison condition are all absent from the abstract, so 'efficacy' cannot be interpreted — including whether the assay measured target engagement, splicing, or any synaptic or SHANK3-related endpoint at all. Wild-type tissue, so the experiment cannot show rescue of a Shank3-deficient phenotype. Flagged for full-text retrieval.
claims.model: mouse brain slices; strain, genotype and age not stated in the abstract. No Shank3 manipulation is reported.
claims.measure: mouse brain slice assay; the readout is not stated in the abstract

claims.text: Two structurally different CLK inhibitors produced genotoxicity findings in the human lymphocyte micronucleus test, which the authors present as a major concern for pan-CLK inhibition in Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
claims.eff: not_reported — no concentrations, fold increases or donor numbers are given in the abstract
claims.limO: The concentrations tested, the number of donors and whether the effect occurred at pharmacologically relevant exposures are all unstated, and an in vitro micronucleus signal at high concentration does not by itself establish in vivo genotoxic risk; no in vivo genotoxicity data are reported in the abstract. That two chemically distinct inhibitors both showed it strengthens the case that the effect is mechanism-related rather than compound-specific, which is what makes this the more serious reading. This is the only safety-limiting result in the batch and should be carried into any discussion of CLK2 inhibition for PMS.
claims.model: in vitro human lymphocyte micronucleus test
claims.measure: micronucleus formation in cultured human lymphocytes (in vitro genotoxicity assay)

claims.text: Shank3fx mice show reduced population-level neural activity and a less integrated, more rigid prefrontal microcircuit than wild-type mice during social behaviour.
claims.n: not_reported — neither the number of mice nor the number of imaged neurons is given in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported — no network metric values, group differences, confidence intervals or p values are given in the abstract
claims.limO: Functional connectivity inferred from correlated calcium activity is not synaptic connectivity, and graph metrics computed from it depend heavily on the correlation threshold and the binarisation rule used to build the graph — none of which is described in the abstract. Miniscope studies typically use very small numbers of animals and the abstract gives none. Calcium imaging also conflates changes in firing rate with changes in connectivity, and the paper reports reduced activity alongside reduced integration, so the two findings are not independent. Single laboratory, no replication known.
claims.model: Shank3fx (floxed / conditional Shank3 allele); the exons targeted and the isoforms affected are not stated in the abstract, nor is the Cre driver or whether the allele was recombined
claims.measure: graph-theoretic network analysis (integration and related network metrics) of functional connectivity between individual neurons, derived from miniscope single-photon calcium imaging in freely behaving mice during social behaviour tasks

claims.text: Machine learning applied to graph-theoretic metrics from prefrontal microcircuits predicted genotype and genotype-associated social behaviour differences between Shank3fx and wild-type mice.
claims.eff: not_reported — no accuracy, AUC, confidence interval or cross-validation scheme is given in the abstract
claims.limO: A classifier trained and evaluated on a small number of mice, with the unit of analysis unstated, risks predicting the animal rather than the genotype: if multiple recordings or sessions from the same mouse appear in both training and test folds, the reported predictive performance is not genotype prediction at all. The abstract names neither the algorithm, nor the validation scheme, nor any performance figure, so the claim is currently unverifiable. No external dataset. This record is kept chiefly as an inventory item: it is machine learning applied to Shank3 circuit data, not a mechanistic model.
claims.model: Shank3fx (floxed / conditional Shank3 allele); details as for R-0614
claims.measure: supervised machine learning (algorithm not stated) applied to graph-theoretic network features to classify genotype and to predict social behaviour differences

claims.text: In Monte Carlo simulations of a five-timepoint trial of intranasal insulin in children with Phelan-McDermid syndrome, stepped wedge designs were competitive in power with parallel-group and matched-pairs designs, and in some settings the most powerful.
claims.n: simulated data only; the number of Monte Carlo replications and the simulated sample sizes are not stated in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported — no power values and no simulated parameter grid are given in the abstract
claims.limO: The result holds only under the assumed model and the assumed parameter values, and the abstract reports neither. A power simulation cannot establish that the linear mixed-effects model with five time points describes real developmental trajectories in PMS; if developmental age plateaus or regresses, as it does in a substantial minority of this population, the model is misspecified and the power ordering may not survive. The simulation also does not represent the non-statistical costs that distinguish these designs in practice — carryover, differential dropout, and the loss of blinding inherent in a stepped wedge. Indexed by the database partly as a Review, although the abstract describes an original simulation study. This is a trial-design simulation, not a model of SHANK3 biology.
claims.model: Monte Carlo simulation under a subject-specific linear mixed-effects model for developmental age across five longitudinal time points, with small sample sizes chosen to reflect a rare disorder
claims.measure: Monte Carlo simulation of statistical power for parallel group, matched-pairs, delayed start and several stepped wedge designs, under an assumed linear mixed-effects model with developmental age as the primary outcome

claims.text: Under the assumed statistical model, the parallel group, matched-pairs, delayed start and stepped wedge designs can all be represented as special cases of a stepped wedge or delayed treatment design.
claims.n: not_applicable — an analytical statement about the model, not an estimate from data
claims.limO: A statement about a model, true by construction within it and carrying no empirical content. It is charted because it is what licenses comparing these designs on a single power scale in R-0616; if the unifying model is wrong for PMS developmental data, that comparison loses its basis. The equivalence also holds only for the statistical structure and not for the practical and ethical differences between the designs.
claims.model: subject-specific linear mixed-effects model for a longitudinal outcome at five time points
claims.measure: analytical reformulation of trial designs within a common linear mixed-effects framework

claims.text: In a graph neural network analysis of protein interactions built from type 2 diabetes GWAS genes and pancreatic single-cell expression, SHANK3 was identified as one of the key genes in the network, alongside SOX10, NCF4 and OSM.
claims.n: 161 genes overlapping between the GWAS-derived set and single-cell expression; the number of donors or cells is not stated in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported — no network centrality values, model performance metrics or significance tests are given in the abstract
claims.limO: The analysis was deliberately restricted to chromosome 22 variants, which is where SHANK3 lies, so the gene's appearance among the highlighted hubs is close to built in rather than discovered. Hub status in a curated protein-protein interaction network also tracks how intensively a protein has been studied, and SHANK3 is heavily studied; degree centrality in such networks is a literature artefact as much as a biological property. No experimental validation, no external dataset, no performance metrics, single-author preprint that is not peer reviewed. The record is charted as an inventory item and as specificity evidence, and should not be read as evidence of a role for SHANK3 in type 2 diabetes.
claims.model: integration of GWAS summary statistics (~29.7 million variants, filtered to high-confidence chromosome 22 variants), polygenic risk scores, pancreatic single-cell RNA sequencing, and a graph neural network over a protein-protein interaction network
claims.measure: graph neural network applied to a protein-protein interaction network, combined with GWAS-derived polygenic risk scoring and single-cell differential expression

claims.text: Among 59 craniosynostosis patients analysed by whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing, one carried a 22q13 duplication.
claims.eff: not_applicable — a single observed carrier, with no comparison to population frequency
claims.limO: The abstract does not state the coordinates or size of the duplication, whether SHANK3 lies inside it, whether it was inherited or de novo, or whether it was judged causal for the craniosynostosis phenotype. It therefore cannot support any statement about SHANK3 dosage and is charted as a lead to be resolved from the full text, not as evidence. A single carrier in a cohort ascertained for an unrelated phenotype carries no information about penetrance or phenotype.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing with targeted in silico panel filtering and detection of structural genomic aberrations

claims.text: In silico structural simulation using AlphaFold3 and HADDOCK predicted that gut-microbiota-associated aberrant phosphorylation remodels SHANK3 and SRRM2 conformations and weakens the binding affinity of SHANK3.
claims.n: not_applicable — number of structures, docking runs and replicates not stated in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported — no docking scores, binding energies, RMSD values or AlphaFold confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE) are given in the abstract
claims.limO: Docking scores are not binding affinities and HADDOCK scores in particular are not calibrated energies; a predicted weakening cannot be converted into a measurable quantity. SHANK3 is a large multidomain protein with long disordered regions, exactly the case where structure prediction confidence is lowest, and no confidence metric is reported. The phosphosites come from mouse hippocampal tissue and are not shown to occur on human SHANK3. Crucially, the structural prediction itself received no experimental validation anywhere in the study: the protein that was validated by Western blot and ELISA was FNDC3A, not SHANK3. No control simulations of unrelated phosphosites are reported. The authors' own wording is hedged ('may promote', 'potentially remodeling') and the record should be read at that strength.
claims.model: AlphaFold3 structure prediction of SHANK3 and SRRM2 in phosphorylated and unphosphorylated states, with HADDOCK protein-protein docking; the phosphosites modelled derive from a mouse hippocampal phosphoproteomic screen
claims.measure: protein structure prediction (AlphaFold3) combined with protein-protein docking (HADDOCK), used to estimate conformational change and binding affinity

claims.text: Faecal microbiota transplantation from children with autism into antibiotic-treated mice reduced hippocampal synaptic density and downregulated the synaptic proteins SYP and PSD-95.
claims.n: not_reported — neither donor numbers nor recipient numbers per group are given in the abstract
claims.limO: Donor and recipient numbers, blinding and randomisation are all absent from the abstract. Microbiota transplantation studies are highly sensitive to donor selection, donor pooling and cage effects, and a cage is not an independent unit of analysis; nothing in the abstract indicates these were handled. SHANK3 itself was not measured in this experiment — the SHANK3 link in this paper is purely computational. The claim is relevant to the molecular and synaptic links of the chain but tells us nothing specific to PMS.
claims.model: antibiotic-treated recipient mice receiving faecal microbiota from children with autism or from typically developing children; strain not stated in the abstract and no Shank3 genotype is involved
claims.measure: synaptic density, and SYP and PSD-95 protein expression, in hippocampal tissue; quantification method not stated in the abstract

claims.text: Of 16,894 SHANK3 single-nucleotide polymorphisms retrieved from public databases, 1,179 were missense and 29 were unanimously classified as deleterious by all prediction tools applied.
claims.eff: 29 of 1,179 missense variants (2.5%) unanimously predicted deleterious; no benchmark against known pathogenic SHANK3 variants and no performance metrics are reported
claims.limO: Agreement between pathogenicity predictors is not independent corroboration: these tools share training data, conservation features and in several cases each other's outputs, so unanimity overstates confidence rather than establishing it. The abstract reports no benchmarking against SHANK3 variants of known clinical significance, so the false-positive rate of this pipeline on this gene is unknown. Allele frequencies are not considered, meaning a common benign variant and a singleton are treated alike. The source databases are not named, so the starting set cannot be reproduced. No experimental validation of any predicted variant. Most importantly for this corpus: these are predictions about variants, not a model of SHANK3 function or dosage.
claims.model: human SHANK3 reference sequence and derived structural models; variants extracted from public SNP databases, which are not named in the abstract
claims.measure: in silico variant effect prediction — consensus across multiple sequence- and structure-based pathogenicity predictors, followed by secondary structure and protein stability analysis

claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulation of the three most destabilising predicted SHANK3 mutations (L47P, G54W and G250D) showed significant changes in intramolecular interactions and high fluctuation of residues 1-350, affecting the ankyrin repeat domain.
claims.n: three mutants simulated; number of replicate simulations not stated
claims.eff: not_reported — no simulation length, replicate count, RMSD or RMSF values and no statistics are given in the abstract
claims.limO: No simulation time, number of replicates, force field or explicit wild-type control is reported, and short single-replicate simulations of point mutants routinely produce fluctuation differences that do not reproduce on repetition. SHANK3 has no full-length experimental structure, so the models simulated are partial and modelled rather than solved, which propagates into every downstream quantity. The mutations simulated were chosen because they were predicted destabilising, so finding them destabilised in simulation is close to circular. None is validated experimentally. This record is the most mechanistic computational work in the batch and it still models a single domain of an isolated protein, not its function in a synapse.
claims.model: modelled structures of the SHANK3 N-terminal region carrying L47P, G54W or G250D, after protein stability prediction; force field, solvent model and simulation length are not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: molecular dynamics simulation of mutant versus modelled wild-type SHANK3 fragments, with upstream protein stability prediction, reported as intramolecular interaction changes and per-residue fluctuation

claims.text: Two consensus deleterious variants, G250C/D and G635R, fall within the first and second binding domains of SHANK3, and none of the consensus deleterious variants falls in a known post-translational modification site.
claims.eff: not_applicable — a positional annotation, not an estimate
claims.limO: The null half of this claim is weaker than it looks: post-translational modification sites in SHANK3 are incompletely annotated, so finding no deleterious variant in one is at least as likely to reflect sparse annotation as real biology, and absence of evidence should not be read as a conclusion about phosphorylation-dependent mechanisms. The domain assignment depends on an annotation source the abstract does not name. No experimental evidence that these positions matter functionally.
claims.model: mapping of consensus deleterious missense variants onto annotated SHANK3 domains and post-translational modification sites; the annotation source is not named in the abstract
claims.measure: in silico mapping of predicted deleterious variants onto protein functional domains and annotated post-translational modification sites

claims.text: An ensemble analysis integrating brain proteomics, WGCNA, machine learning and protein-protein interaction networks nominated 24 Dragon's Blood radiation-mitigation-related proteins, among which Shank3 was one of eight ligand-target proteins.
claims.n: not_reported (number of rats contributing proteomes not stated in the abstract)
claims.eff: not_reported (no importance scores, no cross-validation metrics, no confidence intervals reported in the abstract)
claims.limO: This is gene-list bioinformatics, not a mechanistic model. The machine-learning algorithm, the cross-validation scheme, the number of input proteins and the number of animals are all absent from the abstract. The 24-protein list is derived from, and reported on, the same proteomic dataset that generated it, with no external or held-out set. Shank3 enters as one of 24 names with no SHANK3-specific experiment behind it. The pipeline is a discovery heuristic whose false-positive rate is unstated.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: feature selection on proteomic data: weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) plus machine learning plus protein-protein interaction network construction

claims.text: Molecular docking identified three Dragon's Blood constituents (socotrin-4'-ol, cinnabarone and 2'-methoxysocotrin-5'-ol) as interacting with all eight nominated targets, including Shank3.
claims.eff: not_reported (no binding energies, scoring function, docking software or pose quality metrics given in the abstract)
claims.limO: Docking scores without free-energy validation, without molecular dynamics refinement and without any experimental binding assay are hypothesis-generating at best. No binding affinity, no scoring threshold and no decoy control are reported. The structure of SHANK3 used for docking is not stated, which matters because most of SHANK3 has no experimentally solved full-length structure. A claim that a small molecule 'interacts with Shank3' on docking evidence alone should not be read as target engagement.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: molecular docking (ligand-protein binding pose prediction)

claims.text: In whole-brain irradiated rats, Shank3 was among eight brain proteins dysregulated by radiation and restored by Dragon's Blood administration.
claims.eff: not_reported (no fold change, p value or confidence interval for Shank3 specifically)
claims.limO: The direction of the radiation-induced Shank3 change is not stated in the abstract, only that it was 'dysregulated' and 'restored' — so the record cannot say whether Shank3 went up or down. Sample size, dose and duration are absent. Shank3 is one of eight proteins reported out of a genome-scale proteomic screen with no stated multiple-testing correction, and no orthogonal validation (western blot, targeted MS) of the Shank3 change is described.
claims.model: wild-type rat, whole-brain irradiation; strain not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: Shank3 protein abundance, brain tissue proteomics

claims.text: A random forest analysis of differentially expressed genes from an autism blood transcriptome dataset selected SHANK3 among the ten key feature genes with the highest importance scores for autism prediction.
claims.n: not_reported (GSE18123 sample size not stated in the abstract)
claims.eff: not_reported (importance scores not given; no confidence intervals)
claims.limO: A single public dataset (GSE18123), reanalysed with no independent validation cohort: the random forest is trained and evaluated on the same samples that produced the differentially expressed gene list, which inflates apparent performance. Sample size is not stated anywhere in the abstract. The direction of SHANK3 differential expression is not reported. Connectivity Map drug predictions are computational and were not tested. No experimental validation of any of the ten genes is described.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: machine learning (random forest feature selection) applied to differentially expressed genes from a public blood microarray dataset, with protein-protein interaction network construction, functional enrichment and Connectivity Map drug prediction

claims.text: In ROC analysis of the selected feature genes, MGAT4C showed the strongest discriminatory power between autism and controls (AUC = 0.730); no AUC is reported for SHANK3.
claims.eff: AUC = 0.730 for MGAT4C; no confidence interval reported; no AUC reported for SHANK3
claims.limO: The AUC is presented with no confidence interval and no sample size, so its precision cannot be assessed at all. The best-performing gene is not SHANK3, and SHANK3's own discriminative performance is simply not stated — a selective-reporting pattern worth recording. The ROC is computed on the same dataset used for feature selection, so it is a resubstitution estimate, not validation. An AUC of 0.730 is in any case well below any threshold used for a clinically actionable diagnostic marker. The authors nevertheless describe it as 'robust'.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: receiver operating characteristic analysis (AUC) of individual gene expression for case-control discrimination

claims.text: In silico screening identified a CpG-rich region upstream of SHANK3 exon 3 as the most suitable locus for designing a high-resolution melting methylation assay.
claims.eff: not_reported (no selection criteria, scores or thresholds given in the abstract)
claims.limO: The criteria by which this locus was judged 'most suitable' are not stated, nor is the software, nor how many candidate regions were compared. SHANK3 has multiple promoters and the choice of a single upstream-of-exon-3 region is not justified against the others in the abstract. Nothing links this locus to any PMS-relevant regulatory function.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: in silico CpG island / primer design screening of bisulfite-converted SHANK3 sequence

claims.text: Two of three designed primer sets amplified the target SHANK3 region and produced melting profiles that discriminated fully methylated from unmethylated control DNA on two HRM platforms.
claims.n: 3 primer sets, of which 2 amplified; commercial control DNAs, number of replicates not reported
claims.eff: not_reported (no melting temperature differences, no sensitivity or limit of detection, no quantitative discrimination metric)
claims.limO: Qualitative discrimination between 0% and 100% methylated commercial controls is the easiest possible test and says nothing about performance at intermediate methylation levels, which is where real samples sit. No limit of detection, no linearity across a methylation standard curve, no replicate precision and no patient or control human samples at all. The authors state the assay is 'qualitative'; it therefore cannot support any dose-response claim about SHANK3 methylation. One of three primer sets failed, and no explanation is offered.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: locus-specific high-resolution melting (HRM) of bisulfite-converted DNA, on LightCycler 480 and CFX96 platforms

claims.text: RevGraphVAMP, an unsupervised model combining graph convolutional neural networks with the variational approach for Markov processes and physical constraint optimisation, showed improved accuracy in state transition prediction compared with other VAMPNets models when applied to molecular dynamics trajectories, including those of the Shank3-Rap1 complex.
claims.n: 2 public benchmark datasets plus 1 protein complex (Shank3-Rap1); trajectory lengths and replica counts not reported
claims.eff: not_reported (VAMP scores, accuracy figures and comparator performance not quantified in the abstract)
claims.limO: A machine-learning method paper, not a study of SHANK3 biology: the Shank3-Rap1 complex is used as a demonstration case, so nothing is concluded about SHANK3 function, dosage or disease. No performance numbers, no error bars and no statistical comparison with the baseline VAMPNets are given in the abstract. The underlying molecular dynamics simulation length is not stated, which governs whether the inferred Markov states are converged at all.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: deep learning on molecular dynamics trajectories: graph convolutional neural network plus variational approach for Markov processes (VAMPnet), with an attention mechanism for interaction-region importance

claims.text: The model's attention mechanism was reported to identify key interaction regions and to improve discrimination between conformational substates, including for the Shank3-Rap1 complex.
claims.limO: No specific result about the Shank3-Rap1 complex is actually stated — which residues, which substates, which transitions. 'Interpretable results for protein structural characterisation' is a claim about the method, not a finding about SHANK3. Attention weights are not a causal or thermodynamic quantity and are not validated against any experimental structural observable here.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: attention-weighted dimensionality reduction of molecular dynamics trajectories; substate discrimination

claims.text: Early adolescent male Shank3B heterozygous mice showed enhanced learning performance on an odor-based two-alternative forced choice task compared with wild type siblings, while no gain of function was observed in females.
claims.n: not_reported (both sexes, numbers per genotype not given in the abstract)
claims.eff: not_reported (no effect size, confidence interval or p value in the abstract)
claims.limA: The authors frame the result as evidence that autism risk genes may produce strengths as well as challenges, and that sex and environmental uncertainty modulate the phenotype.
claims.limO: Sample sizes are not reported for any group, which is the central problem for a sex-by-genotype interaction claim: a result present in males and absent in females is a claim about an interaction, and the abstract never reports that the interaction itself was tested. Heterozygotes only, so no dose-response across genotypes is available. Preprint, not peer reviewed. No replication. The task is a single learning assay and generalisation to other domains is not established.
claims.model: Shank3B heterozygote (PDZ-domain-targeting deletion allele); Tsc2 heterozygote studied in parallel
claims.measure: learning performance on an odor-based two-alternative forced choice (2AFC) operant task

claims.text: A reinforcement learning computational model fitted to the mice's trial-by-trial choices attributed the gain of function in male Shank3B heterozygotes to an enhanced positive learning rate rather than to task engagement.
claims.eff: not_reported (no parameter estimates, credible intervals or model comparison statistics in the abstract)
claims.limO: Parameter values, model comparison against simpler alternatives, and any parameter-recovery or posterior-predictive check are all absent from the abstract, so it cannot be judged whether the learning-rate parameter is identifiable in this dataset. A latent parameter difference inferred from a behavioural fit is a description of the behaviour, not an independent mechanism: no synaptic, circuit or molecular measurement links the fitted learning rate to Shank3 dosage. The model is described as novel, so no external validation exists. Preprint.
claims.model: Shank3B heterozygote; Tsc2 heterozygote in parallel
claims.measure: reinforcement learning computational model: trial-by-trial estimation of positive and negative learning rates plus policy-level task engagement and disengagement

claims.text: The learning gain of function in male Shank3B heterozygous mice was absent when the animals were trained with a probabilistic reward schedule.
claims.limO: An absence of effect in a second condition, with no sample size and no equivalence or power analysis, cannot distinguish a genuine null from an underpowered one. The abstract does not report whether the condition-by-genotype interaction was formally tested. Preprint, no replication.
claims.model: Shank3B heterozygote
claims.measure: learning performance on the 2AFC task under a probabilistic reward schedule

claims.text: The SHANK3 polymorphism rs9616915 showed no significant association with autism spectrum disorder in a Bangladeshi sample of 90 cases and 90 controls.
claims.eff: Pearson chi-square p = 0.081; co-dominant p = 0.1131; dominant p = 0.3656; recessive p = 0.0569. No odds ratios or confidence intervals reported in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors restrict the negative conclusion to the southern Bangladeshi population.
claims.limO: 90 versus 90 is far too small for a common-variant association study; a null here is close to uninformative and the abstract reports no power calculation. Only p values are given — no odds ratios, no confidence intervals — so the range of effect sizes the data exclude cannot be determined. The recessive model p = 0.0569 is reported as null without comment. Population stratification is not addressed. The ASD diagnosis procedure is not described.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: genotype-phenotype association, PCR-RFLP plus Sanger sequencing; chi-square and logistic regression under co-dominant, dominant and recessive models

claims.text: In silico structural analysis of the SHANK3 rs9616915 variant predicted two hydrogen bonds between amino acids where the reference structure has one, which the authors interpret as a possible effect on protein stability.
claims.eff: not_reported (no stability free-energy change, no prediction score, no confidence measure)
claims.limO: Counting hydrogen bonds in a single static predicted structure is the weakest form of structural inference: no energy minimisation, no molecular dynamics, no delta-delta-G estimate and no comparison against a benchmark of known destabilising variants are reported. The direction of the stability effect is not even specified — an extra hydrogen bond could stabilise as easily as destabilise. The structural prediction directly contradicts the paper's own negative genetic association, and the abstract does not reconcile them.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: in silico prediction of functional and structural impact of a non-synonymous SNP; hydrogen-bond counting in the predicted protein structure

claims.text: A method combining depth-sensing infrared video, machine learning for animal and posture identification and RFID tracking tracked up to four group-housed mice over several days and extracted individual and collective behavioural profiles.
claims.n: groups of up to 4 mice, monitored over several days; total animal numbers not reported
claims.eff: not_reported (tracking accuracy figures not given in the abstract)
claims.limO: 'Tracks multiple mice accurately' is asserted without any accuracy figure, error rate or inter-rater comparison in the abstract. The number of behavioural traits extracted is not stated, which matters because multi-trait phenotypic profiling invites multiple comparisons. The method is an instrument, not a model of SHANK3 biology.
claims.model: Shank2 and Shank3 mutant mice; alleles not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: machine learning computer vision (depth-sensing camera plus posture classification) with RFID validation; extraction of individual and group behavioural traits

claims.text: Integration of the behavioural profiles of Shank3 mutant female mice revealed distinctive activity levels and distinctive involvement in complex social interactions compared with the other genotypes studied.
claims.eff: not_reported (no per-trait effect sizes, no p values, no correction for the number of traits tested)
claims.limO: 'Distinctive' is not a statistical statement: no effect sizes, no p values and no multiple-comparison correction are reported for a profile built from a large and unstated number of behavioural traits. Only females were characterised, so the sex-specificity of the profile is unknown from this report. The allele is unspecified, so the relationship to SHANK3 dosage cannot be established. Shank2 and Shank3 results are integrated in the reporting, which risks attributing to Shank3 what belongs to Shank2.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant mice; allele not specified in the abstract. Shank2 mutants studied in parallel
claims.measure: machine-learning-derived behavioural trait profile: activity level and participation in complex (three- and four-animal) social configurations

claims.text: In a computational DG-CA3 hippocampal network model in which reduced Shank3 protein was imitated by decreasing glutamatergic excitatory synaptic strength, the excitability of CA3 pyramidal neurons and oriens lacunosum-moleculare interneurons was strongly degraded as NMDA or AMPA synaptic strength was decreased.
claims.n: not_reported (number of simulated neurons and parameter sweep points not stated in the abstract)
claims.eff: not_reported (no quantitative mapping from percentage synaptic strength reduction to firing rate or power change in the abstract)
claims.limO: The link to SHANK3 is an assumption, not a result: Shank3 loss is represented simply as a scalar reduction in synaptic conductance, with no model of SHANK3 dosage, isoforms, scaffold stoichiometry or receptor trafficking, and the mapping from protein level to conductance is neither calibrated nor cited with a value. The model is not fitted to or validated against any SHANK3 or PMS dataset. Parameter values, sweep ranges and sensitivity analysis are absent from the abstract. Single laboratory, no replication, no code or model deposition reported. The target disease is Alzheimer's.
claims.model: conductance-based DG-CA3 hippocampal network model; Shank3 reduction represented as decreased glutamatergic synaptic strength
claims.measure: biophysical neuronal network simulation (DG-CA3 model) with power spectral analysis and dynamical systems analysis of firing rhythm

claims.text: In the same model, the relative power and the peak relative power density in the alpha band decreased as glutamatergic synaptic strength was decreased, which the authors relate to the reduction of alpha rhythm reported in Alzheimer's disease patients.
claims.eff: not_reported (no quantitative dose-response curve or slope reported in the abstract)
claims.limO: Agreement with a human EEG observation in Alzheimer's disease is treated as validation, but this is a qualitative directional match on a single feature, obtained after the human finding was known, and in a hippocampal network model whose output is not scalp EEG. No alternative parameter changes are shown to fail to produce the same alpha reduction, so the result is not specific to glutamatergic synapse loss. Nothing connects it to PMS, where the reported EEG phenotypes are not the same as the Alzheimer's alpha reduction.
claims.model: conductance-based DG-CA3 hippocampal network model
claims.measure: relative spectral power and peak relative power density in the alpha band, power spectral analysis of simulated network activity

claims.text: Homology modelling and molecular dynamics simulations indicated a deleterious effect of the SHANK1 p.(Gly126Arg) variant on protein structure and on function related to protein-protein interactions.
claims.eff: not_reported (no RMSD, no binding free energy, no simulation length, no replicate count)
claims.limO: Simulation length, replicate number, force field and any convergence check are absent from the abstract, and short unreplicated molecular dynamics runs routinely produce apparent destabilisation that does not survive longer sampling. The model is a homology model, so the starting structure is itself a prediction. 'Deleterious' is a computational verdict with no experimental assay of the variant protein. The variant is in SHANK1, and the clinical interpretation rests on a single mosaic case.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: homology modelling plus molecular dynamics simulation of variant versus reference protein structure

claims.text: The SHANK1 variant was predicted to disrupt a conserved region with high homology to a functionally relevant SHANK3 domain implicated in ligand binding, including non-canonical Rap1 binding.
claims.eff: not_reported (no sequence identity percentage, no alignment score, no binding energy)
claims.limO: Homology-based transfer of function in both directions: the SHANK1 region is called functional because a SHANK3 region is, and the SHANK3 domain's relevance is asserted from other work not reported here. No binding experiment with Rap1 or any other ligand is performed. Percent identity and alignment confidence are not given. A conserved region described as 'hitherto unknown' has by definition no independent functional annotation to check against.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: sequence and structural homology analysis between SHANK1 and SHANK3 domains, with inferred ligand-binding disruption

claims.text: In molecular dynamics simulations, the wild type SAPAP extended PDZ-binding motif bound tightly to the N-terminal extended PDZ domain of Shank3 throughout the simulation, whereas loss of binding was observed in different segments of the mutated peptides.
claims.n: 3 simulated systems (wild type, M4P, M5P); replicate count and simulation length not reported in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported in the abstract as numerical values (binding free energies computed by MM/GBSA are stated only as being in agreement with experimental affinities)
claims.limO: Simulation length, number of independent replicates and force field are not stated in the abstract, and MM/GBSA binding free energies are known to be sensitive to all three. The mutations modelled are engineered proline substitutions designed to match an earlier experiment, not patient variants: no PMS-associated SHANK3 variant is simulated. Only an isolated domain-peptide pair is modelled, not the assembled postsynaptic density, so nothing follows about SHANK3 abundance or scaffold stoichiometry in a synapse.
claims.model: molecular dynamics of the Shank3 N-terminal extended PDZ domain (N-PDZ) in complex with wild type and mutated SAPAP extended PDZ-binding motif (E-PBM) peptides
claims.measure: all-atom molecular dynamics simulation with conformational analysis, hydrogen bond analysis and per-residue energy decomposition

claims.text: The simulations indicate that two binding sites, the canonical PDZ domain and the betaN1-prime extension of Shank3, contribute independently to the binding of the SAPAP motif.
claims.eff: not_reported (no per-site binding energy contributions quantified in the abstract)
claims.limO: Independence is inferred from two proline-substitution mutants, which are blunt structural perturbations that can disrupt local backbone geometry beyond the intended site; a genuine test of independence would require a double mutant and an additivity analysis, which is not described. The betaN extension is reported as highly flexible, and conclusions about a flexible region are the most sensitive to insufficient sampling. Single laboratory, no independent computational replication.
claims.model: molecular dynamics of Shank3 N-PDZ with wild type and mutant SAPAP peptides
claims.measure: molecular dynamics with energy decomposition and hydrogen bond analysis; comparison of mutants disrupting each site

claims.text: Binding free energies between the Shank3 N-PDZ domain and the SAPAP peptides calculated by MM/GBSA were in agreement with experimentally measured binding affinities.
claims.n: 3 systems compared against previously published experimental affinities
claims.eff: not_reported (neither computed free energies nor experimental affinities, nor a correlation coefficient, are given in the abstract)
claims.limO: 'In agreement' is not quantified: no calculated values, no experimental values, no correlation and no error estimate appear in the abstract, so the strength of the validation cannot be judged. With three systems, any rank-order agreement is weak evidence. The experimental comparator is prior published work by others on the same constructs, and the proline mutants were chosen to match it, so the comparison is a consistency check on a small, pre-selected set rather than a blind prediction test. MM/GBSA without entropy treatment systematically overestimates absolute binding energies.
claims.model: MM/GBSA free energy calculation on molecular dynamics trajectories of Shank3 N-PDZ with SAPAP E-PBM peptides
claims.measure: binding free energy by Molecular Mechanics / Generalized Born Surface Area (MM/GBSA), compared with published experimental binding affinities

claims.text: In silico analysis revealed a putative microRNA-137 binding site in the SHANK2 3'UTR but found no such site in SHANK1 or SHANK3.
claims.eff: not_reported (prediction algorithm, score and threshold not stated in the abstract)
claims.limO: A negative result from a target-prediction algorithm is weak: the prediction tool, the score threshold and the 3'UTR annotation used are not named, and microRNA target prediction has a high false-negative rate, particularly for non-canonical sites. Unlike SHANK2, the SHANK3 negative was never tested experimentally in this study, so the absence of regulation is predicted, not demonstrated. SHANK3 has multiple annotated 3'UTR isoforms and the abstract does not say which was screened.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: in silico microRNA target site prediction in 3'UTR sequences

claims.text: miR-137 directly targets the SHANK2 3'UTR in a site-specific manner and lowers endogenous Shank2 protein in mouse hippocampal neurons without a detectable change in mRNA, indicating translational repression.
claims.n: not_reported (number of cultures and replicates not stated in the abstract)
claims.eff: not_reported (described as 'significantly lowered'; no magnitude, confidence interval or p value in the abstract)
claims.limO: Effect magnitudes and replicate numbers are absent. The conclusion that regulation is translational rests on a negative mRNA result whose sensitivity is not reported, so a small mRNA change cannot be excluded. Overexpression and inhibition of a microRNA are strong perturbations and do not establish that endogenous miR-137 sets Shank2 levels in vivo. Relevance to SHANK3 is by contrast only.
claims.model: human neuroblastoma cell line and mouse primary hippocampal neurons; luciferase reporter with wild type and mutated SHANK2 3'UTR
claims.measure: luciferase reporter assay, quantitative real-time PCR and western blot for Shank2

claims.text: A numerical simulation of the synaptic response in which Shank3 is disrupted at the postsynaptic density produced an alteration of excitatory AMPA receptor trafficking, presented as an illustration that synaptic modelling can yield quantitative properties of neurological disease states.
claims.n: not_applicable (simulation; number of modelled synapses and parameter sets not reported)
claims.eff: not_reported (no simulated current amplitudes, receptor numbers or parameter values given in the abstract)
claims.limO: This is a brief report whose stated purpose is to illustrate a modelling approach, so the Shank3 simulation is presented as a demonstration rather than as a tested result: no parameter values, no calibration against SHANK3 or PMS data, no sensitivity analysis and no comparison with experimental measurements from a Shank3-deficient synapse. 'Disruption' is binary in the abstract, with no graded dosage, so it does not yet support a dose-response prediction. Published in 2012; no replication or extension to PMS is reported here.
claims.model: biophysical / kinetic model of synaptic transmission incorporating vesicular release location, neurotransmitter molecule number, receptor number and type, and synapse geometry; Shank3 disruption represented at the postsynaptic density
claims.measure: numerical simulation of the synaptic response: AMPA receptor trafficking and resulting postsynaptic current, combined with electrophysiological recordings for the separate ketogenic diet analysis

claims.text: Basal dendritic morphology, spine density, spine morphology, asymmetric synapse density and postsynaptic density length in medial prefrontal cortex layer III were comparable between Shank3-knockout, Shank3-heterozygous and wild-type rats.
claims.n: not_reported (number of rats per genotype not stated in the abstract)
claims.limA: The rat deletion does not affect all Shank3 isoforms and models only mutations causing loss of the N-terminus; the ultrastructural study was restricted to males.
claims.limO: This null arrives without any of the three things that would make it evidence of absence: no statistical test statistic is given for the comparisons reported as similar or comparable, no power calculation or minimum detectable effect is stated, and no confidence interval is attached. The abstract reports the positive comparisons with the word significantly and the null ones with the words similar and comparable, which is a reporting asymmetry, not a result. The authors themselves describe the findings as preliminary. Sample sizes per genotype are absent. This record should be read as no difference detected, not as no difference.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient rat; homozygous knockout and heterozygous; the deletion does not affect all isoforms and models only loss of the N-terminus
claims.measure: dendrite and spine morphology and spine density (light microscopy); density of asymmetric synapses and PSD length (electron microscopy)

claims.text: Spine head diameter of total and non-perforated synapses was significantly larger in Shank3-heterozygous rats than in wild-type rats, and total and non-perforated PSD area was significantly larger in Shank3-heterozygous than in Shank3-knockout rats.
claims.eff: not_reported (described as significantly larger; no test statistic, p value or confidence interval in the abstract)
claims.limA: Preliminary evidence; males only; partial isoform disruption.
claims.limO: Effect sizes and dispersion are absent. The heterozygote is the genotype of interest for PMS, which makes this the relevant comparison, but the number of synapses and of animals contributing to it is not stated, so the unit of analysis (synapse or animal) cannot be checked from the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient rat, heterozygous and homozygous knockout; N-terminal loss only
claims.measure: spine head diameter and PSD area at asymmetric synapses, electron microscopy

claims.text: Spine head diameter was significantly larger than wild-type in Shank3-heterozygous rats but not in Shank3-knockout rats, so the ultrastructural effect did not increase with greater loss of Shank3.
claims.limO: The knockout null is reported only as the absence of a significant difference from wild-type. No test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval are given, so a true effect in the knockout of the same size as in the heterozygote cannot be excluded from the abstract; with unstated and probably small group sizes, this is the classic case of a non-significant result being presented beside a significant one as if the two were a contrast. Formally testing genotype by measure interaction would be required to support a dose-dependence statement, and no such test is reported.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient rat; heterozygous versus homozygous knockout versus wild-type
claims.measure: spine head diameter at total and non-perforated asymmetric synapses, electron microscopy

claims.text: Children with Phelan-McDermid syndrome showed significantly smaller transient visual evoked potential amplitudes and decreased beta and gamma band activity relative to typically developing controls and to unaffected siblings of children with PMS.
claims.n: 175 children: 31 PMS, 79 idiopathic ASD, 45 typically developing controls, 20 unaffected siblings of children with PMS
claims.eff: not_reported (significance asserted; no effect size or confidence interval in the abstract)
claims.limO: No effect sizes, no confidence intervals and no correction for the number of group comparisons are reported in the abstract. The sibling group (n = 20) is the specificity control that matters most and is the smallest. A similar response pattern is reported in a subset of children with idiopathic ASD, which bears directly on whether this marker is specific to PMS; the size of that subset is not given.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: transient visual evoked potentials to standard and short-duration contrast-reversing checkerboards; amplitude and beta and gamma band activity

ref.venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry

claims.text: In children with PMS, deletion size was significantly correlated with P60-N75 visual evoked potential amplitude under both stimulus conditions, and test-retest reliability of the measure was strong.
claims.eff: not_reported (correlation coefficients, intraclass correlation values and confidence intervals are not given in the abstract)
claims.limO: A correlation with deletion size in 31 children is reported without the coefficient, its confidence interval or any adjustment for multiple VEP components. Deletion size is itself correlated with overall severity, so this does not establish a SHANK3-dosage mechanism. Reliability is asserted as strong without the numeric intraclass correlation.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: correlation of 22q13 deletion size with P60-N75 VEP amplitude; intraclass correlation between standard and short-duration conditions and test-retest reliability

ref.venue: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry

claims.text: In a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 18 children with PMS, intranasal oxytocin produced no statistically significant improvement over placebo on the primary outcome, the Aberrant Behavior Checklist Social Withdrawal subscale (Mann-Whitney U = 50, p = 0.055), nor on any secondary outcome, in either the double-blind or the open-label phase.
claims.eff: Mann-Whitney U = 50, p = 0.055; no effect size and no confidence interval reported
claims.limA: Small sample size, potential challenges with drug administration, and expectancy bias from reliance on parent-reported outcome measures.
claims.limO: This null does come with a named statistical test and an exact p value, which is better than most records in this block, but it comes with no power calculation and no confidence interval on the treatment difference. With 18 children randomised, roughly nine per arm, the trial could only have detected a very large effect; p = 0.055 on the primary outcome is a non-significant result that is numerically close to the threshold and in the direction of benefit, which is precisely the situation in which absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. The correct reading is that the trial was uninformative about effects of small or moderate size, not that oxytocin was shown to be ineffective. The authors' conclusion that oxytocin is not efficacious is stronger than the design supports.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Aberrant Behavior Checklist Social Withdrawal subscale (primary) and secondary measures of core ASD symptoms

claims.text: Intranasal oxytocin was generally well tolerated in children with PMS over 24 weeks, with no serious adverse events.
claims.limO: A safety null in 18 children with no comparator statistic, no power consideration and no confidence interval. The upper bound of the rate of a serious adverse event that is compatible with zero events in 18 children is roughly one in six; nothing about rare harm can be concluded. Charted as incidental because the absence of adverse events is a monitoring observation, not a tested hypothesis.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: safety monitoring and adverse events over the study period

claims.text: In 91 individuals with PMS, the shortened form of the Social Responsiveness Scale-2 showed superior validity to the full SRS-2 for measuring autism symptoms, with excellent item discrimination on item response theory analysis, while both forms were reliable.
claims.n: 91 individuals with PMS, recruited at six sites
claims.eff: not_reported (no reliability coefficients, discrimination parameters or confidence intervals in the abstract)
claims.limA: Interpretation limited by uncertain content validity and small sample size; items tailored to severe intellectual disability and specifically to PMS still need to be developed.
claims.limO: No null is reported, so no power statement is at issue; the relevant caution is different. This is an instrument-performance study, and its message for trial design is restrictive: an outcome measure whose scores are known to be driven by language ability and intellectual disability is being evaluated in a population defined by both. The claim of superior validity is made without reported numeric comparison in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: psychometric evaluation of the SRS-2 and its shortened form: internal consistency, test-retest reliability, structural, construct and content validity, and item response theory

claims.text: In 21 individuals with PMS assessed with standardised instruments, 45 per cent were non-verbal, receptive and expressive language standard scores were typically more than 3 SD below the mean, and mean language age equivalence was 13 to 16 months.
claims.eff: language age equivalence 13-16 months on average, range 2-53 months; standard scores typically more than 3 SD below the mean
claims.limO: A 21-person cross-sectional sample with a wide deletion range and no comparison group. Floor effects on standardised language instruments in a largely non-verbal population make standard scores hard to interpret, which the abstract does not address.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: standardised speech, language, social and functional communication assessment; adaptive behaviour

claims.text: In PMS, smaller deletion size was significantly associated with the ability to use phrases (odds ratio 0.36, 95 per cent CI 0.14 to 0.95, p = 0.040), and communication scores were markedly lower than daily living (p = 0.008) and socialisation (p < 0.001) scores.
claims.eff: odds ratio 0.36, 95 per cent CI 0.14 to 0.95, p = 0.040; domain comparisons p = 0.008 and p < 0.001
claims.limO: One of the few records in this batch that reports an effect estimate with a confidence interval. The interval is wide and its upper bound is close to 1, so the association is compatible with a very small effect; with 21 participants this is a single underpowered model and no adjustment for covariates such as age is reported.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: logistic association between deletion size and phrase-level speech; within-person comparison of Vineland communication, daily living and socialisation domains

claims.text: Shank3 exon 4-22 knockout mice showed social deficits, a dysregulated gut microbiome and decreased caecal acetate, and oral acetate supplementation reversed the social deficits with accompanying changes in medial prefrontal cortex gene expression even in antibiotic-treated animals.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Reversal of social deficits is asserted without statistics. Sex is not stated, which matters here because the human arm of the same study reports sex-specific correlations.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse carrying deletion of exons 4-22, with wild-type littermates; groups: control, antibiotic, acetate, antibiotic plus acetate
claims.measure: social behaviour; 16S and metagenomic sequencing; metabolomics; mPFC RNA sequencing

claims.text: In targeted serum metabolomic data from people with Phelan-McDermid syndrome, acetate levels showed sex-specific correlations with hyperactivity scores.
claims.n: not_reported (number of PMS participants contributing serum not stated in the abstract)
claims.eff: not_reported (direction of the correlation, coefficients, p values and confidence intervals are all absent from the abstract)
claims.limO: The number of patients is not stated, the direction of the correlation is not stated, and the measure is a peripheral metabolite with many non-neural determinants including diet and gut flora. A sex-specific correlation found in an unstated and probably small sample, reported without correction for the number of clinical scales tested, is a hypothesis, not a marker.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: serum short-chain fatty acid levels, including acetate, against ASD clinical measures including hyperactivity

claims.text: Shank3 delta-11 knockout mice showed altered gain control in primary visual cortex, indicating a deficit of inhibition onto pyramidal neurons, and this alteration was rescued by potentiating GABA-A receptor activity with midazolam.
claims.limA: The mechanism linking Shank3 deletion in parvalbumin neurons to behavioural alterations is not established; effects on other inhibitory neuron classes are unexplored; the pharmacology of ganaxolone needs further characterisation.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. A homozygous knockout is a poor dosage match to PMS haploinsufficiency; the conditional line used for the behavioural work is heterozygous for Shank3 and is charted separately.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-11 homozygous knockout mice (exon 11 deletion) and wild-type controls
claims.measure: local field potentials and visual evoked responses; cortical gain control

claims.text: Conditional deletion of Shank3 restricted to parvalbumin-positive interneurons produced impairments in grooming, memory and motor coordination, and these deficits, together with evocative memory and repetitive behaviour deficits in Shank3 knockout mice, were rescued by ganaxolone.
claims.limA: Mechanism not established; other inhibitory neuron classes not examined; ganaxolone pharmacology needs further characterisation.
claims.limO: Within-animal before-and-after comparison, with no statistics, sample sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. The design compares the same mice before and after administration, which cannot separate drug effect from repeated testing; the abstract does not state whether a vehicle-treated control group was included. This is directly relevant because the Speed and Powell record in this batch shows how a Cre-dependent manipulation can itself produce the apparent rescue.
claims.model: Pv-cre heterozygous, Shank3 floxed/wild-type conditional mice compared with Pv-cre heterozygous Shank3 wild-type/wild-type; plus Shank3 delta-11 knockout mice
claims.measure: grooming, memory, motor coordination and repetitive behaviour before and after ganaxolone

claims.text: Shank3B knockout mice opened their eyes later than wild-type littermates (p < 0.01) and were slower in the negative geotaxis test from postnatal day 13 to 16 (p < 0.001) in both sexes.
claims.eff: p < 0.01 for eye opening; p < 0.001 for negative geotaxis days 13-16; no effect sizes or confidence intervals reported
claims.limO: p values without effect sizes or confidence intervals, and no litter-level analysis is mentioned, which matters in developmental mouse work where the litter, not the pup, is the independent unit. Homozygous knockout, so a poor dosage match to PMS haploinsufficiency.
claims.model: B6.129-Shank3tm2Gfng/J (Shank3B-/-) homozygous knockout mice and wild-type littermates
claims.measure: battery of early neurodevelopmental milestones and reflexes, including eye opening and negative geotaxis

claims.text: No differences between Shank3B knockout and wild-type mice were observed in upper and lower incisor eruption, ear unfolding, air righting, surface righting or the ear twitch reflex.
claims.limO: These nulls come with no statistical test reported, no power calculation and no confidence interval; the phrase used is no observed differences, which is an observation statement rather than a test result. They are part of a milestone battery in which a handful of measures reached significance, so they are best read as the non-significant remainder of a multiple-comparison battery rather than as established equivalence. Several of the measures are also coarse binary milestones with little resolution. No conclusion of normality on these reflexes is supportable.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mice and wild-type littermates
claims.measure: incisor eruption, ear unfolding, air righting, surface righting, ear twitch reflex

claims.text: No effect of sex was observable in any of the neurodevelopmental tests applied to Shank3B knockout mice.
claims.limO: No test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval are reported for the sex comparison. Sex-by-genotype interactions require substantially larger samples than main effects, and with unstated group sizes this null carries essentially no information; it should not be cited as evidence that the phenotype is sex-independent. It is charted because the comparison was made at all, which is unusual in this literature.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mice and wild-type littermates, both sexes
claims.measure: sex as a factor across the neurodevelopmental test battery

claims.text: In a Brazilian cohort of individuals with PMS, 21 per cent (6 of 29) carried an additional rare copy number variant besides the 22q13.3 deletion, and increased pain tolerance (80 per cent), hypotonia (85 per cent) and sparse eyebrows (80 per cent) were prominent clinical features.
claims.n: 34 individuals with PMS clinically and genetically evaluated; 29 analysed for additional CNVs
claims.eff: proportions as stated; no confidence intervals reported
claims.limO: Phenotype data come from a parent-completed questionnaire and photographs rather than direct examination, which is a serious limitation for features such as pain tolerance. Proportions are given without confidence intervals; with 34 participants, an 80 per cent figure has an interval of roughly 60 to 90 per cent.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: clinical questionnaire completed by parents, photographic dysmorphology assessment, CNV analysis

claims.text: Renal abnormalities, lymphedema and language impairment were positively associated with 22q13.3 deletion size, and an 18-year-old individual carrying a SHANK3 deletion had an IQ within the normal range.
claims.eff: not_reported (associations asserted without coefficients, p values or confidence intervals)
claims.limO: Deletion-size associations in 34 individuals, with no statistics reported in the abstract and no adjustment for the number of traits tested. The proposed minimum deletion sizes for lymphedema and renal problems rest on this single small cohort and should be treated as a hypothesis. The atypical case is a single observation; nothing about resilience mechanisms follows from it.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: association of deletion size with comorbidities, speech status and ASD; single-case cognitive assessment

claims.text: Children with syndromic autism due to Phelan-McDermid syndrome, Rett syndrome or SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability had worse caregiver-reported health-related quality of life than children with other chronic disorders including idiopathic autism, with physical functioning the most severely affected dimension.
claims.n: not_reported (number of families per syndrome not stated in the abstract)
claims.limO: Sample sizes are absent, the three syndromes are reported together rather than separately, and comparisons with other chronic disorders appear to be against published reference data rather than a concurrently recruited group. Caregiver-reported quality of life in profoundly disabled children is known to be influenced by caregiver burden, which the abstract does not address.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: PedsQL health-related quality of life, caregiver report

ref.venue: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders

claims.text: Binding of active Ras or Rap1a to the SPN domain differentially regulates the localisation of Shank3 in dendrites, and the linker between the SPN and ankyrin repeat domains of Shank1 and Shank3 binds inactive alpha-CaMKII, through which both proteins exert a negative effect on alpha-CaMKII activity at postsynaptic sites in mice in vivo.
claims.limO: No quantitative parameters: no binding affinities, no sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. The patient relevance is inferential; the variants studied are described as altering the SPN and ankyrin domains but the abstract does not say that specific patient variants were tested in the functional assays.
claims.model: mouse in vivo plus primary cultured neurons expressing full-length Shank3 and SPN-Ank variants
claims.measure: Shank3 localisation in dendrites, alpha-CaMKII binding and activity, clustering on spine heads versus dendritic shafts

claims.text: A closed conformation of the SPN-ankyrin tandem is required for proper clustering of Shank3 on dendritic spine heads, and Shank3 variants whose ankyrin repeats are not associated with the SPN domain form postsynaptic clusters on dendritic shafts at the expense of spine-like protrusions.
claims.limO: Overexpression of constructs in cultured neurons, with no sample sizes, statistics or confidence intervals in the abstract. species is recorded as other because the abstract says primary cultured neurons without naming the species.
claims.model: primary cultured neurons (rodent; species not specified in the abstract) expressing full-length Shank3 with intact or disrupted SPN-Ank conformation
claims.measure: subcellular localisation and clustering of Shank3 constructs

claims.text: Across more than 542 hours of audio from 18 children with PMS, the automated Language ENvironment Analysis system performed adequately only in a subset of children, specifically younger children and those with fewer stereotypic vocalizations.
claims.n: 18 children with PMS; more than 542 hours of audio
claims.eff: not_reported (no agreement coefficients, error rates or confidence intervals in the abstract)
claims.limO: The failure of the instrument is reported qualitatively: no agreement statistic, no confidence interval and no prespecified adequacy threshold are given, and the subset in which performance was adequate is not quantified. The subgroup pattern (younger children, fewer stereotypies) is reported without a test of the interaction and in 18 children, so it is a post hoc observation. As a negative this is informative in direction but not in magnitude.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: agreement of automated LENA language measures with human coding

ref.venue: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders

claims.text: One LENA-derived measure, the Vocalization Ratio, showed improved accuracy in children with PMS and is proposed as a candidate expressive language measure for severely affected populations.
claims.limO: Improved accuracy is asserted without a number, a comparator threshold or a confidence interval, and the measure was selected after examining the data in the same 18 children, so it is a post hoc selection that has not been validated in an independent sample.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Vocalization Ratio derived from LENA recordings, against human-coded reference

ref.venue: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
