claims.text: In 34 children with a 22q13.3 deletion including SHANK3, maximal developmental functioning ranged from 34 to 52 months depending on domain, language was the weakest domain, and developmental quotients decreased with age across all domains, with 38 per cent showing no improvement in cognitive developmental functioning.
claims.eff: maximal developmental functioning 34-52 months by domain; 38 per cent with no improvement in cognitive functioning; no confidence intervals reported
claims.limO: Developmental quotients falling with age in a cross-sectional-plus-longitudinal design can reflect widening distance from norms rather than regression, and the abstract does not separate the two. No confidence intervals. A plateau expressed as a ceiling age equivalent is useful clinically but is not an interval-scaled outcome that could serve as a trial endpoint.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development third edition, WPPSI third edition, Vineland Screener for Social and Adaptive Behavior

claims.text: Children with very small 22q13.3 deletions covering only SHANK3, ACR and RABL2B had a more favourable developmental phenotype than children with larger deletions.
claims.n: subset of 34 children; number with minimal deletions not stated in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported (no statistics, group sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract)
claims.limO: The number of children in the minimal-deletion group is not given and is probably very small. No statistical comparison is reported. The claim is directly relevant to whether SHANK3 restoration could normalise the phenotype, and that makes the absence of group sizes and intervals a material gap rather than a presentational one.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: standardised developmental assessment compared across deletion size categories

claims.text: Loss of JIP2 (MAPK8IP2) in human pluripotent stem cell-derived neural progenitors contributes to a distinct neurodevelopmental phenotype affecting neuronal maturation, most likely through simultaneous down-regulation of JNK proteins leading to impaired generation of mature neurons.
claims.n: not_reported (number of patient lines not stated in the abstract)
claims.limO: The number of patient and control lines is not stated, which is the single most important parameter in iPSC work because line-to-line variability routinely exceeds genotype effects. No statistics, no confidence intervals. The causal attribution to JIP2 rests on genome editing, which is the right design, but the abstract does not say how many edited clones were examined.
claims.model: human pluripotent stem cell-derived neural progenitor cells and cortical neurons from patients with 22q13.3 deletion, plus genome-edited isogenic lines
claims.measure: neuronal maturation, JNK protein expression

claims.text: Semaphorin signalling was impaired in neural progenitors and neurons derived from patients with 22q13.3 deletion, and pharmacological activation of neuropilin receptor 1 rescued semaphorin pathway activity and JNK expression in patient neurons.
claims.limO: Rescue is reported in a cellular assay with no sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals; the compound is not named in the abstract. A rescue of a molecular readout in vitro is several steps away from a phenotypic rescue, and the abstract does not report that neuronal maturation itself was restored.
claims.model: patient-derived neural progenitors and cortical neurons carrying 22q13.3 deletions
claims.measure: semaphorin pathway activity and JNK expression in patient neurons

claims.text: A mouse model in which all Shank3 isoforms are disrupted showed more severe phenotypes than previously published Shank3 models, including sensory alterations in neonates and adults, strongly altered motor behaviour, increased grooming, increased novelty-induced anxiety, and deficits in Barnes maze learning and reversal and in contextual fear testing.
claims.limO: A very large battery reported without sample sizes, effect sizes, confidence intervals or any statement about correction for multiple comparisons. The comparison with previously published models is informal, across laboratories, backgrounds and protocols, so more severely affected is an impression rather than a measured contrast.
claims.model: mouse with disruption of all Shank3 isoforms; homozygous and heterozygous animals compared with wild-type
claims.measure: broad behavioural battery: general health, neurological reflexes, motor, sensory reactivity, social behaviour, repetitive behaviour, cognition, behavioural inflexibility, anxiety

claims.text: In a mouse model with all Shank3 isoforms disrupted, social behaviours measured with the three-chambered social approach and male-female interaction tests were not strongly impacted, and working memory in the Y-maze spontaneous alternation test was not altered.
claims.limO: The null is stated qualitatively, as not strongly impacted and not altered, with no test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval. Not strongly impacted is not a statistical statement at all and could describe a small significant effect as easily as no effect. Group sizes are unstated. This null cannot be used as evidence that Shank3 loss spares sociability; what it establishes is only that this battery in this laboratory did not produce a marked social deficit.
claims.model: mouse with complete disruption of all Shank3 isoforms, homozygous and heterozygous
claims.measure: three-chambered social approach, male-female interaction, Y-maze spontaneous alternation

claims.text: Heterozygous mice carrying the complete Shank3 deletion showed an intermediate phenotype in many behavioural paradigms, with deficits typically more pronounced in homozygotes.
claims.limO: Intermediate and typically more pronounced are qualitative descriptions with no test of a dose trend, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals. The number of paradigms in which the heterozygote differed from wild-type is not given, so the proportion of the phenotype that is dosage-sensitive cannot be estimated from the abstract.
claims.model: complete Shank3 deletion mouse, heterozygous versus homozygous versus wild-type
claims.measure: behavioural battery compared across genotypes

claims.text: Across 65 genes of the 22q13 region analysed in post-mortem brain RNA sequencing from developmentally normal subjects, most were expressed in brain, ATXN10, MLC1, MAPK8IP2 and SULT4A1 had the highest overall expression, and highly expressed genes tended to peak in the early post-natal period and fall later in development.
claims.n: not_reported (number of post-mortem donors not stated in the abstract)
claims.eff: not_reported (no expression values, dispersion or confidence intervals in the abstract)
claims.limO: A reanalysis of an existing post-mortem transcriptomic resource with the number of donors per stage unstated; post-mortem RNA studies are sensitive to interval and tissue quality, which the abstract does not address. Expression level is not function, and nothing here is measured in PMS tissue.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: RNA sequencing expression of 65 genes on 22q13 across developmental stages and brain regions

claims.text: Spatial analysis showed region-specific differences in the expression of SHANK3, MAPK8IP2 and SULT4A1 in normal human brain development, with a consistently distinct expression profile in cerebellum, and exon-specific analysis showed higher expression of SHANK3 exons contributing to known brain-specific functional isoforms.
claims.eff: not_reported (significance asserted for region-specific differences without statistics or confidence intervals)
claims.limO: Exon-level quantification from bulk short-read RNA sequencing is a weak basis for isoform claims, and the abstract gives neither the method nor any uncertainty estimate. Significance is asserted without values and without stating any correction across 65 genes and multiple regions.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: region-specific and exon-specific expression from RNA sequencing

claims.text: Juvenile male Shank3-deficient null rats did not show the enhanced social approach behaviour typically exhibited after playback of pro-social ultrasonic vocalizations, and showed fewer and shorter bouts of reciprocal social play with reduced anogenital sniffing and allogrooming, while male null pups emitted fewer isolation-induced ultrasonic vocalizations than wild-type controls.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. Males only. The absence of the normal approach response is itself a null within a positive narrative, and no statistic is attached to it.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient rat, null males; wild-type controls
claims.measure: social approach to playback, reciprocal play parameters, isolation-induced ultrasonic vocalizations, post-mortem whole-brain anatomical phenotyping

claims.text: Emission of ultrasonic vocalizations in response to playback was not dependent on Shank3 genotype, although the response calls emitted differed in content, dissociating the receptive and expressive sides of the communication assay.
claims.limO: The null is reported without a test statistic, without a power calculation and without a confidence interval, and with unstated group sizes. Ultrasonic vocalization counts are highly variable between animals, so a null on emission rate in a small group is weak. The accompanying statement that response calls were divergent in meaning is an interpretive claim about call categories that the abstract does not quantify. Presented here as no genotype difference detected in emission rate, not as equivalence.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient rat, null males and wild-type controls
claims.measure: rate of ultrasonic vocalization emission in response to playback, by genotype

claims.text: Mice carrying a single guanine insertion in Shank3 exon 21, reproducing an autism-associated human mutation, lost the major higher molecular weight Shank3 isoforms at the synapse and showed deficits in hippocampus-dependent spatial learning, impaired motor coordination, altered response to novelty and sensory processing deficits.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. Phenotypes are reported in homozygotes, whereas the corresponding patients and PMS are heterozygous. Sex is not stated.
claims.model: Shank3(G) mouse, single guanine insertion in exon 21 causing a frameshift and premature stop; homozygous Shank3(G/G)
claims.measure: spatial learning, motor coordination, novelty response, sensory processing; Shank3 isoform levels at the synapse

claims.text: Shank3 exon 21 insertion mutant mice showed impaired hippocampal excitatory transmission and plasticity and changes in baseline NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic responses.
claims.limO: No cell or animal numbers, no effect sizes, no confidence intervals in the abstract. The same group later showed, in a companion study charted in this batch, that apparent rescue in this very line can be produced by the Cre and tamoxifen system rather than by Shank3 restoration, which is a caution about the interpretability of downstream manipulations in this model, not about this baseline result.
claims.model: Shank3(G/G) mice, exon 21 insertion
claims.measure: excitatory synaptic transmission, synaptic plasticity, NMDA receptor-mediated responses

claims.text: In 30 individuals with PMS compared with matched samples with fragile X syndrome, Down syndrome and idiopathic autism, there were no differences in impulsivity or overactivity, contrary to the previously reported profile of atypically high activity and impulsivity in PMS.
claims.n: 30 individuals with PMS (mean age 10.55, SD 7.08), compared with matched samples with fragile X syndrome, Down syndrome and idiopathic ASD
claims.eff: not_reported (no test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract)
claims.limO: This non-replication arrives with no statistical test reported, no power calculation and no confidence interval, in 30 individuals against matched comparison groups of unstated size. That is a serious weakness for a claim of this kind: with 30 participants, a moderate elevation in impulsivity would frequently fail to reach significance, so the result is compatible both with the previous reports being wrong and with this study being too small to detect what they described. It should be recorded as a failure to reproduce, not as a refutation. The measures are carer questionnaires, and the earlier reports being contradicted used different instruments, so instrument differences are an alternative explanation that the abstract does not exclude.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: carer-completed questionnaires on impulsivity, overactivity, mood, interest and pleasure, repetitive behaviour and ASD phenomenology

claims.text: Compulsive and routine-driven repetitive behaviours were less common in the total PMS sample than in the comparison groups, while motor-based stereotyped behaviours were more common.
claims.n: 30 individuals with PMS and matched comparison samples
claims.limO: No statistics, power or confidence intervals are reported for either the lower or the higher comparison. Repetitive-behaviour subtype scores are strongly confounded by developmental level, and PMS involves more severe intellectual disability than Down syndrome in particular; without adjustment, a lower rate of compulsive and routine-driven behaviour may reflect the cognitive prerequisites of those behaviours rather than a syndrome-specific profile. The abstract does not state whether any such adjustment was made.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: carer-reported repetitive behaviour subtypes

claims.text: Of 30 individuals with PMS, 87 per cent met the cut-off for autism spectrum disorder and 57 per cent the cut-off for autism on a screening measure; the ASD profile of the whole PMS sample differed from idiopathic ASD in communication, social interaction and repetitive behaviour, whereas the profile of the subgroup meeting the autism threshold was comparable to idiopathic ASD.
claims.n: 30 individuals with PMS; 17 of 30 meeting the autism threshold (57 per cent)
claims.eff: proportions as stated; no confidence intervals or test statistics reported
claims.limO: Proportions from a screening instrument rather than diagnostic assessment, without confidence intervals; in 30 people, 87 per cent carries an interval of roughly 70 to 95 per cent. The second analysis is performed on a subgroup of about 17 people selected on the outcome measure itself, which inflates the similarity to idiopathic ASD by construction.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: ASD screening instrument cut-offs and domain profiles, compared with idiopathic ASD

claims.text: Auditory cortex responses to speech and non-speech sounds were weaker in Shank3 heterozygous rats than in wild-type rats, with less spontaneous auditory cortex firing and an inability to respond well to rapid trains of noise bursts.
claims.limO: No numbers of animals or recording sites, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Anaesthetic state during recording is not stated, and it strongly affects cortical responsiveness. The authors state the prediction in advance, which is unusual and worth noting, but the study is not preregistered.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient rat, heterozygous, with wild-type controls
claims.measure: multi-unit auditory cortex responses to speech and non-speech sounds; spontaneous firing rate; responses to rapid noise burst trains

claims.text: In 85 patients with 22q13 rearrangements (78 deletions and 7 duplications), corpus callosum abnormalities were present in 28 per cent of the 35 with brain imaging data, and a second locus at 22q13 was associated with absence of speech, separate from SHANK3.
claims.eff: 28 per cent of 35 with corpus callosum abnormalities; no confidence intervals or association statistics reported
claims.limO: Imaging was available in only 35 of 85 patients and the selection of who was imaged is not described, which is a likely ascertainment bias towards more severely affected children. Region-mapping against clinical features in 85 patients involves many implicit comparisons with no stated correction, and no interval is given for the 28 per cent.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: clinical features, brain imaging, mapping of candidate genomic regions at 22q13 against clinical features

claims.text: An inherited SHANK3 deletion was transmitted to five affected daughters by a mother who had neither intellectual disability nor autism spectrum disorder, and additional clinically relevant copy number variants at ASD loci including 16p11.2 and 15q11q13 were found in some patients.
claims.n: 1 family (mother and 5 daughters) within a cohort of 85
claims.eff: not_applicable - a family observation, not an estimate
claims.limO: A single family. The mother is described as having neither intellectual disability nor ASD, but the depth of her assessment is not stated in the abstract, and mosaicism is not excluded. No statistical claim is attached and none should be: this is an observation of apparently incomplete penetrance, not a tested null, which is why it is not coded as a negative finding.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: segregation of a SHANK3 deletion against clinical status; detection of additional copy number variants

claims.text: In IB2 knockout mice, modelling deletion of the IB2 gene at the 22q13.3 terminal region, cerebellar granule cells showed larger NMDA receptor-mediated current and enhanced intrinsic excitability, the granular layer response to mossy fibre input shifted towards stronger core excitation with weaker surround inhibition, and long-term synaptic plasticity was increased in size and extent.
claims.limO: No cell numbers, animal numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. The claim that IB2 deletion occurs in virtually all cases of PMS is asserted in the background and not evidenced in this study. Homozygous knockout of a gene that is hemizygous in patients.
claims.model: IB2 (Islet Brain-2, MAPK8IP2) knockout mice, either sex
claims.measure: NMDA receptor-mediated currents, intrinsic excitability, spatial organisation of granular layer responses to mossy fibre stimulation, long-term synaptic plasticity

claims.text: Tamoxifen-induced reversion of the Shank3 exon 21 insertion mutation to wild-type in adult mice completely restored SHANK3 protein expression in the brain and appeared to rescue synaptic transmission and some behavioural differences relative to Cre-positive wild-type controls.
claims.limO: The rescue of protein expression is a direct molecular readout and is credible; the apparent rescue of synaptic transmission and behaviour is the part the same paper then shows to be confounded, and it is charted here only so that the confound record has something to attach to. No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3(G) exon 21 insertion mice carrying a tamoxifen-inducible Cre/loxP system (CreTam) allowing reversion to wild-type in adulthood
claims.measure: SHANK3 protein expression in brain; synaptic transmission; behavioural measures

claims.text: Comparisons between vehicle-treated wild-type Cre-negative and Cre-positive mice showed clear effects of the tamoxifen-inducible Cre system itself on baseline synaptic transmission and on some behaviours, making the apparently positive genetic reversal effects difficult to interpret.
claims.limO: Here the usual asymmetry runs the other way: the finding is a detected difference in controls, not a null, so the absence of a power calculation does not weaken it. What is missing is the magnitude: clear effects are asserted without effect sizes, test statistics or confidence intervals, and without stating which behaviours were affected. The result is also a single-laboratory, single-Cre-line observation, so how far it generalises to other inducible Cre lines is unknown.
claims.model: wild-type mice differing only in the presence of the tamoxifen-inducible Cre transgene (Shank3 wild-type CreTam-negative versus CreTam-positive)
claims.measure: baseline synaptic transmission and behavioural measures in genotype-matched wild-type controls

claims.text: Interpretation of adult Shank3 genetic reversal experiments requires comparison against Cre-positive wild-type controls, because the inducible Cre system alone alters the outcome measures used to judge rescue.
claims.eff: not_applicable - a methodological conclusion, not an estimate
claims.limO: A single-laboratory conclusion drawn from one Cre line and one Shank3 allele, with no quantitative statement of how large the Cre effect was relative to the apparent rescue. The recommendation is sound on design grounds independently of the numbers, but the abstract does not allow the reader to judge how much of the published adult-reversal literature would be affected.
claims.model: Shank3(G) reversible mice with tamoxifen-inducible Cre, with the full set of Cre-positive and Cre-negative wild-type comparison groups
claims.measure: synaptic transmission and behaviour, compared across the full control matrix

claims.text: Intranasal administration of exosomes derived from mesenchymal stem cells to Shank3B knockout mice improved social behaviour deficits across multiple paradigms, increased vocalization and reduced repetitive behaviour, with an increase in GABARB1 in prefrontal cortex.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals. A broad behavioural improvement claimed across multiple paradigms with no statement of correction for multiple testing. The dose is given as a concentration without a volume, so the delivered dose cannot be reconstructed. Cell-therapy and exosome studies in neurodevelopmental models have a weak replication record, and no independent replication is cited.
claims.model: Shank3B knockout mice with saline-treated controls and wild-type littermates
claims.measure: social behaviour paradigms, vocalization, repetitive behaviour, GABARB1 expression

claims.text: Hair samples from individuals with Phelan-McDermid syndrome carrying a 22q13.3 deletion including SHANK3 showed a high rate of abnormally low zinc to copper ratios.
claims.n: not_reported (number of hair samples not stated in the abstract)
claims.eff: not_reported (a high rate is asserted without a proportion, a reference range or a confidence interval)
claims.limO: Neither the number of patients nor the number of controls is given, nor the threshold defining an abnormal ratio. Hair trace-element analysis is strongly influenced by diet, supplements, hair treatment and external contamination, and its reliability as a measure of systemic zinc status is contested; the abstract does not address this. Feeding difficulties and restricted diets are common in PMS, which is an obvious alternative explanation for low zinc that the abstract does not exclude.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: zinc and copper concentration in hair by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry; zinc to copper ratio

claims.text: Enterocytes derived from PMS patient induced pluripotent stem cells and Caco-2 cells with SHANK3 knockdown showed decreased mRNA and protein expression of the zinc uptake transporters ZIP2 and ZIP4 correlating with SHANK3 expression level, with ZIP4 forming a complex with SHANK3 at the plasma membrane and the link confirmed in gut sections from Shank3 alpha-beta knockout mice.
claims.n: not_reported (number of patient lines and animals not stated in the abstract)
claims.limO: Line numbers, replicate numbers, statistics and confidence intervals are all absent from the abstract. Three model systems agreeing is a genuine strength; none of the three measures zinc absorption in a patient, so the clinical inference remains indirect. The proposed therapeutic consequence, that zinc supplementation would help, does not follow from reduced uptake transporter expression, and may be contradicted by it.
claims.model: PMS patient-derived iPSC enterocytes; Caco-2 cells with SHANK3 knockdown; Shank3 alpha-beta knockout mouse gut sections
claims.measure: ZIP2 and ZIP4 mRNA and protein levels, co-localisation and co-immunoprecipitation with SHANK3

claims.text: Shank3 is required to recruit Homer1b/c to the postsynaptic density and thereby to mediate mGlu5 receptor signalling, specifically in striatum and cortex, and augmenting mGlu5 receptor activity with 3-cyano-N-(1,3-diphenyl-1H-pyrazol-5-yl)benzamide ameliorated the functional and behavioural defects of Shank3 delta-11 knockout mice.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals. Rescue is claimed in homozygous knockouts, which is not the PMS dosage. Which behavioural defects were ameliorated, and which were not, is not stated, so the completeness of the rescue cannot be judged from the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-11 homozygous knockout mice (exon 11 deletion)
claims.measure: Homer1b/c recruitment to the postsynaptic density, mGlu5 signalling, functional and behavioural deficits

claims.text: Acute tandospirone at 0.01 and 0.06 mg/kg attenuated a spatial acquisition deficit and reduced elevated self-grooming in male Shank3B heterozygous mice, repeated treatment at 0.06 mg/kg sustained the reduction in grooming, and infusion into the anterior cingulate and premotor area reproduced the effect.
claims.limO: Doses are reported, which is better than most intervention records here, but sample sizes, effect sizes and confidence intervals are not. Only two doses were tested and no dose-response relationship is described. The interpretation that the drug worked by improving sensitivity to positive reinforcement is a secondary inference from the same behavioural data.
claims.model: Shank3B heterozygous (Shank3B+/-) mice, males
claims.measure: spatial acquisition, sensitivity to positive reinforcement, self-grooming

claims.text: Only male Shank3B heterozygous mice showed a spatial learning deficit and elevated self-grooming; the corresponding deficits were not detected in females.
claims.limO: The female null is implied by the word only rather than stated as a result, and it comes with no test statistic, no power calculation, no confidence interval and no sex-by-genotype interaction test. Detecting that an effect is significant in one sex and not in the other is not the same as showing the sexes differ, and with unstated group sizes nothing can be concluded about female Shank3B heterozygotes. It should not be cited as evidence that females are spared.
claims.model: Shank3B+/- mice, males and females
claims.measure: spatial learning and self-grooming, by sex

claims.text: SULT4A1 modulates neuronal branching complexity and dendritic spine formation and, by negatively regulating the catalytic activity of Pin1 towards PSD-95, facilitates NMDA receptor synaptic expression and function; pharmacological inhibition of Pin1 restored spine density and NMDA receptor-mediated transmission in SULT4A1 knockdown neurons.
claims.limO: Knockdown rather than deletion, in culture, with no replicate numbers, statistics or confidence intervals in the abstract, and the species of the cultured neurons is not stated. The relevance to PMS is positional: SULT4A1 is in the deleted region, but no PMS material is examined.
claims.model: primary neurons with SULT4A1 knockdown; species not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: neuronal branching, dendritic spine density, NMDA receptor synaptic expression and NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission

claims.text: Across three independent cohorts of Shank3 ankyrin-domain mutant mice, repetitive self-grooming, reduced ultrasonic vocalizations and deficits in reversal of water maze learning were detected in some cohorts but not others.
claims.n: three independent cohorts; number of animals per cohort not reported in the abstract
claims.limO: The failures to reproduce are reported qualitatively, without per-cohort statistics, without cohort sizes, without power calculations and without confidence intervals. That matters in both directions: an endophenotype appearing in one cohort and not another is exactly what underpowered behavioural testing produces by chance, so these data do not establish that the phenotypes are absent, only that they are not robust to cohort. The honest reading is that the effects, if real, are smaller than the study could reliably detect.
claims.model: Shank3 mice with null and heterozygous mutations in the ankyrin repeat domain, evaluated in three independent cohorts
claims.measure: self-grooming, ultrasonic vocalizations, Morris water maze reversal learning, repeated across cohorts

claims.text: All genotypes of Shank3 ankyrin-domain mutant mice displayed normal adult sociability on the three-chambered task, with mild social impairment detected primarily in juveniles during reciprocal interactions.
claims.limO: The null is reported as normal adult sociability without a test statistic, a power calculation or a confidence interval, and without group sizes. The three-chambered task has a well-known ceiling, and a mouse can pass it while being socially abnormal on finer measures, as this study itself shows in juveniles. The record establishes that no adult sociability deficit was detected on this task in this line, and nothing stronger.
claims.model: Shank3 ankyrin repeat domain null and heterozygous mice with wild-type controls
claims.measure: three-chambered social approach task in adults; reciprocal social interaction in juveniles

claims.text: Both homozygous and heterozygous Shank3 ankyrin-domain mutant mice showed reduced glutamatergic transmission and reduced long-term potentiation in hippocampus, with more severe deficits in homozygotes, and null mutants consistently showed impaired novel object recognition and rotarod performance across cohorts.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals. The important structural point is the contrast within this one study: the synaptic phenotypes and two of the behavioural measures held across cohorts while the social and repetitive measures did not, which suggests the electrophysiological end of the chain is the more robust one, though the abstract provides no quantitative basis for that comparison.
claims.model: Shank3 ankyrin repeat domain mutant mice, homozygous and heterozygous
claims.measure: glutamatergic synaptic transmission and long-term potentiation; novel object recognition; rotarod

claims.text: Six weeks of dietary zinc supplementation in Shank3 exon 13-16 knockout mice prevented ASD-related repetitive and anxiety behaviours and deficits in social novelty recognition.
claims.limO: The zinc dose is not stated, which makes the result impossible to translate and impossible to replicate from the abstract. No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals. Prevention in homozygous knockout mice on a supplemented diet from an unstated age is a long way from a supplementation recommendation in children, and the record should not be cited in support of one.
claims.model: Shank3 exon 13-16 homozygous knockout mice (Shank3 ex13-16 -/-)
claims.measure: repetitive and anxiety behaviours; social novelty recognition

claims.text: Dietary zinc supplementation in Shank3 exon 13-16 knockout mice increased synaptic recruitment of SHANK2, reduced NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission, reversed the slowed decay time constant of NMDA receptor currents, and occluded long-term potentiation at cortico-striatal synapses.
claims.limO: No cell or animal numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals. The behavioural benefit is accompanied by reduced NMDA receptor transmission and occluded LTP, which are not obviously desirable changes; the abstract treats them as mechanism rather than as a possible cost, and the full text would be needed to judge.
claims.model: Shank3 ex13-16 -/- mice, cortico-striatal slice electrophysiology
claims.measure: SHANK2 synaptic recruitment, NMDA receptor-mediated transmission, NMDA receptor current decay tau, long-term potentiation

claims.text: Mice with Shank3 gene deletions exhibited self-injurious repetitive grooming and deficits in social interaction, with cellular, electrophysiological and biochemical defects at striatal synapses and in cortico-striatal circuits.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. This is the most-cited behavioural result in the Shank3 field and the foundation of the cortico-striatal account of the phenotype; two records in this batch, from the Crawley group in a different allele, report that the social and grooming phenotypes were not consistently reproducible in their hands. Those are different alleles, so the comparison is not a direct replication test, but any reader of this record should see the other two.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant mice (Shank3B line, exons 13-16 encoding the PDZ domain)
claims.measure: self-grooming, social interaction, striatal synaptic function, biochemistry of the postsynaptic density

claims.text: In Drosophila, which has a single Prosap/Shank family homolog, both loss and overexpression of Shank caused defects in synaptic bouton number and maturation at the glutamatergic neuromuscular junction, and Shank acted by modulating internalisation of the Wnt receptor Fz2 in the postsynaptic cell.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, statistics or confidence intervals in the abstract. The fly gene is the ancestral family member and is not SHANK3; the neuromuscular junction is not a central synapse. The finding that both loss and overexpression are deleterious is the part most worth carrying forward, and it is reported qualitatively, as a dose-dependent manner, with no dose-response data given.
claims.model: Drosophila single Prosap/Shank family homolog; loss-of-function and overexpression
claims.measure: synaptic bouton number and maturation; Fz2 receptor internalisation; Wnt signalling

claims.text: In 40 children with PMS assessed by standardised parental interview, the majority showed persistent deficits in social communication but only half met diagnostic criteria in the restricted and repetitive behaviour domain, and general developmental delay contributed significantly to the ASD diagnosis.
claims.n: 40 parents or guardians of children with PMS interviewed; subset for genotype analysis not quantified
claims.eff: not_reported (no odds ratios, p values or confidence intervals in the abstract)
claims.limO: The negative half of this claim - that only about half met criteria in the repetitive behaviour domain - comes with no confidence interval; in 40 children, a proportion of one half has an interval of roughly 34 to 66 per cent. The regression showing that developmental delay contributes to the ASD diagnosis is reported without coefficients or intervals. Diagnosis rests on parental interview rather than direct observation. Separating autism from severe global delay is the hardest measurement problem in this population and the abstract does not say how it was addressed beyond the regression.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: standardised interview on DSM ASD criteria by domain; logistic regression of ASD diagnosis on developmental delay

claims.text: Analysis relating PMS genotype to behavioural phenotype indicated contributions to the ASD phenotype and other neurobehavioural impairments from genes in both the deleted and the preserved SHANK3 regions.
claims.n: a small subset of the 40-child sample; size not stated in the abstract
claims.limO: The authors describe this analysis as preliminary and conducted in a small subset whose size is not stated. Genotype-phenotype mapping across a contiguous deletion with a handful of patients cannot separate the contributions of neighbouring genes; no statistics or intervals are reported. Treat as hypothesis-generating.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: relationship between extent of disruption of SHANK3 and adjacent genes and specific ASD symptoms

claims.text: Shank3-deficient rats carrying a genetic alteration similar to a human SHANK3 mutation showed impaired long-term social recognition memory and attention and reduced synaptic plasticity in the hippocampal to medial prefrontal cortex pathway, and these deficits were attenuated by oxytocin treatment.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals. Attenuated is not quantified, and whether the attenuation was partial or complete cannot be judged from the abstract. The record is charted chiefly as the preclinical half of a preclinical-to-clinical pair whose clinical half did not succeed; it should always be read with the trial record.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient rat with a genetic alteration similar to a human SHANK3 mutation
claims.measure: long-term social recognition memory, attention, synaptic plasticity in the hippocampal-mPFC pathway

claims.text: Shank3 haplotype-truncated mice showed reduced minimum alveolar concentration and reduced RREC50 for isoflurane, together with down-regulation of NR1 in vestibular nuclei and of PSD95 in spinal cord, indicating increased anaesthetic sensitivity.
claims.eff: not_reported (no MAC values, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract)
claims.limO: A mouse pharmacodynamic result with no numbers given, no sample sizes and no confidence intervals. The authors themselves say it would need confirmation in a clinical study. It should not be used to guide anaesthetic management in people with PMS, and the record is charted so that the Committee can see what the evidence behind a clinically circulating claim actually is.
claims.model: Shank3 +/delta-C mice, heterozygous C-terminal truncation
claims.measure: minimum alveolar concentration and RREC50 of isoflurane; NR1 and PSD95 expression

claims.text: The S-nitroso-proteome of cortex and striatum differed between InsG3680 Shank3 mutant mice and wild-type at both young and adult ages, with S-nitrosylated calcineurin associated with increased phosphorylation of Synapsin1 and CREB, raised 3-nitrotyrosine in adult mutant cortex and higher S-nitrosoglutathione concentrations in mutants.
claims.limO: A discovery proteomics study with no sample sizes, no false discovery rate, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals reported in the abstract. Pathway enrichment described as showing processes affected in ASD is a post hoc annotation of a discovery list. The allele is homozygous for a mutation that patients carry heterozygously.
claims.model: InsG3680 (+/+) mice, a human mutation-based Shank3 model
claims.measure: SNOTRAP mass spectrometry identification of S-nitrosylated proteins; phosphorylation of Synapsin1 and CREB; 3-nitrotyrosine; S-nitrosoglutathione concentration

claims.text: Neuronal nitric oxide synthase showed no significant difference in level or neuronal localisation between InsG3680 Shank3 mutant and wild-type mice.
claims.limO: A single mechanistic control comparison reported as no significant difference with no test named, no power calculation and no confidence interval, and with no group sizes. Western blot and immunohistochemical comparisons in small groups of mice have very low power to exclude moderate differences, so this null does not establish that nNOS is unchanged; it establishes only that a change was not detected. Charted as incidental because it is a control check within a discovery study, not a hypothesis of its own.
claims.model: InsG3680 (+/+) Shank3 mutant mice and wild-type controls
claims.measure: neuronal nitric oxide synthase protein level and localisation in neurons

claims.text: Shank1-Shank3 double knockout mice show a strong developmental reduction in the activation of Akt, S6, ERK1/2 and eEF2 intracellular signalling pathways.
claims.limA: The authors present Akt function as a possible therapeutic target rather than an established one.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or p values in the abstract. A double knockout removes two scaffolds at once and is not a model of PMS, where only SHANK3 is affected; attributing the signalling deficit to Shank3 is not possible from this design. Low survival rate of the DKO raises a survivor-selection concern that the abstract does not address.
claims.model: Shank1-Shank3 double knockout (DKO); exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: activation (phosphorylation) of Akt, S6, ERK1/2 and eEF2

claims.text: Shank1-Shank3 double knockout mice show a low survival rate and severe behavioural impairments.
claims.limO: 'Severe behavioural impairments' is not quantified and the tests are not named. No statistics in the abstract. Not informative about SHANK3 haploinsufficiency, which is the human condition.
claims.model: Shank1-Shank3 double knockout (DKO)
claims.measure: survival and a behavioural battery, tests not named in the abstract

claims.text: The TC genotype of the SHANK3 rs9616915 polymorphism was associated with increased risk of Parkinson disease in a North Iranian case-control sample.
claims.n: 100 patients with Parkinson disease and 100 control volunteers
claims.limA: The authors state that further studies are needed to confirm the role of SHANK3 in Parkinson disease.
claims.limO: 100 versus 100 is small for a candidate-SNP association. The confidence interval (1.04-3.74) only just excludes 1, there is no correction for the genotype models tested, and population stratification is not addressed. No replication cohort.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: rs9616915 genotype by PCR-RFLP, genotype distribution compared between cases and controls

claims.text: No significant difference in SHANK3 rs9616915 allele distribution was found between Parkinson disease cases and controls.
claims.n: 100 patients with Parkinson disease and 100 control volunteers
claims.eff: p = 0.7; no odds ratio and no confidence interval reported for the allelic test
claims.limO: This null comes WITH a statistical test (p = 0.7) but WITHOUT any power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval or an odds ratio, so the range of allelic effects the data exclude cannot be determined. It is therefore not evidence of absence of an allelic association. It also sits awkwardly beside R-1002: a significant genotype distribution with a non-significant allele distribution in the same 200 samples is a pattern that commonly arises from Hardy-Weinberg deviation or from testing several genetic models, and the abstract reports neither a Hardy-Weinberg test nor a multiple-comparison correction.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: rs9616915 allele frequency compared between cases and controls

claims.text: Shank3(e4-9) mutant mice have reduced levels of Homer1b/c, GKAP and GluA1 at the postsynaptic density and attenuated activity-dependent redistribution of GluA1-containing AMPA receptors.
claims.limO: No quantities, effect sizes or p values in the abstract. Age and sex of the animals used for the biochemistry are not stated, which matters because SHANK3 phenotypes are developmentally staged.
claims.model: Shank3(e4-9) homozygous mutant mouse; exons 4-9 deleted, disrupting major isoforms
claims.measure: Homer1b/c, GKAP and GluA1 levels at the PSD; activity-dependent GluA1 redistribution

claims.text: Basal synaptic transmission was normal in CA1 hippocampus of Shank3(e4-9) mice while long-term potentiation was deficient.
claims.limO: The null half of this claim comes WITHOUT a stated statistical test, WITHOUT any power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval; 'normal' is asserted, not quantified. A null of this kind cannot establish that basal transmission is unaffected, only that no difference was detected in an unstated number of slices. The LTP deficit is likewise unquantified. Induction protocol, age and recording configuration are all absent from the abstract, and all three strongly affect CA1 LTP.
claims.model: Shank3(e4-9) homozygous mutant mouse
claims.measure: basal excitatory synaptic transmission and long-term potentiation in CA1

claims.text: Shank3(e4-9) homozygous mutant mice display abnormal social behaviours, communication, repetitive behaviours and learning and memory, with male mice more severely impaired than females in motor coordination.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or p values in the abstract, and no correction for the number of behavioural domains tested. The sex difference in motor coordination is reported without an interaction statistic.
claims.model: Shank3(e4-9) homozygous mutant mouse
claims.measure: behavioural battery: social interaction, ultrasonic communication, repetitive behaviour, learning and memory, motor coordination

claims.text: Dietary zinc supplementation reversed hyperactivity and social preference deficits in Shank2 knockout mice but did not alter their working memory deficits, and did not rescue deficits in NMDA/AMPA receptor-mediated transmission.
claims.limA: The authors conclude that dietary zinc has differential effectiveness across ASD mouse models, even within the Shank family.
claims.limO: The two null results (working memory, NMDA/AMPA transmission) are reported WITHOUT any statistical test value, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals. They cannot establish that zinc has no effect on these measures; with unreported n they are compatible with a real but undetected effect. No dose, duration or sample size is given. The null is also asymmetrically reported against significant positive findings in the same animals, which is the classic setting in which an underpowered null is over-interpreted as a dissociation.
claims.model: Shank2-/- knockout mouse; exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: hyperactivity, social preference and working memory behaviour; NMDA/AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission

ref.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

claims.text: SHANK3 protein was highly expressed at synapses of Shank2 knockout mice and was returned to wild-type levels by dietary zinc supplementation.
claims.limO: No quantification, no statistics, no n. The direction is recorded as mixed because SHANK3 is elevated by the Shank2 deletion and lowered again by zinc. Relevant caution for the corpus: synaptic SHANK3 level moves in response to a perturbation of a different Shank gene, so it is not a specific readout of SHANK3 dosage.
claims.model: Shank2-/- knockout mouse
claims.measure: synaptic SHANK3 protein level

ref.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

claims.text: Heterozygous shank3ab frameshift mutant zebrafish show significantly slower digestive tract peristaltic contractions and prolonged passage time, and intestinal bulb emptying is restored by injection of human SHANK3 mRNA.
claims.eff: p < 0.001 for contraction rate, p < 0.004 for passage time; no effect size and no confidence interval reported
claims.limA: The authors note that the mRNA rescue restored intestinal bulb emptying but that deficits in posterior intestinal motility persisted.
claims.limO: p values only, with no effect sizes, no confidence intervals and no sample sizes. The rescue is partial and the abstract does not say whether the residual posterior deficit was formally tested. Zebrafish gut physiology differs substantially from human; the heterozygous design is nevertheless the right dosage match to PMS.
claims.model: shank3abΔC heterozygote; CRISPR/Cas9 C-terminal frameshift mutations in shank3a and shank3b paralogues, described by the authors as clinically related
claims.measure: digestive tract peristaltic contraction rate and passage time by imaging

claims.text: Serotonin-positive enteroendocrine cells were significantly reduced in shank3ab mutant zebrafish, while enteric neuron counts and overall digestive tract epithelial structure, including goblet cell number, were unaffected in heterozygotes.
claims.eff: p < 0.05 for the enteroendocrine cell reduction; no effect size or confidence interval. No statistic at all for the unaffected measures.
claims.limO: The null component (enteric neuron counts, epithelial structure, goblet cell number unaffected) is reported WITHOUT a statistical test, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, so it cannot be read as evidence that these are preserved; cell-count assays of this kind are routinely underpowered for moderate differences. The positive component carries only p < 0.05 with no effect size, from an unreported number of larvae.
claims.model: shank3abΔC heterozygote and homozygote zebrafish
claims.measure: serotonin-positive enteroendocrine cell counts; enteric neuron counts; goblet cell number and epithelial structure

claims.text: No significant difference in response rate between synchronous and asynchronous stroking was observed in Shank3-knockout mice, whereas wild-type mice showed a significantly stronger response to synchronous stroking, indicating that the rubber tail illusion is not obvious in Shank3-knockout mice.
claims.eff: not_reported; the abstract gives neither test statistics, p values, effect sizes nor confidence intervals for either genotype
claims.limA: The authors state explicitly that the influence of hyporeactivity cannot be completely ruled out.
claims.limO: This null is reported WITHOUT any test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval, and with no sample size. It is therefore not evidence of an absent illusion. The authors' own caveat is the decisive one and is a floor effect: the overall response rate in knockout mice was much lower than in wild type, so a synchronous-asynchronous difference could be undetectable simply because there are too few responses of any kind to differ. Interpreting this as altered body representation requires a measure not subject to that floor.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse; allele and exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: response rate on grasping of the rubber tail, as an index of the body ownership illusion

claims.text: Maternal dietary zinc supplementation during pregnancy and lactation prevented social interaction deficits, normalised anxiety behaviour and prevented repetitive grooming in offspring Shank3 knockout mice, with effects maintained into adulthood.
claims.limA: The authors frame the finding as showing that zinc supplementation from the beginning of brain development can prevent deficits long term.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or p values in the abstract, and no correction across the behavioural domains tested. Critically for translation, the design is preventive and prenatal: it says nothing about supplementation begun after birth, which is the only option available to a family after a PMS diagnosis. 150 ppm dietary zinc in mice is not directly convertible to a human dose.
claims.model: Shank3-/- knockout mouse; allele and exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: social interaction, anxiety behaviour and repetitive grooming

claims.text: Maternal zinc supplementation altered postsynaptic NMDA receptor-mediated currents and presynaptic function at glutamatergic synapses onto medium spiny neurons in the corticostriatal pathway of offspring Shank3 knockout mice.
claims.limO: 'Altered' is not a direction: the abstract does not say whether the currents moved towards or away from wild-type values, so this record cannot be used to claim normalisation. No n, no statistics.
claims.model: Shank3-/- knockout mouse offspring
claims.measure: NMDA receptor-mediated postsynaptic currents and presynaptic function by whole-cell recording

claims.text: Behavioural phenotypes of Shank3-deficient mice were largely strain-independent: only very modest strain effects were found across a large battery of behavioural analyses in C57BL/6, 129SVE and FVB/Ntac backgrounds.
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistics, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors describe the result as surprising and had intended to use strain differences to identify modifier loci.
claims.limO: This null is reported WITHOUT test statistics, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and with no sample sizes. That matters more here than usual: detecting a genotype-by-background interaction requires substantially more power than detecting a main effect, so a large battery of underpowered interaction tests is the expected way to produce exactly this result. 'Very modest' is also not 'none', and the abstract does not say which measures did show effects. The claim is best read as 'no large strain effect was detected', not as 'genetic background does not modify Shank3 phenotypes'. It is nevertheless the most direct available test of that assumption, which this corpus elsewhere treats as established.
claims.model: Shank3 heterozygous, knockout and wild-type mice; targeted disruption of exons coding the ankyrin-repeat domain, disrupting expression of full-length Shank3
claims.measure: large battery of observable behaviours, tests not enumerated in the abstract, compared across three genetic backgrounds

claims.text: Maternal Cronobacter sakazakii infection downregulated SHANK3 and PSD-95 expression in rat offspring, alongside impaired novel odour recognition, depressive behaviour and altered dendritic and spine morphology.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, effect sizes or p values in the abstract. SHANK3 is one of many measured readouts in a study not about SHANK3, so the risk of selective reporting is real. Direction only, no quantification.
claims.model: not_applicable; wild-type rats, maternal infection model
claims.measure: SHANK3 and PSD-95 expression; axon length, dendritic branching and spine morphology; novel odour recognition and tail suspension tests

claims.text: Synaptic levels of ProSAP2/Shank3 regulate AMPA and NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission and change the levels of presynaptic and postsynaptic proteins through neurexin-neuroligin transsynaptic signalling in rat hippocampal neurons.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no statistics. Overexpression and knockdown in culture are strong perturbations that do not establish what endogenous SHANK3 does at normal dosage, and a heterozygous reduction as in PMS is not modelled.
claims.model: rat hippocampal neurons; ProSAP2/Shank3 levels manipulated, ASD-associated mutations expressed
claims.measure: AMPA and NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission; presynaptic and postsynaptic protein levels

claims.text: ASD-associated mutations in ProSAP2/Shank3 disrupt postsynaptic AMPA and NMDA receptor signalling and also interfere with transsynaptic signalling to presynaptic structure and function.
claims.limO: The abstract itself notes that in earlier work the glutamate receptor and spine phenotypes of Shank3 mutations were 'not universally penetrant'. That is an acknowledgement of inconsistency across studies, not a result of this one, and this record should not be read as resolving it. No n, no statistics.
claims.model: rat hippocampal neurons expressing ASD-associated ProSAP2/Shank3 mutations
claims.measure: AMPA and NMDA receptor signalling; presynaptic structure and function

claims.text: AMPA receptors, NMDA receptors and Shank family members are distributed differently at synapses onto hippocampal interneurons than at synapses onto pyramidal neurons.
claims.limO: The abstract reports 'Shank family members' without saying which paralogues were resolved, so this record cannot be attributed to SHANK3 specifically. No n, no statistics, no effect sizes. The paper is primarily methodological and the biological comparison is an application example.
claims.model: not_applicable; YFP-ChR2 mice expressing the reporter exclusively in interneurons
claims.measure: single-synapse quantification of over 40 synaptic proteins by an adapted Magnified Analysis of the Proteome (MAP) expansion protocol

claims.text: Knockdown of Shank1 or Shank2, but not of Shank3, reduced the number of AMPA receptor-containing synapses at rat hippocampal SC-CA1 synapses; Shank3 knockdown alone did not reduce either the number or the unitary response.
claims.n: not_reported (dual whole-cell patch clamp pairs; number of pairs and cultures not stated)
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistics, no effect sizes, no confidence intervals
claims.limA: The authors frame the work as showing that Shank family proteins have distinct rather than redundant functions.
claims.limO: The Shank3 null is reported WITHOUT a stated test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval, and with no number of recorded pairs. Paired-recording designs are sensitive but the absence of an interval means the size of the Shank3 effect the data exclude is unknown. Knockdown efficiency for each paralogue is not reported in the abstract, and an ineffective Shank3 knockdown would produce exactly this result; this is the first thing to check in the full text. The dissociation between paralogues is asserted from three separate comparisons without a reported interaction test.
claims.model: rat hippocampal slice culture; lentivirus-mediated knockdown of Shank1, Shank2 or Shank3 with molecular replacement
claims.measure: AMPA receptor-mediated synaptic response by paired whole-cell recording, decomposed into number of active synapses and unitary response

claims.text: Simultaneous knockdown of Shank1 and Shank2 reduced both the number and the unitary response of active synapses and decreased NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic response, and synaptic transmission was restored by molecular replacement with Shank2 or Shank3c, requiring an intact SAM domain.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics, no effect sizes. The rescue is by overexpression of a replacement construct on a knockdown background, which is not the same as restoring endogenous dosage. Shank3c is a short isoform and the abstract does not report whether full-length Shank3 was tested.
claims.model: rat hippocampal slice culture; double knockdown of Shank1 and Shank2 with molecular replacement by Shank2, Shank3c or SAM-domain mutants
claims.measure: AMPA and NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic responses by paired whole-cell recording

claims.text: Shank3b knockout mice show altered membrane properties and excitability of medial prefrontal cortex pyramidal neurons together with reduced inhibitory postsynaptic currents.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. 'Deficiencies in GABA release or GABAA receptor transport' is stated as an inference from the IPSC change rather than as a measured mechanism. Note for the contradiction catalogue: S-1018 in this same batch reports NO significant change in IPSC frequency in Shank3-deficient mice, but in hippocampal primary neurons rather than mPFC slices, so the two are not directly comparable and are not recorded as contradicting.
claims.model: Shank3b knockout mouse
claims.measure: whole-cell patch-clamp recording of membrane properties, excitability and inhibitory postsynaptic currents

claims.text: Prefrontal cortex tissue of Shank3b knockout mice shows differentially expressed genes enriched in synaptic function and calcium channel signalling pathways, alongside reduced postsynaptic density at excitatory synapses.
claims.limO: No n, no fold changes, no adjusted p values and no enrichment statistics in the abstract. Bulk tissue RNA sequencing cannot separate cell types, and the ultrastructural measurement is reported without quantities.
claims.model: Shank3b knockout mouse
claims.measure: RNA sequencing of PFC tissue with pathway enrichment; electron-microscopic measurement of postsynaptic density

claims.text: Shank3b knockout mice whose mothers received faecal microbiota transplantation from children with autism showed impaired learning and exacerbated anxiety-like behaviour in adulthood, and increased colon permeability.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. Donor material came from an unstated number of children, so the exposure is poorly specified and could reflect one donor's microbiome. Only male offspring were studied.
claims.model: Shank3b-/- male offspring of Shank3b+/- dams that received FMT from children with ASD
claims.measure: learning and anxiety-like behaviour; colon permeability assessed by zonula occludens (ZO1, ZO3) and claudin markers

claims.text: Faecal microbiota transplantation from children with autism improved learning in adolescent Shank3b knockout mice while impairing it in the same genotype in adulthood.
claims.limO: A reversal of sign between two ages, reported without statistics, without n and without an age-by-treatment interaction test, is the single most fragile pattern in behavioural work and should not be cited as an established developmental effect until the full text is read. The abstract flags it only as 'interestingly'.
claims.model: Shank3b-/- male offspring after maternal FMT from children with ASD
claims.measure: learning performance; task not named in the abstract

claims.text: Overexpression of the zinc-sensitive ProSAP1/Shank2 or ProSAP2/Shank3 increased synapse density at excitatory postsynapses, whereas overexpression of zinc-insensitive Shank1 did not, although knockdown of any of the three decreased synapse density.
claims.limO: The negative arm here — Shank1 overexpression failing to increase synapse density — is reported WITHOUT a statistical test, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval, and carries the interpretive weight of the zinc-sensitivity argument. No n and no effect sizes anywhere in the abstract. Overexpression is a strong perturbation and the inference that zinc sensitivity explains the paralogue difference is correlational.
claims.model: cultured neurons; selective overexpression and shRNA knockdown of each ProSAP/Shank family member
claims.measure: synapse density and recruitment of ProSAP/Shank proteins to the postsynaptic density

claims.text: Depletion of synaptic zinc combined with knockdown of zinc-insensitive Shank1 caused rapid disintegration of postsynaptic densities and loss of Homer1, PSD-95 and NMDA receptors.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics. Zinc chelation in culture is a severe manipulation of uncertain relation to dietary zinc status in vivo.
claims.model: cultured neurons with synaptic Zn2+ depletion and Shank1 knockdown
claims.measure: postsynaptic density integrity; Homer1, PSD-95 and NMDA receptor levels

claims.text: Shank3 exon 4-22 deletion heterozygous mice show no significant behavioural impairments at baseline.
claims.limO: This null is stated as a background property of the model, WITHOUT any statistical test, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and with no sample size or list of tests. It is therefore not evidence that heterozygous Shank3 deletion has no behavioural consequence; it is a statement that none was detected in unspecified assays. Taken at face value it would nonetheless be important, because the homozygous models that carry most of the preclinical literature are not the genotype of people with PMS. Recommended for full-text confirmation before any use.
claims.model: Shank3 exon 4-22 deletion heterozygous mutant (Sh3+/-)
claims.measure: behavioural battery; tests not enumerated for the baseline characterisation

claims.text: Two weeks after a systemic lipopolysaccharide challenge, Shank3 haploinsufficient mice showed motor impairment, anxiety-like behaviour and excessive grooming while wild-type mice recovered, and anti-inflammatory treatment partially reversed these changes.
claims.limA: The authors present the model as supporting a potential mechanism for human behavioural regression and explicitly leave it for future investigation.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. 'Partially reversed' is unquantified and the anti-inflammatory agent is not named. The human observation the hypothesis rests on is described by the authors as a small cohort. Phenotype penetrance in the het depends on the baseline null R-1027 holding.
claims.model: Shank3 exon 4-22 deletion heterozygous mutant (Sh3+/-) with LPS challenge
claims.measure: motor function, anxiety-like behaviour and grooming; transcriptomic analysis; microglial markers, TLR4, synapse engulfment

claims.text: Soluble amyloid beta prevented association of zinc with ProSAP2/Shank3 and decreased dendritic zinc clusters, and zinc supplementation or saturation of amyloid beta with zinc counteracted the reduction in synapse density and in ProSAP2/Shank3 levels.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no statistics. The human AD hippocampal comparison is described without sample size or post-mortem interval. Relevance to PMS is as a counter-example rather than as a mechanism.
claims.model: rat hippocampal cultures with amyloid beta oligomer accumulation; APP-PS1 mice and human AD hippocampus for the tissue comparison
claims.measure: zinc association with ProSAP2/Shank3, dendritic zinc cluster concentration, synapse density, ProSAP2/Shank3 and Shank1 levels at the PSD

claims.text: The amyloid-beta-induced dysregulation of ProSAP/Shank was independent of any alteration at the transcriptional level.
claims.limO: This null is reported WITHOUT a statistical test, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and without the assay's sensitivity. The whole post-transcriptional interpretation rests on it, and a modest transcriptional change cannot be excluded by an untested, unquantified null. The abstract also does not say which Shank paralogue transcripts were measured.
claims.model: rat hippocampal cultures with amyloid beta oligomers
claims.measure: ProSAP/Shank transcript levels

claims.text: Shank3 knockout mice show early synaptic deficits at postnatal day 14 within the medial prefrontal cortex and in its projections to the mediodorsal thalamus, with reduced excitability of excitatory neurons, while behavioural deficits were already detectable at postnatal day 11.
claims.limA: The authors note that behavioural deficits preceded the observed synaptic changes and raise compensatory mechanisms as an interpretation.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. Only two developmental timepoints were sampled, so 'behaviour precedes synaptic change' rests on the absence of a P11 synaptic measurement rather than on a measured null; the earliest synaptic timepoint is P14. The claim about ordering should not be cited as established.
claims.model: Shank3-/- knockout mouse; allele and exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: network activity, cellular excitability and synaptic transmission in mPFC and mPFC-MD projections; early behavioural assays

claims.text: By adulthood the early medial prefrontal cortex hypofunction of Shank3 knockout mice had progressed to network hyperfunction with layer 5 pyramidal cell hyperexcitability and augmented glutamatergic signalling to mediodorsal thalamus.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics. The hypofunction-to-hyperfunction reversal is inferred from two timepoints in different animals, not from longitudinal measurement. Important consequence if it holds: a circuit or EEG endpoint in PMS could move in opposite directions depending on the age at which it is measured, which would make a single-timepoint biomarker uninterpretable.
claims.model: Shank3-/- knockout mouse
claims.measure: network activity, layer 5 pyramidal excitability, glutamatergic transmission to MD and action potential production

claims.text: No significant change in inhibitory postsynaptic current frequency was found in primary hippocampal neurons from Shank3-deficient mice, whereas prenatally valproate-exposed rats showed a decrease.
claims.eff: not_reported; the abstract gives no test statistic, no effect size and no confidence interval for the Shank3 null
claims.limA: The authors nonetheless conclude that the findings strongly support the excitatory-inhibitory imbalance hypothesis in ASD, which for the Shank3 arm rests on the GABAergic marker results rather than on IPSC frequency.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT a reported test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval, and with no number of recorded cells or cultures, so it cannot establish that inhibitory transmission is intact in Shank3-deficient neurons. The comparison is also asymmetric: a significant effect in one model and a null in the other is reported as a dissociation without an interaction test, and the two models are different species (mouse versus rat). The authors' overall conclusion runs ahead of the Shank3 data. Note for the contradiction catalogue: S-1012 in this same batch reports REDUCED inhibitory postsynaptic currents in Shank3b mPFC pyramidal neurons. The two are not recorded as formally contradicting because the region (hippocampus versus mPFC) and the preparation (primary culture versus slice) differ, but the committee should see them side by side.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient mouse; allele and exons not stated in the abstract. Prenatally VPA-exposed rats studied in parallel
claims.measure: inhibitory postsynaptic current frequency in primary hippocampal neurons

claims.text: Shank3-deficient mice showed a reduced proportion of GABAergic neurons in the hippocampus and reduced expression of Gabarap and Gabarapl1, together with altered temporal dynamics of inhibitory synaptic transmission.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. The number of glutamatergic neurons was increased only in the VPA rats, not in the Shank3 mice, so the E/I shift in the Shank3 model rests on the inhibitory side alone. A change in inter-event interval distribution without a change in mean frequency is a weak and easily artefactual signal in culture recordings.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient mouse; allele not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: proportion of GABAergic neurons; Gabarap and Gabarapl1 gene expression; cumulative probability of inter-event intervals for inhibitory currents

claims.text: The F-actin binding protein Abp1 binds through its SH3 domain to a conserved proline-rich motif in the C-terminal region of ProSAP1/Shank2 and ProSAP2/Shank3, and can bind dynamic F-actin and ProSAPs simultaneously.
claims.eff: not_applicable; a binding interaction, not an estimate
claims.limO: No quantification of binding affinity or stoichiometry in the abstract. The functional significance for synaptic plasticity is proposed, not demonstrated. The proline-rich motif is shared with Shank2, so the interaction is not SHANK3-specific.
claims.model: not_applicable; rat brain tissue and hippocampal neurons
claims.measure: affinity purification, co-immunoprecipitation, colocalisation and in vivo recruitment assays

claims.text: Patients carrying SHANK3 mutations showed impaired valence-oriented sniffing and altered electroencephalographic responses to odours.
claims.eff: not_reported; no statistics, no effect size and no confidence interval in the abstract
claims.limO: The number of patients is not stated anywhere in the abstract, which for a human SHANK3 cohort is the single most important missing number. No statistics, no control group description, no age or sex distribution. Sniffing and EEG responses both depend on arousal and compliance, which are hard to equate between patients with intellectual disability and controls; the abstract does not say how this was handled. Recorded as biomarker-relevant because it is a non-invasive, odour-evoked EEG measure in humans with SHANK3 mutations, which is a rare combination, but it should not be cited quantitatively from the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: valence-oriented sniffing behaviour and odour-evoked EEG response

claims.text: Shank3B knockout mice showed blunted behavioural responses to both attractive and aversive odours, associated with attenuated odour-evoked calcium signals and reduced excitatory synaptic transmission in the cortical amygdala.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. Blunted responses to both valences are also compatible with a general reduction in responsiveness rather than with a valence-coding deficit specifically; the abstract does not report a control for overall odour detection.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- knockout mouse
claims.measure: behavioural responses to attractive and aversive odours; odour-evoked calcium signals; excitatory synaptic transmission in CoA

claims.text: Acute cortical-amygdala-specific Shank3 deletion recapitulated the olfactory valence deficits, and targeted restoration of Shank3 expression in the cortical amygdala rescued odour-induced appetitive and aversive behaviours.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no statistics, and no description of the restoration construct, its expression level or its timing relative to the behavioural test. Restoration by viral overexpression is not equivalent to restoring endogenous dosage and can overshoot. The rescue is of one behaviour in one region and should not be generalised.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant mice with acute CoA-specific deletion and with targeted CoA Shank3 re-expression
claims.measure: odour-induced appetitive and aversive behaviour

claims.text: ASD-associated Shank2 single nucleotide variants reduced synaptic density and the frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents in rat hippocampal neurons, and these deficits were prevented by chronic zinc supplementation.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. The variants are expressed on top of endogenous Shank2 rather than replacing it, so the design tests a dominant effect, not haploinsufficiency. SHANK3 is not measured; relevance to PMS is by family analogy only. 10 micromolar zinc in culture has no established correspondence to any achievable human exposure.
claims.model: dissociated rat hippocampal cultures expressing EGFP-tagged Shank2 wild type or ASD-associated SNVs
claims.measure: synaptic density and miniature excitatory postsynaptic current frequency

claims.text: Shank3b mutant mice showed deficits in both social interaction and attentional allocation.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values, and the behavioural tasks are not named.
claims.model: Shank3b mutant mouse
claims.measure: social interaction and attentional allocation tasks; tasks not named in the abstract

claims.text: Optogenetic activation of the anterior cingulate cortex to zona incerta circuit rescued social impairments in Shank3b mutant mice, whereas activation of the anterior cingulate cortex to limbic thalamic reticular nucleus pathway restored attentional performance.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no statistics. A double dissociation claim requires the cross-conditions to have been tested and reported as null; the abstract does not state that they were. Optogenetic rescue of an acute behavioural readout says nothing about whether the circuit is the developmental origin of the deficit.
claims.model: Shank3b mutant mouse with pathway-specific optogenetics
claims.measure: social interaction and attentional performance after circuit activation

claims.text: Female mice subjected to vicarious learned helplessness showed reduced prefrontal cortex expression of the postsynaptic scaffolding proteins PSD-95 and SHANK3, whereas males showed deficits in BDNF and glucocorticoid signalling instead.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values, and no sex-by-treatment interaction statistic for a claim that is entirely about a sex difference. SHANK3 is one of many measured readouts in a study not about SHANK3.
claims.model: not_applicable; C57BL/6J mice in a vicarious learned helplessness paradigm
claims.measure: PSD-95 and SHANK3 protein by immunoblotting; Oxtr, Bdnf, Nr3c1, mGluR2 and Il6 by RT-qPCR

claims.text: No significant differences in behavioural performance or in Shank3 expression were observed between perinatally lead-exposed and control male C57BL/6J offspring, despite confirmed lead accumulation in blood and brain.
claims.eff: not_reported; the abstract gives no test statistic, no effect size and no confidence interval for the null
claims.limA: The authors state that further studies are warranted on dose-dependent effects, sex-specific vulnerabilities and broader molecular pathways, and restrict their conclusion to the conditions tested.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT any reported test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and with no sample size. It is therefore not evidence that perinatal lead has no effect on behaviour or on Shank3 expression; it is a failure to detect one at a single dose, in one sex, with unreported n. The exposure validation is the strongest part of the design: lead did reach the brain, which rules out the most common explanation for a null in this literature. Only males were studied and only one dose was used, both of which the authors acknowledge.
claims.model: not_applicable; C57BL/6J mice, maternal lead acetate exposure
claims.measure: three-chambered social-nonsocial interaction test and Morris water maze; Shank3 expression by real-time PCR

ref.venue: The Journal of Veterinary Medical Science

claims.text: Lead concentrations were significantly elevated in blood, brain, bone, liver and kidney of perinatally exposed offspring, confirming maternal-foetal lead transfer.
claims.limO: Concentrations are not given, only their significance, so the exposure cannot be compared with human environmental levels.
claims.model: not_applicable; C57BL/6J mice
claims.measure: lead concentration by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry

ref.venue: The Journal of Veterinary Medical Science

claims.text: Antisense oligonucleotide-mediated inhibition of the glycine transporter Slc6a20a normalised ASD-related phenotypes in male Shank2- and Shank3-mutant mice, with model-dependent rescue profiles.
claims.limA: The authors themselves frame the work as showing both the potential and the limitations of the approach, and describe rescue as model-dependent.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values, no dose and no duration. 'Model-dependent rescue profiles' means some phenotypes were not rescued, but the abstract does not say which, so the negative half of this result is not extractable and should be sought in the full text. Only male mice were studied, which for a candidate therapeutic is a material gap.
claims.model: Shank3-mutant and Shank2-mutant mice; alleles and exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: ASD-related behavioural phenotypes

claims.text: Slc6a20a antisense oligonucleotide treatment rescued NMDA receptor hypofunction and synaptic phospho-proteomic profiles in the prefrontal cortex of Shank-mutant mice.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no statistics. The abstract does not separate the Shank2 and Shank3 results for this measure, so the SHANK3-specific effect cannot be isolated. Phospho-proteomic 'rescue' is a profile-level statement without a stated metric.
claims.model: Shank2- and Shank3-mutant mice
claims.measure: NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic function; synaptic phospho-proteomic profile

claims.text: An antisense oligonucleotide targeting human SLC6A20 rescued suppressed NMDA receptor function in human cortical organoids carrying SHANK3 or SHANK2 mutations.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no statistics, and no statement of whether the organoids derive from patients or from engineered isogenic lines. That distinction decides whether this is P2 evidence at all. Organoid NMDA receptor function is measured in an immature tissue with no circuit context. study_population is recorded as not_reported rather than pms because the abstract does not say the lines came from people with PMS.
