claims.model: human cortical organoids harbouring SHANK3 or SHANK2 mutations; origin of the lines and the specific variants not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: NMDA receptor function

claims.text: Shank3 was among a subset of postsynaptic density proteins whose turnover was stabilised following contextual fear conditioning in mouse hippocampus.
claims.limO: No n, no turnover rates, no statistics and no correction across a proteome-wide screen in which Shank3 is one of many proteins. Direction is recorded as decrease, meaning a decreased turnover rate (increased stability); the abstract does not quantify it.
claims.model: not_applicable; wild-type mice with stable isotope labelling in mammals
claims.measure: protein turnover rate by stable isotope labelling and mass spectrometry

ref.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

claims.text: No alteration in spinogenesis was observed in human iPSC-derived neurons carrying a de novo heterozygous truncating SHANK3 mutation 30 days after transplantation into newborn mouse cortex, in contrast to previous in vitro findings.
claims.n: not_reported; one patient line and one control line, number of animals not stated
claims.eff: not_reported; the abstract gives no test statistic, no effect size and no confidence interval for the null
claims.limA: The authors attribute the discrepancy to the early age of analysis, saying no alteration was seen 'at this early age'.
claims.limO: This null is reported WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval, and with no number of neurons, spines or animals. It cannot establish that spinogenesis is unaffected in vivo. The design is also a single patient line against a single control line, so line-to-line variation is fully confounded with genotype and no isogenic control is mentioned. Thirty days is explicitly early, and the authors' own explanation — that the phenotype has not yet emerged — is untested. The co-transplantation design is a genuine strength: patient and control neurons sat in the same host brain.
claims.model: human iPSC-derived cortical neuronal precursors from a patient with a de novo heterozygous SHANK3 truncating mutation, co-transplanted with control precursors into newborn mouse cortex (chimeric mouse)
claims.measure: dendritic spine density and morphology (spinogenesis) in transplanted human neurons

claims.text: Human iPSC-derived neurons carrying a de novo heterozygous truncating SHANK3 mutation showed reduced cell soma size in selective neuronal categories and reduced axonal projections 30 days after transplantation into mouse cortex.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. 'Selective neuronal categories' is not specified, which leaves open how many categories were tested and whether the selection was post hoc. One patient line against one control line, with no isogenic control mentioned.
claims.model: chimeric mouse carrying co-transplanted patient and control human iPSC-derived neurons
claims.measure: cell soma size by neuronal category; axonal projection extent

claims.text: A SHANK3 methylation marker in cervical scrapings discriminated endometrial cancer from benign endometrial thickening with an area under the curve of 0.782.
claims.n: 20 patients with endometrial cancer and 20 benign endometrial thickening controls, split 6:4 into training and validation cohorts
claims.eff: single-gene AUC 0.782, reported without a confidence interval and without sensitivity or specificity for this marker alone
claims.limA: The authors describe it as a single-centre exploratory study with a small sample size requiring validation in large-scale multi-centre independent cohorts.
claims.limO: 20 versus 20, with three markers selected from 745 differentially methylated genes in the same small training set, is a textbook setting for overfitting; the AUC carries no confidence interval, which at this sample size would be very wide. The validation cohort is a split of the same 40 samples, not an independent cohort. Direction of methylation change at the SHANK3 locus is not stated.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: DNA methylation of the SHANK3 marker region in cervical scrapings by methylated CpG tandem amplification and sequencing; discrimination reported as AUC

claims.text: Saracatinib normalised elevated basal protein synthesis, novel object recognition memory and social behaviour in FMR1 knockout mice but did not normalise the glutamatergic synapse protein interaction network, instead inducing extensive changes to protein complexes containing Shank3, NMDA receptors and Fyn.
claims.limA: The authors conclude explicitly that behavioural rescue does not correlate with network normalisation.
claims.limO: The negative component — failure to normalise the protein interaction network — is reported WITHOUT a statistical test, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and a network-level 'not normalised' is in any case a composite judgement rather than a single test. No n, no doses, no durations. Relevance to SHANK3 is contextual: Shank3-containing complexes are a readout here, not the perturbed gene.
claims.model: not_applicable for SHANK3; FMR1-/y mouse
claims.measure: protein interaction network state by quantitative multiplex co-immunoprecipitation; basal protein synthesis; novel object recognition and social behaviour

claims.text: Protein interaction network states downstream of NMDA receptor stimulation were similar to wild type in FMR1 knockout neurons, whereas unstimulated networks resembled mGluR-stimulated wild-type networks.
claims.limO: This null is reported WITHOUT a statistical test, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals. 'Similar to WT' in a high-dimensional network comparison is particularly weak without a stated similarity metric and a null distribution, and it carries the specificity argument for the mGluR result.
claims.model: FMR1-/y mouse cortical neurons and acute slices
claims.measure: glutamatergic synapse protein interaction network state

claims.text: Primary oligodendrocyte cultures derived from Shank3 InsG3680 mutant mice show impaired molecular and physiological glutamatergic traits, indicating a postsynaptic role for Shank3 in oligodendrocytes.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. 'Impaired molecular and physiological glutamatergic traits' aggregates several measures that are not enumerated in the abstract.
claims.model: InsG3680 Shank3 knock-in mouse, carrying a mutation observed in patients
claims.measure: molecular and physiological glutamatergic traits of primary oligodendrocyte cultures

claims.text: InsG3680 Shank3 mutant mice show reduced expression of myelination-related transcripts and proteins, deficits in myelin ultrastructure and white matter, reduced axonal conductivity and impaired motor skills.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values across a wide battery of measures with no stated correction. The abstract does not say whether the white matter measurement was imaging-based, which decides whether the measure has a direct human counterpart.
claims.model: InsG3680 Shank3 knock-in mouse
claims.measure: myelination transcripts and proteins, myelin ultrastructure by electron microscopy, white matter measures, axonal conductivity, motor skill tests

claims.text: Induced pluripotent stem cell-derived oligodendrocytes from a patient carrying the InsG3680 SHANK3 mutation showed significant impairments.
claims.n: one patient; number of lines, differentiations and cells not reported
claims.limO: A single patient line, with no isogenic control mentioned, so line-to-line variation is confounded with genotype. The impairments are described as 'significant' and 'with clinical relevance' without a single number, test or effect size in the abstract. The strongest claim in the paper rests on the weakest reported design.
claims.model: patient-derived iPSC oligodendrocytes carrying the InsG3680 SHANK3 mutation
claims.measure: oligodendrocyte molecular and functional measures; not enumerated in the abstract

claims.text: Shank1, Shank2 and Shank3 messenger RNAs are all present in the synaptic neuropil of rat hippocampal CA1, with Shank1 the most abundant, and the half-lives of all three are predicted to be 18 to 28 hours.
claims.eff: predicted half-lives 18-28 hours, reported as a range across the three transcripts without per-transcript values or confidence intervals
claims.limO: Half-lives are described as predicted, not measured directly, and the prediction method is not named in the abstract. No n, no statistics. Rat hippocampus, which may not generalise to human cortex or to other regions. The novel 3' ends reported are for Shank1 and Shank2, not Shank3.
claims.model: not_applicable; wild-type rat hippocampus
claims.measure: Shank1, Shank2 and Shank3 mRNA levels in microdissected neuropil; mRNA half-life; 3' end sequencing for alternative polyadenylation

ref.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

claims.text: Basolateral amygdala pyramidal neurons are hyperactive in Shank3 InsG3680 knock-in mice, with increased excitatory and decreased inhibitory input, and chemogenetic inhibition of these neurons rescued the anxiety phenotype.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no p values. Chemogenetic rescue of anxiety behaviour is an acute manipulation and does not establish that BLA hyperactivity causes the phenotype developmentally. Homozygous knock-in, whereas people with PMS are heterozygous.
claims.model: Shank3 InsG3680 knock-in homozygous mouse (InsG3680+/+)
claims.measure: excitatory and inhibitory synaptic input by whole-cell recording; anxiety-like behaviour

claims.text: Medial prefrontal cortex control of the basolateral amygdala is diminished in Shank3 InsG3680 knock-in mice, and optogenetic activation of the mPFC-BLA pathway rescued the anxiety phenotype by increasing feedforward inhibition of the amygdala.
claims.limO: No n, no effect sizes, no statistics. Acute optogenetic rescue, with the same developmental caveat as R-1058.
claims.model: Shank3 InsG3680 knock-in homozygous mouse
claims.measure: feedforward inhibition of BLA; anxiety-like behaviour

claims.text: Mice transgenically expressing the human endogenous retrovirus type W envelope protein showed downregulation of Shank3 among other autism and schizophrenia risk genes in hippocampus, together with increased LSD1 activity, and oral LSD1 inhibition with ORY-1001 normalised H3K4 methylation and rescued behavioural and cognitive deficits.
claims.limO: No n, no fold changes, no adjusted p values. Shank3 is one of several downregulated genes named from a genome-wide screen, so its selection for mention is not independent of the result. The behavioural rescue is not attributed to Shank3 restoration and this record must not be read as showing that an LSD1 inhibitor raises SHANK3 expression in PMS; whether Shank3 transcript recovered under ORY-1001 is not stated.
claims.model: not_applicable for SHANK3; transgenic mice expressing human HERV-W ENV
claims.measure: genome-wide RNA sequencing of hippocampal tissue; LSD1 enzymatic activity; H3K4 mono-, di- and tri-methylation; behavioural and cognitive tests

claims.text: Mice carrying the neuroligin-3 R617W mutation showed significantly reduced expression of the postsynaptic scaffolding proteins PSD95 and SHANK3 and a significantly reduced number of excitatory synapses in hippocampal CA1, CA3 and sensory cortex.
claims.eff: p < 0.05 for the scaffolding protein reduction and p < 0.01 for the synapse number reduction; no effect sizes and no confidence intervals
claims.limO: p values only, with no effect sizes, no confidence intervals and no sample sizes, across a large number of measures with no stated correction. Western blot quantification of SHANK3 is not isoform-resolved.
claims.model: not_applicable for SHANK3; NL3 R617W knock-in mouse
claims.measure: PSD95 and SHANK3 protein by Western blot; excitatory synapse number by confocal microscopy

claims.text: The neuroligin-3 R617W mutation did not affect neuroligin-3 expression at the cell membrane, its intracellular distribution, or endoplasmic reticulum retention, while it did reduce the interaction with neurexin 1 and the expression of VGluT I.
claims.limO: This null is reported WITHOUT a statistical test, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and immunofluorescence localisation is a weak assay for excluding a trafficking defect. It carries the argument that the mutation acts through binding rather than through trafficking, which that evidence cannot settle. Relevance to SHANK3 is contextual only.
claims.model: not_applicable; 293T cells expressing NL3 R617W
claims.measure: immunofluorescence of membrane and intracellular NL3; co-immunoprecipitation with neurexin 1; synaptic marker expression

claims.text: Adult Shank3 knockout mice showed a 39% increase in IBA1 expression in the central nucleus of the amygdala and a 13% increase in microglial density in the caudal pontine reticular nucleus.
claims.eff: 39% increase in IBA1 in CeA, p = 0.01; 13% increase in microglial density in PnC, p = 0.02. No confidence intervals and no sample sizes reported.
claims.limA: The authors describe the alterations as moderate and possibly circuit-dependent rather than global, and call for further investigation.
claims.limO: Percentage changes and p values without confidence intervals or sample sizes. Six regions and at least four measures were examined, so roughly two dozen comparisons; p values of 0.01 and 0.02 would not survive correction for that number, and the abstract reports no correction. A 13% density difference is within the range that immunofluorescence counting methods can produce from sectioning and thresholding differences alone.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse; allele and exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: microglial density, morphology and fluorescence intensity of IBA1 and CD68 by immunofluorescence microscopy

claims.text: No evidence of robust microglial activation was found in Shank3 knockout mice: there were no morphological changes and no alterations in CD68 expression across any of the six examined brain regions.
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistics, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals are given for the null, in contrast to the positive findings in R-1063 which carry p values
claims.limA: The authors conclude that the alterations are moderate and may be circuit-dependent rather than a global phenomenon.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT any reported test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, although the companion positive findings in the same paper are given with p values. That asymmetry matters: the study was evidently powered well enough to detect a 13% density difference, which makes the CD68 null somewhat more informative than most in this batch, but no formal equivalence test or bound is reported, so it still cannot establish the absence of microglial activation. Morphological assessment is also the least sensitive of the available measures. Qualified as 'no evidence of ROBUST activation', which is a weaker statement than no activation.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse; allele not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: microglial morphology and CD68 fluorescence intensity by immunofluorescence microscopy

claims.text: People with PMS aged 3-32 years have quantitatively distinctive craniofacial features compared with age- and sex-matched typically developing people, comprising an elongated face, pointed chin, flattened midface and nasal expansion.
claims.n: 100 children and young adults with PMS; 536 typically developing comparison subjects
claims.limA: The authors state that facial dysmorphology assessment is subjective and that a typical PMS facial phenotype has not previously been well characterised.
claims.limO: Controls come from an external resource (FaceBase consortium) rather than being recruited alongside the cases, so acquisition and device differences cannot be excluded from the abstract. No effect size, test statistic or confidence interval is given for the group contrast.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: craniofacial shape, 3D morphometrics analysed by PCA, Procrustes MANOVA and canonical variates analysis

claims.text: Although the PMS group differs from matched controls, individual variation is the greatest single contributor to facial variation in the sample.
claims.n: 100 children and young adults with PMS; 536 typically developing comparison subjects
claims.limA: The authors frame this as a qualification of the group-level finding, and propose pairing craniofacial assessment with genotype.
claims.limO: This is a null for the practical question — whether facial morphometrics could discriminate at the level of an individual — and no quantitative partition of variance, no test statistic and no confidence interval is reported for it in the abstract. No power analysis is reported, so this cannot be read as evidence that a usable individual-level signal is absent, only that none was demonstrated here.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: partition of facial shape variance between group membership and individual variation

claims.text: In a cohort of 213 individuals with PMS, deletion size within 22q13.3 is a major determinant of phenotype, with larger deletions associated with more severe global functional impairment.
claims.limA: The authors present the additional loci as candidate genes whose putative interactions were explored, not as established contributors.
claims.limO: No effect size, test statistic or confidence interval accompanies the deletion-size association in the abstract. GFAP is an instrument developed by the same group, so the exposure and the outcome are not independently derived.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: deletion size against Global Functional Assessment of the Patient (GFAP), unsupervised clustering

claims.text: SHANK3 does not account for the full phenotypic spectrum of PMS; CERK, TBC1D22A, CELSR1 and GRAMD4 are proposed as additional candidate genes within 22q13.3 contributing to core PMS phenotypes.
claims.limA: Described as candidate genes with putative interactions; the authors call for patient stratification and precision medicine rather than asserting causation.
claims.limO: This is phrased as a negative about SHANK3's explanatory sufficiency, but no null hypothesis test of SHANK3-only explanation is reported, and no statistic, power calculation or confidence interval supports it in the abstract. It should not be cited as a demonstrated limit on SHANK3's contribution.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: candidate gene identification within 22q13.3 against clinical phenotype

claims.text: A young male with PMS features carried two de novo pathogenic frameshift variants, one in SHANK3 and one in SRCAP, and presented with recurrent neuropsychiatric symptoms and developmental regression diagnosed as antibody-negative autoimmune encephalitis that improved after immunomodulatory treatment.
claims.limA: The authors note that SRCAP and SHANK3 phenotypes overlap in intellectual, speech, behavioural and psychiatric features.
claims.limO: A single case with two co-occurring de novo pathogenic variants: the SHANK3 contribution cannot be separated from the SRCAP contribution. The autoantibody result is negative, which is a diagnostic null rather than a research null, and no test of association with SHANK3 is attempted. Response to immunomodulation in one unblinded case carries no control for natural course.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: clinical course, whole-exome sequencing, cerebrospinal fluid white cell count

claims.text: Children with PMS show a distinct faecal microbiota composition compared with age-matched healthy controls, including lower abundance of Faecalibacterium and Agathobacter, and reduced short-chain fatty acid levels.
claims.n: not_reported (numbers of PMS children and of controls are not given in the abstract)
claims.limA: The authors present the work as suggesting potential avenues for microbiota-targeted therapies, not as establishing a mechanism.
claims.limO: Neither group size is stated in the abstract, so the study cannot be weighed at all from this record. No correction for multiple comparisons is described across a 16S dataset, where it is essential.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: faecal bacterial composition by 16S rRNA gene sequencing; short-chain fatty acids by gas chromatography

claims.text: Several pro-inflammatory cytokines were higher in the PMS group than in healthy controls, but the differences were not statistically significant.
claims.n: not_reported (numbers of PMS children and of controls are not given in the abstract)
claims.limA: The authors report the direction of the difference while stating that it did not reach significance, and do not build on it in the conclusion.
claims.limO: No test statistic, no p value, no confidence interval and no power calculation are reported, and the sample size itself is absent from the abstract. This null is therefore not evidence of absence of an inflammatory difference in PMS: with an unknown and probably small paediatric rare-disease sample, a real effect of the size suggested by the reported direction could easily have been missed. It should be read as an underpowered non-significant trend, and cited only as such.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: faecal cytokine levels by multiplex cytokine assay

claims.text: Ribosomal protein Rpl3 and overall protein synthesis are downregulated in the cortex and striatum of Shank3 knockout mice and in neurons differentiated from iPSCs of a person with PMS.
claims.limA: The authors state that mechanisms other than synaptic dysfunction through which Shank3 regulates neuronal function remain unclear.
claims.limO: Neither sample sizes nor sex of the animals are reported in the abstract, and the hiPSC work rests on a single patient line with no isogenic control described.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse; targeted exons and affected isoforms not specified in the abstract. Also hiPSC-derived neurons from a PMS patient.
claims.measure: Rpl3 expression and global protein synthesis

claims.text: Chronic treatment with the mGlu5 positive allosteric modulator VU0409551 rescues Rpl3 expression and protein synthesis and produces long-lasting improvement of behavioural deficits in Shank3 knockout mice.
claims.limA: The authors propose the mechanism as accounting 'at least in part' for the behavioural alterations.
claims.limO: No group sizes, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals in the abstract; sex not stated, which matters because Shank3 phenotypes are reported to be sex-sensitive. No preregistration and no blinding described for the behavioural readouts.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse; targeted exons not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: Rpl3 expression, global protein synthesis, excessive grooming and other behavioural deficits

claims.text: In 17 unrelated Israeli individuals with PMS, all had global developmental delay or intellectual disability, with autism spectrum disorder in 70%, seizures in 47%, sleep difficulties in 76% and bowel movement disorders in 76%.
claims.eff: proportions as stated; no confidence intervals reported
claims.limA: The authors present the series as adding to knowledge of manifestations and symptomatic treatment in Israel and as infrastructure for future clinical trials.
claims.limO: Seventeen individuals ascertained at a single centre, all of Jewish descent, so the proportions carry wide and unreported uncertainty and are not generalisable. No confidence interval accompanies any proportion.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: clinical, demographic and genetic evaluation at a single medical centre

claims.text: Various symptomatic treatments, including full-spectrum cannabidiol oil extracts, were used in this cohort with variable results.
claims.n: not_reported (number treated is not broken out of the 17)
claims.limA: The authors describe the results as variable and do not claim efficacy.
claims.limO: Uncontrolled, unblinded, retrospective observation within a clinical series. No numbers treated, no outcome instrument, no statistical test and no confidence interval. 'Variable results' is not a null result and must not be cited as evidence either for or against cannabidiol in PMS.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: clinician-reported symptom response

claims.text: Aortic root dilation was present in 8 of 59 participants (14%) with PMS in a multisite observational natural history study.
claims.limA: The authors note that literature on cardiovascular abnormalities in PMS is currently limited.
claims.limO: No comparison with a non-PMS reference population is reported, so the 14% cannot be read as an excess over background without external norms. No confidence interval on the proportion.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: aortic root measurement on echocardiography

ref.venue: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A

claims.text: Aortic root dilation was significantly associated with larger chromosome 22 deletions, confirming the study's a priori hypothesis, and participants with aortic root dilation had significantly more deleted genes.
claims.n: 59 participants, of whom 8 with aortic root dilation
claims.eff: p = 0.047 for the deletion-size association; p = 0.013 for number of genes deleted; no effect estimate and no confidence interval reported
claims.limA: The authors frame the result as potentially aiding identification of individuals at higher risk, not as established risk stratification.
claims.limO: Eight events. The association is reported at p = 0.047, which is a boundary result on a single prespecified split with no effect estimate and no confidence interval, and it should not be treated as a settled finding. The deletion-size cutpoint is stated as a priori, which is unusually good practice for this literature and is worth noting; formal preregistration is not claimed.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: presence of aortic root dilation against deletion size and against number of genes deleted

ref.venue: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A

claims.text: Shank3 heterozygous mice show altered structural plasticity of dendritic spines in response to long-term depression and a heterosynaptic response in neighbouring spines.
claims.limA: The authors frame the findings as suggesting that Shank3 haploinsufficiency induces synaptic alterations during postnatal development that affect memory in adulthood.
claims.limO: No numbers of spines, cells, cultures or animals in the abstract, and no effect sizes or confidence intervals. Organotypic culture is not intact circuitry, so generalisation to in vivo plasticity is an assumption.
claims.model: Shank3+/- mouse, heterozygous loss of one copy; targeted exons not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: dendritic spine volume change after plasticity induction, two-photon imaging and glutamate uncaging

claims.text: Increased GluN2B expression and larger NMDA receptor currents underlie the altered plasticity in Shank3 heterozygous mice and may influence object recognition memory.
claims.limA: The authors use the hedged verb 'may influence' for the link to memory.
claims.limO: The causal link from receptor composition to object recognition is asserted, not tested by manipulation, in what the abstract reports. No group sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals.
claims.model: Shank3+/- mouse; targeted exons not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: GluN2B expression, NMDA receptor currents, novel object recognition test

claims.text: Extracellular vesicles derived from SHANK3 mutant human iPSC cortical neurons transferred hyperexcitability and accelerated maturation phenotypes to control neurons.
claims.limA: The authors attribute the cargo enrichment to known actin cytoskeletal dysregulation driven by SHANK3 deficiency.
claims.limO: No line numbers, replicate counts, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. Whether isogenic controls were used is not stated, which is the decisive methodological question for any iPSC comparison.
claims.model: human iPSC-derived cortical neurons with SHANK3 mutation; variant not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: neuronal excitability and maturation; proteomic analysis of vesicle cargo

claims.text: Extracellular vesicles derived from control neurons failed to rescue the phenotypes of SHANK3 mutant neurons.
claims.limA: The authors offer a post hoc explanation, that control vesicles have decreased enrichment of synaptic proteins, flagged by their own word 'likely'.
claims.limO: No statistical test, no equivalence or non-inferiority analysis, no power calculation and no confidence interval is reported for this failure to rescue. It therefore does not establish that control-neuron vesicles have no effect, only that none was detected in an experiment of unstated size. The proteomic explanation is offered after the fact and is not itself tested.
claims.model: human iPSC-derived cortical neurons, SHANK3 mutant and control; variants not specified
claims.measure: neuronal excitability and maturation after vesicle transfer

claims.text: Extracellular vesicles from mesenchymal stem cells and healthy donor iPSCs rescued hyperexcitability and normalised maturation in SHANK3 mutant neurons, and intranasal administration of iPSC-derived vesicles rescued ASD-like behavioural deficits in Shank3B-/- mice.
claims.limA: The authors present this as revealing a novel mechanism and emphasise therapeutic potential.
claims.limO: Shank3B-/- is homozygous and so does not model the heterozygous dosage of PMS. No group sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals; no blinding or randomisation described for the behavioural outcomes. A single laboratory, not replicated.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mouse, homozygous; plus human iPSC-derived SHANK3 mutant cortical neurons
claims.measure: neuronal excitability and maturation in vitro; ASD-like behavioural deficits in mice

claims.text: Nine CELSR1 variants predicted to cause loss of function were identified in a primary lymphoedema cohort, and eight carriers had a kidney anomaly, most often ureteropelvic junction obstruction.
claims.n: 742 index patients exome sequenced; 9 variants identified; 8 carriers with kidney anomaly
claims.eff: penetrance 87% in females versus 20% in males, described as statistically significant; no test statistic or confidence interval reported
claims.limA: The authors state that CELSR1 'may be' the long-sought gene for the renal defects, and present the association as a suggestion.
claims.limO: Nine variants and eight renal events. No formal association test against a control group for the renal phenotype is described, and no confidence interval accompanies the penetrance figures. The link to PMS is an inference by the authors, not a measurement in anyone with PMS.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: exome sequencing; clinical lymphoedema and renal phenotype

claims.text: Four of the CELSR1 loss-of-function variants were tested for nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and none was observed.
claims.limA: The authors note that most truncated CELSR1 proteins would lack the transmembrane domain, if produced, which is itself conditional.
claims.limO: A null in four variants, with no test statistic, no detection threshold, no power calculation and no confidence interval reported. With n = 4 and an assay of unstated sensitivity, absence of detected decay is not evidence that decay does not occur; it is an undersized negative that should be cited only as 'not detected in four variants'.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: presence of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay of the mutant transcript

claims.text: Sleep disturbances were present in 64.3% of a cohort of 56 individuals with PMS, the most common being waking during the night (39%).
claims.eff: 64.3% overall; 39% waking during the night; no confidence intervals reported
claims.limA: The authors present the data as helpful for recognising and managing sleep disturbances and for identifying candidate genes and biomarkers.
claims.limO: Caregiver questionnaire without objective sleep measurement such as actigraphy or polysomnography. No comparison group. No confidence intervals on any proportion.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: sleep disturbance by standardised observer or caregiver questionnaire

claims.text: Sleep disturbances were more prevalent in individuals with a SHANK3 pathogenic variant (89%) than in individuals with 22q13.3 deletions of any size (59.6%).
claims.n: 56 individuals, split between variant and deletion groups of unstated size
claims.eff: 89% versus 59.6%; no test statistic and no confidence interval reported
claims.limA: The authors use the difference to argue that SHANK3 is the main candidate gene for this manifestation.
claims.limO: The sizes of the two genotype groups are not given, and the 89% figure is almost certainly based on a small number of individuals with sequence variants. No test, no confidence interval and no power calculation accompany the comparison, so the difference is a descriptive contrast and not a demonstrated association.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: prevalence of sleep disturbance by genotype group

claims.text: In Shank3 exon 4-22 knockout mice, quantal mEPSC amplitudes and AMPA receptor responses to photo-uncaged glutamate are increased at cerebellar mossy fibre to granule cell synapses, with faster decay kinetics, inward rectification and increased IEM-1460 sensitivity indicating a higher proportion of calcium-permeable AMPA receptors.
claims.limA: The authors note that Shank3 function in the cerebellum has been little studied compared with forebrain regions.
claims.limO: Homozygous knockout of exons 4-22 removes all major isoforms, which is a more complete loss than PMS haploinsufficiency. No cell or animal numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract, and sex is not reported.
claims.model: homozygous Shank3 delta-exon4-22 knockout mouse, full-length isoform deletion
claims.measure: miniature and evoked EPSC amplitude and kinetics; GluA2 and GluA4 immunohistochemistry

claims.text: Shank3 exon 4-22 knockout mice have less ramified microglia in the cerebellar cortex than control mice in early adulthood.
claims.limA: The authors describe the finding as suggesting a shift in microglial morphological state and as a possible contributing mechanism.
claims.limO: Morphology alone, with no functional microglial measure. No animal numbers, no effect size, no confidence interval, sex not reported.
claims.model: homozygous Shank3 delta-exon4-22 knockout mouse
claims.measure: microglial morphology by IBA1 immunohistochemistry

claims.text: Lithium chloride and carbamazepine had no effect on the visual motor response in either shank3 zebrafish model or in wild-type fish.
claims.n: not_reported (larvae per condition not stated in the abstract)
claims.limA: The authors conclude that drug effects on sensory processing are highly genotype- and drug-dependent.
claims.limO: No test statistic, no confidence interval and no power calculation are reported for either null, and the number of larvae per condition is not stated. A single concentration and a single 24-hour exposure window cannot exclude an effect at another dose or duration. This is not evidence that lithium or carbamazepine are inert on sensory processing; it is a non-detection in one assay of unstated size.
claims.model: zebrafish shank3ab mutants with frameshift mutations at the N-terminus and at the C-terminus; wild-type comparison
claims.measure: visual motor response, locomotion during four ten-minute light-to-dark transition cycles

claims.text: The mGlu5 antagonist MPEP reduced the visual motor response in wild-type zebrafish to the level seen in shank3 mutants but produced no change in either shank3 mutant model.
claims.limA: The authors note that MPEP is a drug tested in rodent models of PMS rather than prescribed to patients, and conclude that drug effects are genotype-dependent.
claims.limO: No statistic, no confidence interval and no power calculation for the null in the mutants, and no larval numbers. A floor effect is a live alternative explanation the abstract does not exclude: the mutants already have a reduced response, and MPEP lowers the wild-type response to that same level, so there may have been no room left to detect a decrease. The null therefore cannot be read as showing that mGlu5 antagonism is inactive in shank3 mutants.
claims.model: zebrafish shank3ab mutants, N-terminal and C-terminal frameshift lines; wild-type comparison
claims.measure: visual motor response, locomotion across light-to-dark transitions

claims.text: Risperidone normalised the visual motor response in shank3 zebrafish models, and shank3 mutants were resistant to the hyperactivity induced in wild-type fish by pentylenetetrazol.
claims.limA: The authors conclude that effects on sensory processing vary in ways that are highly genotype- and drug-dependent.
claims.limO: No larval numbers, effect sizes, confidence intervals or multiplicity correction across four compounds and three genotypes. Normalisation of a light-to-dark locomotor response is a long way from the sensory experience of a child, and should not be presented to families as support for risperidone.
claims.model: zebrafish shank3ab mutants, N-terminal and C-terminal frameshift lines
claims.measure: visual motor response; locomotor response to pentylenetetrazol

claims.text: Seizures were present in 41% of 98 individuals with PMS in a prospective longitudinal study, and their presence was associated with significantly lower adaptive and intellectual functioning.
claims.eff: not_reported; described as statistically significant, with no coefficients or confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors state that a larger cohort might identify additional associations with medical features.
claims.limO: Cross-sectional association within a longitudinal cohort; direction of causation is not established, since more severely affected individuals may be more likely to have seizures. No regression coefficients and no confidence intervals in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: seizure presence, type and age of onset against VABS-II Adaptive Behavior Composite and best-estimate full-scale IQ, multiple linear regression

claims.text: Seizure prevalence did not differ across genetic classes in PMS, although participants with 22q13 deletions and seizures had more genes included in their deletions than those with deletions and no seizures.
claims.n: 98 individuals, of whom 41% with seizures; group sizes per genetic class not reported
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistic, p value or confidence interval given in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors describe the genotype-phenotype analyses as discrepant and suggest that deletion size must be taken into account to detect genotype-phenotype relationships.
claims.limO: A chi-square test is described as having been performed, but no statistic, p value, confidence interval or power calculation is reported, and the number of participants in each genetic class is not given. With 98 participants split across classes, the comparison is almost certainly underpowered for anything but a large difference, so this null is not evidence that seizure risk is equal across genetic classes. The deletion-size result in the same sentence points the other way, which the authors themselves call discrepant.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: seizure prevalence by genetic class, chi-square; number of genes deleted in deletion carriers with and without seizures

claims.text: No associations were found between the presence of seizures and sex, history of pre- or neonatal complications, features manifesting in early infancy, or medical features.
claims.limA: The authors state that a larger cohort might be able to identify additional associations with medical features, which is an explicit acknowledgement that these nulls may reflect sample size.
claims.limO: A battery of exploratory comparisons with no reported test statistics, p values, confidence intervals, power calculation or multiplicity handling. Roughly 40 participants with seizures gives little power for anything but a large association, and the authors say so themselves. These nulls are the ordinary noise of a wide screen and carry no evidential weight either way.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: chi-square tests and t-tests of seizure presence against demographic, perinatal, early-infancy and medical features

claims.text: In the PMS Foundation International Registry, 284 of 384 individuals (73.4%) with confirmed 22q13 deletions or SHANK3 pathogenic variants had a sleep disturbance, and prevalence rose with age from 56% at 0-3 years to 90% above 18 years.
claims.eff: 73.4% overall; 56% at 0-3 years rising to 90% over 18 years; no confidence intervals reported
claims.limA: The authors note that sleep disturbances in neurodevelopmental disorders are not well studied and that little research has addressed parents' concern about them.
claims.limO: Registry data are self-selected and caregiver-reported, with no objective sleep measurement and no control group. The age gradient is cross-sectional, so it cannot distinguish worsening with age from cohort or reporting effects. No confidence intervals.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: caregiver-reported sleep disturbance recorded in a patient registry

claims.text: Sleep disturbances were similarly frequent among individuals with SHANK3 pathogenic variants (84.8%) and individuals with 22q13 deletions (71.9%), which the authors take as supporting a role for SHANK3 haploinsufficiency in sleep.
claims.n: 384 individuals in total; sizes of the two genotype groups not reported
claims.eff: 84.8% versus 71.9%; no test statistic, p value or confidence interval reported
claims.limA: The authors draw a positive conclusion from the similarity, namely support for the role of SHANK3 haploinsufficiency.
claims.limO: This is an absence of a difference being used as positive evidence for a mechanism, and it is reported without any test, confidence interval or power calculation, and without the sizes of the two groups. A 13-percentage-point gap called 'similar' is not an equivalence result: no equivalence margin was set and none could be met at these unstated group sizes. The inference from this null to SHANK3 haploinsufficiency is not supported by what is reported.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: prevalence of caregiver-reported sleep disturbance by genotype group

claims.text: Individuals with PMS show atypical sensory features on the Short Sensory Profile-2, with high scores in the avoiding and seeking domains.
claims.n: 41 patients with PMS and 24 patients with SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability
claims.limA: The authors propose sensory measurements as potential clinical endpoints for trials of novel therapeutics in these populations.
claims.limO: No comparison with a typically developing or non-syndromic autism group is reported, so 'atypical' rests on instrument norms rather than on a matched contrast. No effect sizes or confidence intervals, and no age or sex composition.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Short Sensory Profile-2, sub-scores for seeking, avoiding, sensitivity and registration plus overall sensory and behaviour scores

claims.text: Both PMS and SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability groups showed the same pattern of atypical sensory features, with no distinguishing sensory phenotype reported between them.
claims.n: 41 with PMS and 24 with SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability
claims.limA: The authors state at the outset that it is not known whether syndromic autism disorders have unique sensory phenotypes, and their conclusion reports a shared pattern rather than a distinguishing one.
claims.limO: No direct statistical comparison between the two syndromes is reported in the abstract, so the absence of a distinguishing phenotype is an absence of reporting rather than a demonstrated null. With 41 and 24 participants, no test statistic, no confidence interval and no power calculation, any between-syndrome difference short of a large one would have been undetectable. This must not be cited as showing that sensory profiles cannot distinguish PMS from other syndromic intellectual disability.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: between-syndrome comparison of Short Sensory Profile-2 sub-scores

claims.text: The biological activity of the IGFBP2-mimetic peptide JB2 involves NMDA receptor activation, gene transcription and translation and IGF2 receptors, and is not dependent on the IGF1 receptor.
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: This is a mechanistic null stated as a bare sentence. No statistical test is reported, no power calculation or minimum detectable effect is given, and no confidence interval is attached. A null of this kind cannot establish that IGF1R plays no part; it establishes only that no IGF1R dependence was detected under the conditions used, which are not described in the abstract. Neither the blocking agent nor the concentration is stated, so an inadequate blockade cannot be ruled out. Read as absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.
claims.model: cultured neurons and mice; the Shank3 heterozygous line used for the in vivo work is not identified by allele or exon in the abstract
claims.measure: dependence of JB2 effects on receptor identity, pharmacological/mechanistic dissection; readouts not specified in the abstract

claims.text: JB2 rescued deficits in synaptic function and plasticity, learning and memory, ultrasonic vocalisations and motor function, and normalised neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility, in a Shank3 heterozygous mouse.
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: A multi-domain rescue claim with no effect size, no p value, no confidence interval and no sample size for any single domain. The word rescued is used for every outcome without distinguishing partial from complete normalisation. The number of comparisons implied is large and no correction for multiple testing is mentioned. Sex is not stated, which matters because the batch contains a Shank3 study reporting sex-specific behavioural effects.
claims.model: Shank3 heterozygous mouse; allele, exons and isoform affected not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: battery of synaptic, electrophysiological and behavioural readouts, described in the abstract only as synaptic function and plasticity, learning and memory, ultrasonic vocalisations, motor function, neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility

claims.text: JB2 rescued deficits in auditory evoked response latency, alpha peak frequency and the steady-state electroencephalography response in a Shank3 heterozygous mouse.
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: No effect size, no confidence interval, no sample size. The translational value asserted for these measures is an argument, not a result: the abstract does not report that the same measures were compared against human PMS data. Treat the translational claim as the authors' framing rather than as evidence.
claims.model: Shank3 heterozygous mouse; allele not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: auditory evoked response latency, alpha peak frequency and steady-state EEG response

claims.text: On the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire, both Phelan-McDermid syndrome and SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability showed significant sleep abnormalities compared with unaffected siblings, with SYNGAP1-related intellectual disability more severely affected than Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
claims.n: 47 individuals with PMS, 64 with SYNGAP1-related ID, 61 unaffected siblings
claims.eff: not_reported; described as significant, with no test statistic, p value or confidence interval in the abstract
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: The comparison group is unaffected siblings aged 1-17 while the affected groups extend to 46 and 64 years, so the age ranges do not overlap across most of their span and an age-confounded comparison cannot be excluded from the abstract. CSHQ is a caregiver questionnaire validated in typically developing children; its use in profound intellectual disability is not validated in the abstract. No effect size and no confidence interval.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ), caregiver report

claims.text: Within Phelan-McDermid syndrome, sleep disturbance was more severe in individuals aged 11 years and older than in those under 11, and individuals with either synaptopathy were more likely than unaffected siblings to use sleep aids.
claims.n: 47 individuals with PMS, split at age 11; subgroup sizes not reported
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: The age split at 11 years is not justified in the abstract and may be post hoc; no correction for multiple comparisons is mentioned. Subgroup sizes are absent, so this age contrast is drawn from fewer than 47 individuals per cell. No confidence interval, no effect size.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: CSHQ total and subscale scores by age band; reported use of sleep aids

claims.text: Autism spectrum disorder diagnoses did not differ between individuals with Class I 22q13 deletions, Class II deletions and SHANK3 sequence variants in a cohort of 170 individuals with Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
claims.n: 170 individuals with PMS; group sizes not reported in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistic, p value or confidence interval is given for the ASD comparison
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: This null carries none of the three things that would make it evidence of absence: no test statistic, no power calculation or minimum detectable difference, and no confidence interval. The asymmetry of reporting is conspicuous, since every positive contrast in the same abstract is stated as a difference while this one is stated as an absence. Group sizes are not given, so the comparison could rest on a small sequence-variant subgroup. At 170 individuals this is the largest cohort in the batch and the null is correspondingly more informative than most, but it still establishes only that no difference was detected.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: autism spectrum disorder diagnosis, derived from prospective direct evaluation, caregiver interview, questionnaires and medical history

claims.text: Individuals with Class I deletions or SHANK3 sequence variants had fewer delayed developmental milestones and higher cognitive ability than those with Class II deletions, but had more skill regressions.
claims.n: 170 individuals with PMS; group sizes not reported
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: No effect sizes, p values or confidence intervals in the abstract. Regression is ascertained partly by caregiver report and is subject to recall and to a floor effect: a person with higher baseline ability has more skills available to lose, which could generate the regression difference without any genotype-specific mechanism. Cognitive ability measured across a cohort with severe to profound impairment is subject to floor effects in the opposite direction.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: developmental milestone attainment, cognitive ability and reported skill regression, from direct evaluation, caregiver interview, questionnaires and medical history

claims.text: Individuals with Class II 22q13 deletions were more likely to have renal abnormalities, spine abnormalities and ataxic gait, while those with Class I deletions or SHANK3 sequence variants were more likely to carry psychiatric diagnoses including bipolar disorder, depression and schizophrenia.
claims.n: 170 individuals with PMS; group sizes not reported
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: A long list of medical and psychiatric features is compared across three genotype groups with no stated correction for multiple testing and no effect sizes. Psychiatric diagnosis in people with limited expressive language is ascertainment-dependent, and the group reported to carry more psychiatric diagnoses is also the group reported to have higher cognitive ability and more language, which is an obvious route to differential ascertainment rather than differential prevalence.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: medical history and psychiatric diagnosis, from prospective evaluation and caregiver interview

claims.text: Among 21 cases diagnosed with Phelan-McDermid syndrome at a single Chinese centre, 13 carried a 22q13.2-q13.33 deletion ranging from 69 kb to 9.06 Mb and five carried a pathogenic variant or an intragenic deletion in SHANK3, with three familial cases attributable to a parental balanced translocation.
claims.n: 21 cases (7 prenatal, 14 postnatal) at one centre
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: A single-centre consecutive case series with no comparison group; percentages in the abstract (62.5 per cent deletions, 37.5 per cent variants, 6.7 per cent familial) are computed over very small denominators and should not be read as population frequencies. The deletion and variant counts given do not sum to the 21 cases stated, so the breakdown cannot be reconciled from the abstract alone.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: genetic diagnosis by conventional karyotyping, chromosomal microarray analysis and whole exome sequencing

claims.text: The authors propose TNFRSF13C and NFAM1 as candidate haploinsufficient genes for immunological features of Phelan-McDermid syndrome, and TCF20, SULT4A1, PARVB, SCO2 and UPK3A for intellectual and behavioural, neurological, macrocephaly/hypotonia, oculopathy and renal adysplasia features respectively.
claims.n: 21 cases; the genotype-phenotype mapping draws on the 13 cases with a deletion
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: These are gene attributions inferred from interval overlap in 13 deletion cases, without statistical testing, without a control set of deletions and without functional evidence. The abstract presents them as suggested candidates and they should be carried no further than that. The spelling TNFRSFI3C appears in the source text where TNFRSF13C is the approved symbol; recorded here with the approved symbol and the discrepancy flagged.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: mapping of deleted intervals against reported clinical features

claims.text: Children with Phelan-McDermid syndrome showed significantly greater sensory hyporeactivity and fewer hyperreactivity and seeking symptoms on the Sensory Assessment for Neurodevelopmental Disorders than children with idiopathic autism spectrum disorder and typically developing children.
claims.n: 52 children with PMS, 132 with idiopathic ASD, 54 typically developing
claims.eff: not_reported; described as significant, with no test statistic, p value or confidence interval in the abstract
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: Three-group comparison with no effect sizes and no correction for multiple testing stated. The SAND combines clinician observation with caregiver interview, and caregiver report of hyporeactivity in a child with profound intellectual disability and motor impairment is hard to separate from report of reduced responding generally.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Sensory Assessment for Neurodevelopmental Disorders (SAND), clinician-administered observation with corresponding caregiver interview, scored against DSM-5 ASD sensory criteria

claims.text: Sensory reactivity did not differ between children with Class I 22q13 deletions or SHANK3 sequence variants and children with larger Class II deletions.
claims.n: 52 children with PMS; genotype subgroup sizes not reported
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistic, no p value, no confidence interval

It cannot support the inference the authors draw from it. The authors conclude from the absence of a difference that SHANK3 haploinsufficiency is the main driver of the sensory phenotype; that is the classic misuse of a null, since a genotype comparison that is underpowered will fail to detect a contribution from the other deleted genes whether or not one exists. A comparison of this size has power to detect only very large prevalence differences, so the absence of a significant difference is close to uninformative, and chaining ten such nulls into the conclusion that SHANK3 haploinsufficiency is the major contributor to the phenotype is not supported by the data as reported. It is also not possible to tell from the abstract whether the deletion sizes in the sample spanned a wide enough range for a relation to be detectable at all: restricted range alone can produce this result. Two selective-reporting problems should be noted even though neither is itself a null: the inferior longitudinal fasciculus appears in the title but no result for it is given in the abstract, and the stated investigation of trends between autism diagnosis and tract integrity is likewise reported without a result. Both must be recovered from the full text, which is paywalled, before this source is used; an unreported comparison is not a negative result and has not been recorded as one here.

The readout is protein level, not function: no synaptic, electrophysiological or behavioural consequence is reported. Motoneurons are a tractable but phenotypically remote cell type for a disorder of forebrain synapses. The screen is described as systematic but the number of oligonucleotides tested is not given, so the two reported successes cannot be set against the number of failures, which is itself a negative result that the abstract does not quantify.

The phrase little to no changes in most tests is a summary that conceals which tests showed something and which did not. claims.measure: brain expression of autism-associated genes including Shank3; method not stated in the abstract

claims.text: F1 generation mice showed fetal brain expression profiles and adult social behaviour abnormalities that were substantially different from, and milder than, those of the F2 generation.
claims.limO: No test statistic, effect size or confidence interval given for the F1/F2 comparison; 'milder' is an unquantified qualitative statement in the abstract.
claims.model: F1 generation descendants of developmentally thyroid-hormone-overexposed (DIO3-deficient) mice
claims.measure: fetal brain gene expression profile and three-chamber social box test

claims.text: Lentiviral overexpression and knockdown of the Shank3 interaction partner ProSAPiP1 did not alter the formation of pre- or postsynaptic specializations in hippocampal neurons.
claims.limO: A null with no statistical test, no power calculation and no confidence interval reported in the abstract. It therefore does not establish that ProSAPiP1 has no role in synapse formation, only that none was detected at the sensitivity of this experiment. An equivalence or non-inferiority framing would be needed for the authors' word 'dispensable' to be supported.
claims.model: primary cultured hippocampal neurons; lentiviral ProSAPiP1 overexpression and knockdown; species of culture not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: formation of pre- and postsynaptic specializations; method not stated in the abstract

claims.text: ProSAPiP1 regulates SPAR levels at the postsynaptic density and the maturation of dendritic spines in hippocampal neurons.
claims.limO: Direction of the SPAR change and of the spine maturation effect is not stated in the abstract; no effect size or dispersion given.
claims.model: primary cultured hippocampal neurons; lentiviral ProSAPiP1 overexpression and knockdown; species of culture not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: postsynaptic SPAR levels; dendritic spine maturation

claims.text: The GABAergic false neurotransmitter R-4APA at 50 mg/kg worsened startle behaviours in Shank3-deficient mice.
claims.limO: The abstract states worsening without giving the direction of change in startle amplitude, the magnitude, the test, the group sizes or a confidence interval. A harm signal reported this thinly cannot be sized, only flagged.
claims.model: Shank3-/- mouse; allele, targeted exons and affected isoforms not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: startle behaviours

claims.text: Racemic 4APA did not suppress excitotoxicity in hippocampal slices or increase survival in Aldh5a1-/- mice, whereas racemic 2MeGlu suppressed 81% of excitotoxicity and increased survival by 105%.
claims.eff: rac-2MeGlu: 81% suppression of excitotoxicity, 105% increase in survival; rac-4APA: no effect reported, magnitude not quantified
claims.limO: The 4APA null carries no test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval, and the comparator percentages are given without dispersion. The null for 4APA is an absence of detected effect, not demonstrated equivalence to vehicle.
claims.model: hippocampal slices; Aldh5a1-/- mice (SSADH deficiency model of excitation-inhibition imbalance)
claims.measure: excitotoxicity in hippocampal slices; survival

claims.text: The direct interaction between delta-catenin and the Shank3 ankyrin repeat domain was not affected by phosphorylation or palmitoylation of delta-catenin.
claims.limO: A biochemical null with no quantified binding affinity, no statistical test, no power calculation and no confidence interval in the abstract. It cannot exclude a modest modulation of affinity by these modifications; it only shows none was detected.
claims.model: purified synaptic protein fractions, biochemical binding assays and primary cultured neurons; species of culture not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: delta-catenin binding to the Shank3 Ank domain under phosphorylation and palmitoylation

claims.text: In mouse postsynaptic fractions, the absence of SPN-Ank-containing large Shank3 isoforms results in loss of postsynaptic delta-catenin.
claims.limA: The authors state that work in mice and in primary cultured neurons may not faithfully reproduce the situation in human brain neurons, and that the cultured-neuron work was hampered by the lack of a specific antibody for endogenous delta-catenin.
claims.limO: No quantification, sample size or dispersion in the abstract. Isoform-specific: it constrains which SHANK3 isoform a restoration strategy would need to restore, which is why it is kept.
claims.model: mouse lacking SPN-Ank-containing large Shank3 isoforms; allele not named in the abstract
claims.measure: postsynaptic delta-catenin content by analysis of postsynaptic fractions

claims.text: The ASD-associated L68P mutation in the SPN domain of Shank3 significantly increased the interaction of Shank3 with delta-catenin.
claims.eff: reported as significant; magnitude, test statistic and confidence interval not given in the abstract
claims.limO: A gain of interaction for a loss-of-function-associated variant is counter-intuitive and is not explained in the abstract; full text needed before this is cited.
claims.model: expression of Shank3 variants in biochemical assays and primary cultured neurons
claims.measure: Shank3-delta-catenin interaction

claims.text: Homozygous R1117X Shank3 mutant mice showed deficits in sensory gating, motor coordination and pain perception, severe anxiety in a novel environment, and impaired learning and memory.
claims.limO: No effect sizes, test statistics or confidence intervals in the abstract, and no multiple-comparison handling stated for a large behavioural battery. Homozygous, whereas human SHANK3 loss of function is characteristically heterozygous.
claims.model: homozygous R1117X Shank3 mutant mouse (truncating mutation reproducing a patient variant)
claims.measure: battery of behavioural tests: sensory gating, motor coordination, nociception, anxiety, learning and memory, spontaneous fine motor behaviour

claims.text: R1117X Shank3 mutant mice showed hippocampal morphological changes, impaired synaptic transmission and plasticity, and downregulation of glutamatergic receptors, particularly NMDA receptor subtypes.
claims.limO: Which NMDA receptor subunits, by which method, and with what magnitude, is not stated in the abstract. Most published Shank3 work localises the primary deficit to striatum and cortex, so a hippocampal claim should be read as requiring independent replication.
claims.model: homozygous R1117X Shank3 mutant mouse
claims.measure: hippocampal histology; synaptic transmission and plasticity; glutamatergic receptor expression including NMDA receptor subtypes

claims.text: Juvenile Shank3-deficient rats showed sex-specific sleep abnormalities on EEG/EMG, with males exhibiting fragmented sleep and frequent brief arousals and females prolonged wakefulness, and both sexes showing reduced NREM delta power.
claims.limO: No group sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract, and no statement of how the sex-stratified comparisons were corrected. A sex-by-genotype interaction is claimed but no interaction test is reported.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-e11-21 rat, lacking Shank3 protein
claims.measure: sleep architecture and NREM delta power, EEG/EMG recording

claims.text: After six hours of sleep deprivation, Shank3-deficient rats displayed a blunted homeostatic sleep rebound.
claims.limO: No quantification of the rebound deficit, no test and no confidence interval in the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-e11-21 rat
claims.measure: homeostatic sleep rebound following sleep deprivation

claims.text: Clock and Bmal1 mRNA were significantly downregulated in the prefrontal cortex and striatum of Shank3-deficient rats.
claims.eff: reported as significant; magnitude, test statistic and confidence interval not given in the abstract
claims.limO: Method of quantification, time of day of tissue collection and group sizes are not stated. Circadian gene expression is time-of-day dependent, so a single unstated sampling time limits interpretation.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-e11-21 rat
claims.measure: Clock and Bmal1 mRNA levels

claims.text: Remote ischemic preconditioning did not reduce the incidence of perioperative neurocognitive disorder in elderly patients undergoing major surgery (44% in both groups, P = 0.982).
claims.eff: 44% versus 44%, P = 0.982; no risk difference with confidence interval reported in the abstract
claims.limO: The null reports a significance test but no confidence interval on the risk difference and no power calculation or pre-stated minimal clinically important difference. With 120 patients and an event rate of 44%, the trial can exclude only a large effect; it is not evidence of absence of a clinically meaningful one. The identical 44% in both arms is a point estimate, not an equivalence demonstration.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: incidence of perioperative neurocognitive disorder across six neurological tests before and after surgery

claims.text: Serum myeloid differentiation factor 2 and cystatin C did not differ between patients who developed perioperative neurocognitive disorder and those who did not, and did not predict its occurrence.
claims.limO: No test statistic, no confidence interval and no power calculation for this comparison; the abstract states only that there was no significant difference. A null of this kind in roughly 50 cases per group cannot exclude a modest predictive signal and is not evidence of absence.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: serum MD2 and cystatin C concentrations by ELISA, compared between PND and non-PND groups

claims.text: A SHANK3 variant (rs4824145) was among 3877 mutated genes identified exclusively in patients who developed perioperative neurocognitive disorder, in an exploratory whole-genome sequencing analysis.
claims.n: subset of the 120 randomised patients; number sequenced not stated in the abstract
claims.eff: not_reported; no association statistic, odds ratio or confidence interval given for rs4824145
claims.limO: An uncorrected exploratory screen: 3877 genes 'exclusively' mutated in one arm of a small cohort is a count, not an association test, and with no multiple-testing correction, allele frequency or effect estimate the singling out of SHANK3 is hypothesis-generating at best. The authors' concluding sentence that carriers 'may be more susceptible' is not supported by any statistic in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: whole-genome sequencing, genes mutated exclusively in the PND group; KEGG pathway enrichment

claims.text: In one-month-old female mouse offspring exposed prenatally to maternal immune activation, Shank3 levels were decreased and the effect was confined to the cerebellum.
claims.limA: The authors note the study is limited to female offspring and a single postnatal time point.
claims.limO: No magnitude, test statistic, sample size or confidence interval in the abstract. Region-specificity is asserted from a pattern of significant and non-significant results across regions, without an interaction test.
claims.model: maternal immune activation with poly(I:C); genetically normal female offspring
claims.measure: Shank3 protein level among selected synaptic markers; method not stated in the abstract

claims.text: In the same offspring, total Tau levels, Tau phosphorylation at sites other than Ser416, the other synaptic markers examined and Shank3 outside the cerebellum showed no changes.
claims.limO: No test statistics, no power calculation and no confidence intervals for any of the null comparisons. With a single time point, one sex and unstated group sizes, these nulls are not evidence that the pathways are unaffected; the word 'robust' in the abstract is not operationally defined.
claims.model: maternal immune activation with poly(I:C); genetically normal female offspring
claims.measure: total Tau, site-specific Tau phosphorylation, selected synaptic proteins

claims.text: The striosome compartment of Shank3 delta-11 homozygous mice was enlarged and showed much higher GAD65 expression than in wild-type mice, alongside excessive self-grooming and decreased locomotor activity.
claims.limO: No group sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. Wild-type littermates were used as comparators, which is a strength; the striosome/matrix imbalance is described by the authors as a first report, so it is unreplicated.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-11/delta-11 mouse (homozygous deletion of exon 11)
claims.measure: self-grooming and locomotor activity; GAD65 immunolabelling distribution; striatal RNAseq across four brain regions

claims.text: Differentially expressed genes in Shank3 delta-11 mice were identified mainly in the striatum among the four brain regions sequenced.
claims.limO: The near-absence of differentially expressed genes outside the striatum is an unstated null: the abstract gives no counts per region, no false-discovery threshold, no sample sizes and no power consideration. Transcriptomic nulls are particularly sensitive to depth and n, so this cannot be read as evidence that the other regions are transcriptionally unaffected.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-11/delta-11 mouse
claims.measure: RNAseq differential expression per brain region

claims.text: No specific EEG abnormality was found in a clinical cohort of individuals with SHANK3 loss-of-function mutations or 22q13 microdeletions encompassing SHANK3.
claims.n: not_reported; a single-clinic retrospective chart review, cohort size not stated in the abstract
claims.limO: A null with no cohort size, no statistical test, no power calculation and no confidence interval, from a retrospective single-centre chart review of clinically indicated EEGs rather than a standardised protocol. It is therefore not evidence that no SHANK3-specific EEG signature exists; it is evidence that routine clinical EEG review did not reveal one. Referral to a tertiary neurology clinic also biases the cohort towards those with seizures.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: electroencephalography studies reviewed by a board-certified neurophysiologist; seizure semiology, frequency, age of onset and treatment response from chart review

claims.text: EEG abnormalities were present both in individuals with SHANK3 mutations diagnosed with epilepsy and in those with no history of clinical seizure.
claims.limO: No numbers are given for either subgroup, no test and no confidence interval. The claim that EEG abnormality does not discriminate epilepsy status rests on an unquantified overlap.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: presence of EEG abnormality against presence or absence of clinical seizure history

claims.text: No consistent seizure semiology or neuroimaging finding was present in the majority of individuals with SHANK3 mutations, although atypical absence was the most common semiology.
claims.limO: Heterogeneity is asserted without proportions, denominators or any dispersion measure, and without a power calculation that would say how large a consistent subtype could have been missed. Retrospective, single-centre, with neuroimaging performed for clinical rather than research indications.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: seizure semiology, frequency, age of onset, treatment efficacy; neuroimaging reviewed by a paediatric neuroradiologist and a child neurologist

claims.text: Homozygous and heterozygous Shank3 deficiency aggravated LPS-induced hypothermia, serum IL-6 elevation and sepsis mortality in mice, whereas Shank2 and Trpv1 deficiency did not.
claims.limO: The Shank2 and Trpv1 comparisons are reported only as absences of effect, with no test statistic, power calculation or confidence interval, so they establish specificity weakly: a smaller effect in those genotypes would not have been detectable. The heterozygous Shank3 result is the PMS-relevant one and is not separately quantified in the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3 homozygous and heterozygous deficient mice; Shank2-deficient and Trpv1-deficient mice as comparison genotypes; Nav1.8-Cre Shank3 conditional knockout; allele designations not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: core body temperature, serum IL-6 by ELISA, sepsis mortality

claims.text: Shank3-deficient mice had normal basal core body temperature but failed to adjust body temperature after cold or heat perturbation or auricular vagus nerve stimulation.
claims.limO: The baseline null has no test, no power calculation and no confidence interval, so 'normal basal core temperature' is an undetected difference rather than a demonstrated equivalence. The informative content is the contrast between an unremarkable baseline and a deficit under challenge, which the abstract does not test as an interaction.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient mouse; allele not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: core body temperature at baseline and after challenge

claims.text: In silico structural simulation with AlphaFold3 and HADDOCK indicated that gut-microbiota-associated aberrant phosphorylation may remodel SHANK3 conformation and weaken its binding affinity.
claims.eff: not_reported; no docking scores or confidence metrics given in the abstract
claims.limO: Entirely predictive: no experimental validation of the SHANK3 conformational change or of the binding affinity is reported, and the abstract itself hedges with 'may promote' and 'plausible'. No prediction confidence values, no control proteins and no comparison against unphosphorylated baseline are quantified. The wet-lab arm of the paper does not measure SHANK3.
claims.model: AlphaFold3 structure prediction and HADDOCK docking of phosphorylated SHANK3 and SRRM2; accompanying wet-lab work in antibiotic-treated mice receiving faecal microbiota transplantation from children with ASD
claims.measure: predicted SHANK3 conformation and docking binding affinity under phosphorylation

claims.text: Increased S100B levels reduced synaptic SHANK2 and SHANK3 levels in a zinc-dependent manner, with the effect most pronounced early in neuronal development.
claims.limO: No magnitudes, group sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract, and the developmental-stage dependence is asserted rather than tested as an interaction.
claims.model: in vitro neuronal cultures and in utero exposure of mice to elevated S100B; culture species not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: synaptic SHANK2 and SHANK3 protein levels; free zinc

claims.text: Mice exposed in utero to high S100B levels showed reduced brain free zinc and reduced SHANK2, together with hyperactivity, increased stereotypic and abnormal social behaviours and cognitive impairment.
claims.limO: The in vivo result names free zinc and SHANK2 but not SHANK3, although SHANK3 was measured in vitro. Whether SHANK3 was unchanged in vivo or simply not reported cannot be determined from the abstract, and this should not be read as an in vivo null until the full text is checked.
claims.model: mice exposed in utero to elevated S100B
claims.measure: brain free zinc, SHANK2 level, behavioural battery

claims.text: Male mice with Shank3 downregulated in the nucleus accumbens during early postnatal development performed fewer lever presses to gain access to social interaction with an unfamiliar juvenile mouse.
claims.limO: No group sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. A region-restricted, postnatally induced knockdown is a different exposure from constitutive heterozygous SHANK3 loss in PMS, and the abstract does not report knockdown efficiency.
claims.model: Shank3 knockdown targeted to the nucleus accumbens during early postnatal development (Shank3-NAcKD)
claims.measure: lever presses for social access in the social instrumental task

claims.text: The same mice did not develop a preference for the chamber associated with social stimuli in a conditioned place preference task and allocated exploration differently between paired and unpaired chambers.
claims.limO: Absence of a within-group preference is a null tested against zero, not a between-genotype difference, and the abstract reports neither statistic. No power calculation or confidence interval. The unsupervised motif analysis is exploratory and its multiple-comparison handling is not described.
claims.model: Shank3-NAcKD mouse
claims.measure: social conditioned place preference; unsupervised analysis of locomotor motifs

claims.text: Training with background odors improved behavioural performance and neural discriminability of odor mixtures in Shank3B heterozygous mice as it did in wild-type mice.
claims.limO: The absence of a genotype difference in the benefit of training is reported without an interaction test, group sizes, effect size, power calculation or confidence interval. It cannot establish that learning is equally preserved in Shank3B+/- mice, only that no difference was detected.
claims.model: Shank3B+/- mouse (and Cntnap2-/- mouse as a second autism model), with wild-type comparators
claims.measure: target odor recognition performance and neural discriminability of odor mixtures

claims.text: Naive Shank3B heterozygous mice showed greater trial-to-trial neural variability than wild-type mice, and training produced a widespread reduction in olfactory bulb responses to background odors in the autism models but not in wild-type mice.
