claims.limO: No effect sizes, group sizes or confidence intervals. The 'but not in wild-type mice' contrast is drawn from significant versus non-significant results rather than from a tested interaction.
claims.model: Shank3B+/- mouse and Cntnap2-/- mouse, with wild-type comparators
claims.measure: trial-to-trial variability of glomerular calcium responses; response amplitude to background odors

claims.text: Shank1 was expressed in the mouse cochlea but Shank2 and Shank3 expression was not detected there by immunofluorescence and quantitative real-time PCR.
claims.limO: An absence of detection, with no detection limit, no positive control tissue reported in the abstract, no quantitative values and no confidence interval. Antibody and primer sensitivity bound this result entirely: it shows Shank2 and Shank3 were not detected, not that they are absent.
claims.model: wild-type mouse cochlea; Shank1-/- and Shank1+/+ littermates
claims.measure: Shank1, Shank2 and Shank3 expression by immunofluorescence and quantitative real-time PCR

claims.text: Shank1-/- mice showed subtle changes in the morphology and composition of cochlear afferent postsynaptic densities at the 8 kHz region but no differences in auditory brainstem responses at matching or higher frequencies.
claims.limO: The functional null has no power calculation, no confidence interval and no stated detection threshold in dB, so the size of an ABR difference that could have been missed is unknown. Number and localisation of postsynaptic densities were explicitly unchanged, which makes the molecular change small; a null function result on top of a small molecular change is weak evidence either way.
claims.model: Shank1-/- mice compared with Shank1+/+ littermates
claims.measure: postsynaptic density morphology and composition by immunofluorescence; auditory brainstem responses

claims.text: Shank1 was identified in vestibular afferent postsynaptic densities but no differences in vestibular sensory evoked potentials were detected in Shank1-/- mice compared with wild-type littermates.
claims.limO: No test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval. A null evoked-potential result without a sensitivity analysis is not evidence that Shank1 is functionally dispensable in the vestibular periphery.
claims.model: Shank1-/- mice compared with Shank1+/+ littermates
claims.measure: vestibular sensory evoked potentials

claims.text: Agonist-induced internalisation of synaptic mGluR5 was significantly reduced in Shank knockdown hippocampal neurons and was rescued by re-expression of wild-type Shanks but not by mutants unable to bind Homer1b/c, Dynamin2 or Cortactin.
claims.eff: reported as significant; magnitude, test statistic and confidence interval not given in the abstract
claims.limO: The rescue failures with binding-deficient mutants are nulls reported without power or confidence intervals, so they cannot by themselves establish that those interactions are required; expression level of each mutant is not reported in the abstract. The knockdown is of Shank proteins collectively, so the specific contribution of Shank3 cannot be separated.
claims.model: primary cultured hippocampal neurons with Shank knockdown and rescue constructs; species of culture not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: agonist-induced internalisation of synaptic mGluR5; proportion of synapses associated with an endocytic zone

claims.text: A SHANK2 mutation found in autism spectrum disorder similarly disrupted mGluR5 trafficking and the association of synapses with an endocytic zone.
claims.limO: The variant is not identified in the abstract, so it cannot be checked against ClinVar or gnomAD; no quantification is given.
claims.model: primary cultured hippocampal neurons expressing an ASD-associated SHANK2 mutant
claims.measure: mGluR5 internalisation and endocytic zone association

claims.text: Shank3B heterozygous male mice showed reduced vasopressin inputs from the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis to the lateral septum.
claims.limO: No group sizes, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. Male-only, so the generality of the circuit finding is untested.
claims.model: Shank3B+/- mouse
claims.measure: vasopressin inputs from BNST to lateral septum

claims.text: Selective activation of vasopressin receptor 1a or 1b in the lateral septum rescued sociability and social aggression deficits respectively in Shank3B heterozygous male mice.
claims.limO: A rescue claim with no agent named, no dose, no duration, no group size and no confidence interval in the abstract. Acute local receptor activation in adult male mice is a long way from a systemic chronic therapy, and the dissociation between the two receptors rests on two separate comparisons rather than on an interaction test.
claims.model: Shank3B+/- mouse; pharmacological manipulation of AVPR1a and AVPR1b in the lateral septum
claims.measure: sociability and social aggression

claims.text: Parvalbumin-expressing interneurons in the anterior cingulate cortex of Shank3B-/- mice show reduced excitability and in vivo hypoactivity as early as postnatal day 15.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no test statistics, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals appear in the abstract for any comparison. Homozygous null, whereas PMS is a haploinsufficiency; the abstract does not report heterozygotes.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mouse (deletion of the PDZ domain-encoding exons); homozygous
claims.measure: intrinsic excitability (whole-cell recording) and in vivo activity of PVINs

claims.text: The early hypoexcitability of ACC parvalbumin interneurons in Shank3B-/- mice occurs despite normal levels of glutamatergic input to those cells.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT a reported test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals. It is therefore not evidence of absence: with no stated n and no equivalence bound, a real but moderate reduction in glutamatergic drive at P15 cannot be excluded. The word 'normal' in the abstract is an unquantified comparison with wild-type littermates.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mouse; homozygous
claims.measure: glutamatergic synaptic input to PVINs (voltage-clamp recording)

claims.text: At postnatal day 15, layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons in the ACC of Shank3B-/- mice display normal excitability and normal synaptic input while already showing reduced Ih currents.
claims.limO: A mixed record: the Ih reduction is a positive finding, the excitability and synaptic-input results are nulls. The nulls carry NO test statistic, NO power calculation and NO confidence interval, so they do not establish that pyramidal excitability is intact at P15; they establish only that a difference was not detected. The study was evidently sensitive enough to detect an Ih difference in the same cells, which makes the excitability null somewhat more informative than a bare null, but no equivalence bound is reported.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mouse; homozygous
claims.measure: intrinsic excitability, glutamatergic synaptic input, and HCN-mediated Ih current

claims.text: Shank1 knockout mice show altered PSD protein composition, reduced dendritic spine size, smaller and thinner PSDs, and weaker basal synaptic transmission.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, test statistics or confidence intervals in the abstract. Paralogue, not SHANK3: nothing here transfers to PMS without an explicit argument.
claims.model: Shank1 knockout mouse; constitutive
claims.measure: PSD protein composition, spine size and PSD dimensions by electron microscopy, basal synaptic transmission

claims.text: Standard measures of synaptic plasticity were normal in Shank1 knockout mice despite reduced spine size and weaker basal synaptic transmission.
claims.limO: The null is reported WITHOUT any test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and the plasticity protocols are not even named in the abstract. A null stated this way is not evidence of absence of a plasticity phenotype; it is evidence that the protocols used did not detect one. 'Standard measures' is doing a lot of unspecified work.
claims.model: Shank1 knockout mouse; constitutive
claims.measure: long-term potentiation and other standard plasticity protocols (field recordings); specific protocols not named in the abstract

claims.text: Shank1-deficient mice showed enhanced performance in a spatial learning task while their long-term memory retention in the same task was impaired.
claims.limA: The authors frame the result as a differential role for Shank1 in specific cognitive processes rather than a global deficit.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics, no confidence intervals. Acquisition and retention were measured in the same animals in the same task, so the opposing directions are not independent results.
claims.model: Shank1 knockout mouse; constitutive
claims.measure: spatial learning acquisition and long-term retention; task not named in the abstract

claims.text: SHANK3 was one of five candidate biomarkers selected by LASSO regression for coronary artery calcification, but PXDN, not SHANK3, showed the strongest diagnostic performance and was the only candidate carried forward to validation.
claims.n: discovery cohort 8 CAC and 8 controls; validation cohort 6 CAC and 6 controls
claims.eff: PXDN AUC 0.95 (discovery) and 0.83 (validation); no confidence intervals reported. No AUC, effect size or p value is reported for SHANK3 itself.
claims.limO: Very small cohorts (8+8 and 6+6) with samples excluded for quality before analysis. SHANK3 appears only in a candidate list and is then dropped without any reported statistic, so this is not a SHANK3 result in either direction. An AUC of 0.95 from eight cases per group, with no confidence interval, is not a stable estimate.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: differential expression and LASSO-based biomarker selection from transcriptomic datasets; diagnostic value by ROC

ref.venue: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

claims.text: Mice born to mothers with mild zinc deficiency throughout pregnancy displayed increased anxiety, deficits in nest building and in social interaction paradigms, and mild alterations in ultrasonic vocalisations, without any specific genetic susceptibility for autism.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. The link to SHANK biology is asserted through the Neurexin-Neuroligin-Shank pathway and zinc binding by Shank family members, not measured in this study: no Shank protein or transcript result is reported in the abstract.
claims.model: wild-type mice born to dams on a mild zinc-deficient diet through all trimesters; no genetic manipulation
claims.measure: extensive behavioural battery: anxiety, nest building, social interaction paradigms, ultrasonic vocalisation

claims.text: A sex-specific analysis of prenatally zinc-deficient mice revealed only few sex-specific differences in the autism-like behavioural battery.
claims.limO: A null WITHOUT any reported test, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and additionally a null about an interaction, which needs substantially more power than a main effect. Sex-stratified subgroups of an unstated and probably small n cannot support a conclusion of no sex difference. The hedged wording ('only few') is itself uninterpretable without the numbers.
claims.model: wild-type mice prenatally exposed to mild zinc deficiency
claims.measure: sex-stratified comparison across the behavioural battery

claims.text: Shank2 Dex7-/- mice possess an excessive fraction of silent, AMPA-receptor-lacking synapses, a maturation deficit emerging during the third postnatal week that the authors offer as the mechanism for the increased capacity for long-term potentiation in this model.
claims.limA: The authors attribute the divergence between the two lines to possible differences in genetic background and invoke modifier genes.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Genetic background is offered as the explanation for the divergence but is not reported as having been controlled or equalised, so the construct difference (exon 7 versus exons 6-7) and the background difference remain confounded.
claims.model: Shank2 Dex7-/- mouse (deletion of exon 7); compared directly with the independently generated Shank2 Dex6-7-/- line
claims.measure: minimal stimulation estimate of the silent synapse fraction; long-term potentiation in vivo and in vitro

claims.text: A direct comparison of Shank2 Dex7-/- mice with the independently generated Shank2 Dex6-7-/- line showed that the two models have a different set of synaptic phenotypes, and the enhanced synaptic plasticity of the Dex7 line runs contrary to all previous studies of SHANK protein function.
claims.limA: Attributed to possible genetic background differences and to the supposed existence of modifier genes in the expression and inheritance of autism spectrum disorders.
claims.limO: The divergence between lines is asserted from a head-to-head comparison but WITHOUT any statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals in the abstract, and crucially without any formal test of the line-by-genotype interaction, which is the comparison that a claim of different phenotypes actually requires. A failure to find the other line's phenotype here is not, by itself, evidence that the other line's phenotype is absent. Note also the asymmetry: the authors successfully reproduced their OWN earlier result, so this is a between-laboratory discrepancy, not a within-laboratory failure.
claims.model: Shank2 Dex7-/- mouse compared head to head with Shank2 Dex6-7-/- mice generated by a different laboratory
claims.measure: long-term potentiation in vivo and in vitro, and the silent synapse fraction, compared between the two knockout lines

claims.text: Four hours of whole-body hyperthermia significantly reduced compulsive grooming in Shank3B- mice, whereas systemic inflammation induced by bacterial endotoxin suppressed most activities over 5 to 48 hours.
claims.eff: reported as significant with a threshold of p < 0.05; no effect sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals given in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors state plainly that they show behavioural, cellular and molecular changes but provide no specific mechanistic explanation for the observed behavioural improvements. They also note that experimental hyperthermia in patients would carry significant risks.
claims.limO: The abstract reports improvement of repetitive behaviour AND social interaction in C58/J but names only grooming for the Shank3B- line; whether social behaviour was tested and found unchanged in Shank3B- mice cannot be determined from the abstract and is NOT recorded here as a null. Sample sizes absent. A battery of behaviours across two models and two interventions implies many comparisons with no stated correction.
claims.model: Shank3B- mice and, separately, C58/J mice
claims.measure: compulsive grooming, repetitive behaviour and social interaction; brain temperature; inflammatory signatures in brain

claims.text: Only lipopolysaccharide induced inflammatory signatures in the brain and only whole-body hyperthermia produced fever-range hyperthermia, dissociating the temperature component of fever from the inflammatory component as the source of behavioural improvement.
claims.limO: The design yields two nulls by construction (no inflammation after hyperthermia, no fever-range temperature rise after LPS), and neither is accompanied by a test statistic, a power calculation or a confidence interval. Without a sensitivity bound these nulls cannot exclude a smaller inflammatory contribution to the hyperthermia effect. The statistical methods are named (ANOVA, t-tests, Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Whitney) but no result is quantified in the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3B- and C58/J mice
claims.measure: brain inflammatory signatures and brain temperature

claims.text: Thalamocortical neurons in Shank3 mutant mice show hyperexcitability with excessive burst firing and a temporal mismatch with slow cortical rhythms during sleep, and these alterations together with sensory hypersensitivity and sleep fragmentation are causally linked to HCN2 channelopathy.
claims.limO: The allele is not identified in the abstract, which leaves the P3/P4 placement unsettled. Causality is asserted from viral and pharmacological rescue; no sample sizes, statistics or confidence intervals appear in the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant mouse; the specific allele is not named in the abstract
claims.measure: in vivo thalamic unit recording, burst firing, coupling to slow cortical rhythms, sensory responsiveness, sleep architecture

claims.text: Restoring HCN2 function early in postnatal development, by a viral approach or by lamotrigine, ameliorated sensory and sleep problems in Shank3 mutant mice.
claims.limA: The human evidence offered in support is a retrospective case series, which the authors present as supportive rather than confirmatory.
claims.limO: No dose, no duration, no sample size, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. The accompanying human evidence is a retrospective case series of lamotrigine in autism, uncontrolled and not in a PMS population; it is recorded separately and must not be read as a trial result. The rescue is stated to work when given early in development, which is a serious constraint on translation.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant mouse; allele not named in the abstract
claims.measure: sensory hypersensitivity and sleep fragmentation

claims.text: SHANK3 was among the most frequently mutated genes in the primary tumours of regional lymph-node-positive pure mucinous breast cancer, found in three of six cases, and was not detected in the primary tumours of node-negative cases.
claims.n: 166 patients with pure mucinous breast cancer in the clinical series; whole-exome sequencing of 12 primary tumours and 4 positive lymph nodes; the SHANK3 result rests on 6 node-positive tumours
claims.eff: 3 of 6 node-positive primary tumours; no p value, no confidence interval, no multiple-testing correction reported
claims.limA: The authors state that further investigation including multi-omics studies is needed.
claims.limO: A 3-of-6 frequency from an exome-wide scan with no correction for the number of genes tested and no confidence interval. The contrast with node-negative tumours is an absence in an equally small group, reported WITHOUT a test, WITHOUT power and WITHOUT an interval, so it cannot support the claim that these alterations are specific to node-positive disease. Somatic, not germline.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: whole-exome sequencing of primary tumours and lymph nodes; mutation frequency by node status

claims.text: The N-terminal and ankyrin repeat domain of Shank3a/b was predicted to form complexes with 348 proteins, significantly enriched for RNA-binding, spliceosome and ribosome-associated molecules, and the X-linked intellectual disability protein Nono was validated as a Shank3 interactor in mouse brain.
claims.n: 348 interacting proteins predicted (102 RNA-binding, 22 spliceosome, 9 ribosome-associated); number of biological replicates not reported
claims.eff: not_reported; enrichment described as significant without a stated statistic or correction
claims.limO: An affinity-capture interactome from a tagged isolated domain is a list of candidates, not of physiological partners; only one (Nono) is validated. No replicate counts, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Isoform-restricted: NT-Ank is present in Shank3a/b but not in the shorter isoforms, so this does not generalise to all SHANK3 protein in the cell.
claims.model: GFP-tagged Shank3 NT-Ank construct; Shank3a/b-knockout mouse for validation
claims.measure: mass spectrometry-based proteomic interactome; co-immunoprecipitation validation

claims.text: The thalamus of Shank3a/b-knockout mice aberrantly expressed splicing isoforms of the autism-associated genes Nrxn1 and Eif4G1, both before and after kainic acid-induced seizures.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics, no confidence intervals and no dose for the kainic acid. 'Aberrantly expressed' is not given a direction in the abstract, so the record cannot state whether the isoforms increased or decreased. Two genes reported out of an unstated number examined.
claims.model: Shank3a/b-knockout mouse
claims.measure: splicing isoform expression of Nrxn1 and Eif4G1

claims.text: Mice lacking Shank3b show increased levels of inflammation-related molecules in the cerebellum and peripheral blood, together with immune dysfunction in bone marrow and spleen.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Which molecules were measured is not stated. The claim that oxidative stress and inflammation establish the behavioural phenotype is a causal reading of a correlation plus a drug rescue, and N-acetylcysteine is not selective for the proposed pathway.
claims.model: Shank3b-/- mouse
claims.measure: inflammation-related molecules in cerebellum and peripheral blood; immune cell populations in bone marrow and spleen

claims.text: N-acetylcysteine treatment rescued inflammation in the cerebellum and peripheral blood of Shank3b-/- mice, reduced production of pro-inflammatory molecules in bone marrow and spleen, and counteracted social impairment.
claims.limO: No dose, no duration, no route, no sample size, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Only social impairment is reported as rescued; whether repetitive behaviour was tested and did not respond cannot be determined from the abstract and is NOT recorded here as a null. A single compound with broad antioxidant action does not establish that oxidative stress is the causal pathway.
claims.model: Shank3b-/- mouse
claims.measure: inflammatory molecules in cerebellum, peripheral blood, bone marrow and spleen; social behaviour

claims.text: Shank3 knockout mice showed a reduction in the frequency of calcium transients in superior colliculus neurons projecting to the ventral tegmental area, and the interneuronal correlation in these mice correlated with the severity of social deficits.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Allele not named, so the P3/P4 placement cannot be settled. The correlation with social deficit severity is reported without a coefficient or an interval.
claims.model: Shank3-/- mouse; allele not named in the abstract
claims.measure: miniscope calcium imaging of SC-VTA projection neurons; neuronal correlation; intrinsic cellular properties; social orienting

claims.text: In young children with autism spectrum disorder, functional MRI showed a significant decrease in connectivity between the superior colliculus and the ventral tegmental area, and this connectivity correlated with the severity of social deficits.
claims.eff: described as a significant decrease; no effect size, no correlation coefficient and no confidence interval reported in the abstract
claims.limO: No sample size, no age range, no sex distribution and no correction for multiple comparisons reported. Resting-state connectivity between two small subcortical structures is technically demanding and susceptible to motion, particularly in young children, and the abstract says nothing about motion control.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: functional MRI connectivity between superior colliculus and ventral tegmental area; social deficit severity

claims.text: 22q13 deletions were found in 4 of 230 Chinese patients with unexplained intellectual disability (1.7%), a frequency much higher than the 0.24% derived from a review of previous genome-wide microarray studies in intellectual disability.
claims.n: 230 patients with unexplained intellectual disability passing quality control, from 234 recruited; 101 controls passing quality control, from 103
claims.eff: 4/230 = 1.7% against a literature figure of 0.24%; no confidence interval and no formal test of the difference reported
claims.limA: The authors state that the frequency of 22q13 deletions in intellectual disability is unclear and believed to be largely underestimated.
claims.limO: Four events. A proportion of 1.7% from 4 of 230 has a wide binomial interval that the abstract does not give, and the 0.24% comparator is pooled from heterogeneous published series with different platforms, resolutions and ascertainment, so the comparison is descriptive rather than a test. 'Unexplained' intellectual disability is an enriched, pre-screened population, which inflates yield relative to unselected series.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: 22q13 deletion frequency by SNP microarray

claims.text: The 22q13 deletions found in the intellectual disability cases were absent in the parents of those cases and in 101 controls, and the region shared by all four cases encompasses SHANK3.
claims.n: 4 cases with deletions, their parents, and 101 controls
claims.eff: 0 of 101 controls and 0 of the tested parents; no confidence interval reported
claims.limO: This null carries NO test statistic, NO power calculation and NO confidence interval. With 101 controls, the upper bound of a zero-event rate is roughly 3% at 95% confidence, which is far above the population frequency of 22q13 deletion; the control result therefore excludes almost nothing quantitatively, and its real function is to establish that the deletions are de novo rather than to estimate a background rate. The number of parents tested is not stated.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: presence of 22q13 deletion in parents and controls by SNP microarray

claims.text: Overexpression of the patient-derived SHANK3 Y1015X nonsense mutant in cultured embryonic mouse cortical neurons significantly affected neurite outgrowth compared with wild-type SHANK3.
claims.eff: described as significantly affected; direction, magnitude, p value and confidence interval not reported in the abstract
claims.limO: The abstract does not state the direction of the effect, so direction is recorded as not_applicable rather than guessed. Overexpression in a wild-type mouse background models a gain or dominant-negative action, not the haploinsufficiency that the patient has; the two are different genetic situations and the experiment does not distinguish them. No n, no statistics, no confidence interval.
claims.model: embryonic mouse cortical neurons transfected with control plasmid, wild-type SHANK3, or the Y1015X mutant
claims.measure: neurite outgrowth in culture

claims.text: Extracellular vesicles derived from Lactobacillus paracasei significantly improved autistic-like behaviours in Shank3-knockout mice, as well as in Drd2-knockout, Oxtr-knockout heterozygous and adenylyl cyclase-5 knockout mice.
claims.limO: The Shank3 line is the last of four models in a screen and is given a single clause in the abstract: no behaviour is named for it specifically, no n, no dose, no duration, no statistics and no confidence intervals. The mechanistic work (RNA sequencing, oxytocin receptor) was done in Drd2-KO mice, not in the Shank3 line, so nothing mechanistic in this paper is established for SHANK3. An intervention that improves behaviour in four unrelated genetic models is, on the face of it, acting non-specifically.
claims.model: Shank3-knockout mouse, allele not named; tested alongside Drd2-KO, Oxtr-KO heterozygous and Adcy5-KO lines
claims.measure: social behaviour and repetitive grooming

claims.text: Dendritic spine density and the levels of GAD1, NR1, VGAT and synaptophysin were significantly reduced in juvenile Shank3 delta4-22 and Cntnap2-/- mice compared with controls, irrespective of sex.
claims.eff: reported as significant; no effect sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limO: No sample sizes. Whole-cortex homogenate is a coarse measure that will dilute region-specific changes. Four protein markers plus spine density across two genotypes and two sexes is a large comparison set with no stated correction.
claims.model: Shank3 delta4-22 mutant mice (deletion of exons 4-22, removing all major isoforms) and Cntnap2-/- mice, with wild-type littermates
claims.measure: dendritic spine density by Golgi staining; protein levels of NR1, GAD1, VGAT and synaptophysin by immunoblot

claims.text: Female Shank3 delta4-22 mice showed the same synaptic and behavioural alterations as their male counterparts, with no differences between male and female mice in the three-chamber sociability test.
claims.limO: This null arrives WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and it is a null on an interaction, which needs roughly four times the sample of a main effect to detect at the same size. The study is not reported as powered for sex differences; it is powered for genotype differences and then stratified. No equivalence test and no bound on the size of a sex difference that could have been missed. The conclusion that females 'need to be studied along with the male animals' is well taken as a methodological recommendation, but the evidence offered for behavioural equivalence is an undetected difference, not a demonstrated absence of one. This record should be cited for its recommendation, not as proof that sex does not matter in Shank3 models.
claims.model: Shank3 delta4-22 and Cntnap2-/- mice with wild-type littermates
claims.measure: three-chamber sociability test; spine density; NR1, GAD1, VGAT and synaptophysin levels, compared between sexes

claims.text: Brief postnatal exposure to bisphenol A on days 6 to 8 decreased cortical expression of Shank3 and Homer1 and decreased social preference in male rats.
claims.limO: No dose, no sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. A small gene panel of unstated size with no stated correction. Shank3 is measured as a transcript in a region-level homogenate; nothing links the expression change to the behavioural change beyond co-occurrence in the same animals.
claims.model: wild-type rats exposed to bisphenol A postnatally; no genetic manipulation
claims.measure: cortical expression of a small panel of genes including Shank3 and Homer1; social preference; indicators of cell death

claims.text: There were no significant effects of brief postnatal bisphenol A exposure in female rats on apoptosis in the medial prefrontal cortex, on social preference or on cortical gene expression.
claims.limO: The null is reported WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals. Per-sex group sizes are not given, and a study sized to detect an effect in the pooled sample is typically underpowered within each sex, so 'no significant effects in females' here most likely means a non-significant result in a half-sized group rather than a demonstrated absence of effect. No equivalence test or bound is offered. This null should not be used to support the claim that females are protected.
claims.model: wild-type female rats exposed to bisphenol A postnatally
claims.measure: indicators of cell death, social preference, cortical gene expression including Shank3 and Homer1

claims.text: Deletion of the large intrinsically disordered region of SHANK3 impairs its liquid-liquid phase separation and clustering at dendritic spines of mouse hippocampal neurons, reducing postsynaptic density size and AMPA receptor expression.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. The work is in cultured neurons with engineered constructs; whether condensate behaviour described in vitro reflects the native postsynaptic density is a live question in the field and the abstract does not address it.
claims.model: mouse hippocampal neurons expressing SHANK3 with the large intrinsically disordered region deleted
claims.measure: phase separation and clustering of SHANK3; postsynaptic density size; AMPA receptor expression

claims.text: The human autism-related SHANK3 InsG3680 mutation truncates part of the large intrinsically disordered region, disrupts SHANK3 phase separation, and causes deficits in postsynaptic density remodeling and AMPA receptor recruitment.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics, no confidence intervals. A single patient variant tested in a heterologous mouse neuron system; whether the mechanism generalises to the deletions that account for most PMS cases is not addressed. InsG3680 is a specific insertion and most people with PMS carry whole-gene loss, where there is no mutant protein to misbehave, so the condensate mechanism described here may not be the relevant one for them.
claims.model: mouse hippocampal neurons expressing SHANK3 carrying the InsG3680 mutation
claims.measure: SHANK3 condensate formation, postsynaptic density remodeling, AMPA receptor recruitment

claims.text: Adult male Shank3-knockout mice carrying the delta13-16 allele showed spatiotemporal gait impairment, with decreased stand and swing duration, increased body and swing speed, and altered print position parameters.
claims.limA: The authors state that the contributions of other brain regions such as the basal ganglia and cerebral cortex, and of other cerebellar cell types such as granule cells and interneurons, remain to be elucidated, and that restriction to male mice leaves potential sex-dependent differences unexplored.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Many gait parameters reported from a single apparatus with no stated correction. Male only, so nothing here speaks to the female half of the PMS population.
claims.model: homozygous Shank3-knockout mouse, delta13-16 allele
claims.measure: digital gait analysis: stand duration, swing duration, body speed, swing speed, print position

claims.text: Optogenetic inhibition of cerebellar Purkinje cells in wild-type mice induced gait impairments, while optogenetic excitation of Purkinje cells in Shank3-knockout mice rescued gait abnormalities.
claims.limA: Other brain regions and other cerebellar cell types may contribute; the study is restricted to male mice.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics, no confidence intervals, no stimulation parameters. Acute optogenetic rescue of a developmental phenotype shows that the circuit is sufficient to move the readout, not that Purkinje cell hypoactivity is the developmental cause.
claims.model: Shank3-knockout delta13-16 mice and wild-type mice, with optogenetic manipulation of Purkinje cells
claims.measure: digital gait parameters

claims.text: Mice harbouring mutations in Fmr1, Cntnap2 or Shank3B all showed a blunted update of priors during decision-making, a common computational anomaly across genetically distinct autism models.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. The prior-updating measure is model-derived, so it depends on the behavioural model chosen, which the abstract does not specify. No PMS-specific interpretation is possible: the finding is explicitly shared across three genotypes.
claims.model: Shank3B mutant mice alongside Fmr1 and Cntnap2 mutant lines
claims.measure: high-yield rodent psychophysics with behavioural modelling of prior updating; brain-wide electrophysiology

claims.text: In mouse models of autism including Shank3B mutants, sensory cortical responses did not differentiate between expected and unexpected observations, while frontal areas contained more units encoding deviations from the animals' long-run prior.
claims.limO: This null is presented as a positive finding but it is a null: an expectation effect was not detected in sensory responses. It comes WITHOUT a reported test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and no equivalence bound is given, so it cannot establish that sensory cortex carries no expectation signal in these animals. The companion positive result in frontal cortex shows the recording approach was sensitive to something, which makes the sensory null somewhat more informative than a bare null, but the two measures are not on a common scale.
claims.model: Shank3B, Fmr1 and Cntnap2 mutant mice
claims.measure: single-unit encoding of expected versus unexpected observations during psychophysics

claims.text: Postsynaptic density proteins including PSD95 and Shank proteins were decreased in the mouse hippocampus 72 hours after electric foot shocks, and this loss was prevented by Nlrp3 knockout.
claims.limO: The abstract says 'Shank proteins' without naming an isoform, so it cannot be determined whether SHANK3 specifically was measured; the relation to SHANK3 is therefore recorded as contextual and this record should not be cited as a SHANK3 result. No n, no statistics, no confidence intervals. The protein result is one strand of a large multi-method paper whose primary subject is fear memory, not synaptic scaffolds.
claims.model: wild-type and Nlrp3-/- mice exposed to electric foot shocks in a contextual fear paradigm
claims.measure: PSD-related protein levels including PSD95 and Shank proteins, by immunoblot and RNA sequencing of hippocampal tissue

claims.text: Shank3 deficiency led to a significant reduction in GEPHYRIN/GABA-A receptor colocalisation in the piriform cortex and in primary neurons isolated from the olfactory bulb, with reduced mRNA levels of GABA transporter 1 in the olfactory bulb and of Collybistin in the frontal cortex.
claims.eff: reported as significant; no effect sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals. Allele not named. A panel of GABAergic markers was measured across three regions, with two reaching significance and the rest not, and no correction for multiple comparisons is reported; with that many region-by-marker combinations, two significant results is close to what would be expected by chance alone.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient (-/-) mouse; allele not named in the abstract
claims.measure: GEPHYRIN/GABA-A receptor colocalisation by immunofluorescence; mRNA levels of GABAergic markers

claims.text: Analysis of the remaining GABAergic neurotransmission markers in Shank3-deficient mice did not yield statistically significant results, Somatostatin in the frontal cortex showed only a non-significant trend towards reduction, and no change in cell morphology was observed.
claims.limO: These nulls come WITHOUT reported test statistics, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and the markers that returned nothing are not even named, so the size of the panel cannot be established from the abstract. A null of this kind is not evidence that SHANK3 loss leaves the rest of the GABAergic machinery intact; it is evidence that this study did not detect changes in an unnamed set of markers at an unknown sample size. The Somatostatin 'trend' is a non-significant result and is recorded as such.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient (-/-) mouse; allele not named in the abstract
claims.measure: expression of further GABAergic markers including Somatostatin; cell morphology of primary olfactory neurons

claims.text: SHANK3 protein levels in testis tissue were decreased in the EMF-28 group but not in the EMF-42 group after prenatal and postnatal exposure to a 50-Hz, 3-mT electromagnetic field.
claims.limO: The EMF-42 result for SHANK3 is a null and it arrives WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval; the abstract reports only which group reached significance. It is therefore not evidence that the longer exposure leaves SHANK3 unchanged, only that this study did not detect a change at an unreported sample size. Note also the inverted dose-response: the SHANK3 and antioxidant effects appear at the shorter exposure while the structural, hormonal, VEGF and IGF1 effects appear at the longer one, which no mechanism in the abstract explains and which is the pattern expected when several outcomes are tested in two groups without correction. No litter effects are addressed although pups from the same dams are used.
claims.model: wild-type Sprague-Dawley rat offspring; no SHANK3 manipulation
claims.measure: SHANK3 protein level in testis tissue; assay method not stated in the abstract

claims.text: Mild traumatic brain injury caused ipsilateral and contralateral loss of hippocampal dendritic spines and excitatory synapses with partial recovery in wild-type mice, whereas no significant synaptic alterations, no Arc or p-cofilin upregulation and no microglial proliferation were detected in Shank3 delta-11 knockout mice.
claims.limO: The central result is a null in the knockout arm, and it comes WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval. The title states that plasticity is 'abolished', which is an inference drawn from failure to reject the null in one genotype while rejecting it in another; no genotype-by-injury interaction test is reported, and comparing a significant effect in one group with a non-significant effect in another is not the same as demonstrating that the groups differ. The knockout mice also start from a lower baseline spine density, so a floor effect is an unexcluded alternative explanation for the absent loss.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-11 homozygous knockout mouse (exon 11 deletion) and wild-type littermates
claims.measure: dendritic spine density and excitatory synapse number by histology; Arc and p-cofilin protein levels; microglial proliferation by Iba1 counting (method not stated in the abstract)

claims.text: Mild traumatic brain injury increased fear memory in wild-type mice, while Shank3 delta-11 knockout mice, whose fear memory was already enhanced at baseline, increased only slightly after injury.
claims.limO: 'Increased only slightly' is not a statistical statement: the abstract does not say whether the post-injury increase in the knockout mice reached significance, and no test, power calculation or confidence interval is given for it. A ceiling effect on an already-enhanced baseline is not excluded.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-11 homozygous knockout mouse (exon 11 deletion) and wild-type littermates
claims.measure: fear memory, assay not named in the abstract

claims.text: Knockdown of Shank3 restricted to the nucleus accumbens decreased social preference in the three-chamber assay and decreased social motivation in the social conditioned place preference assay in male and female mice.
claims.limO: No group sizes, no effect sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. The knockdown is viral and region-restricted, so spread and knockdown efficiency, neither reported here, bound the interpretation.
claims.model: Shank3 exon 4-22 floxed (Shank3 flox/flox) mouse line with nucleus accumbens-restricted knockdown; conventional Shank3 delta-e4-22 deletion line used as comparator
claims.measure: social preference, three-chamber assay; social motivation, social conditioned place preference

claims.text: Shank3 deficiency restricted to the nucleus accumbens did not alter food reward seeking, reciprocal social investigation or anxiety-like behaviours, all of which the same group reports as altered in conventional Shank3 delta-e4-22 deletion mice.
claims.limO: These nulls come WITHOUT test statistics, WITHOUT any power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals. They are not evidence that SHANK3 in the nucleus accumbens is irrelevant to food reward or anxiety; they are evidence that this study did not detect an effect at an unreported sample size, with an unreported knockdown efficiency. The claim of social specificity rests entirely on the contrast between a significant social result and non-significant non-social results, and no interaction test is reported to support that contrast.
claims.model: Shank3 exon 4-22 floxed (Shank3 flox/flox) mouse with nucleus accumbens-restricted knockdown
claims.measure: food reward seeking; reciprocal social investigation; anxiety-like behaviour; assays not individually named in the abstract

claims.text: A mutation of a single copy of SHANK3 on chromosome 22q13 can result in language and/or social communication disorders.
claims.limA: The authors state that the mutations concern only a small number of individuals.
claims.limO: The abstract gives no cohort size, no variant list, no segregation data and no statistics, so nothing here can be checked without the full text. The cohort is ascertained for autism and Asperger syndrome rather than for PMS, so the phenotype described is the one visible from that ascertainment.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: SHANK3 sequencing and copy number in autism spectrum disorder families; language and social communication phenotype

claims.text: Male and female Shank3 delta-C homozygous mice slept significantly less than wild-type and Shank3 heterozygous siblings shortly after weaning, with increasing sleep fragmentation during adolescence.
claims.eff: reported as significant; no effect sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors state that the study used a single ASD mouse model and that broader implications need models with distinct genetic vulnerabilities.
claims.limO: No group sizes or statistics in the abstract. Home-cage monitoring infers sleep from movement rather than measuring it electrophysiologically, so the measure is not directly comparable to polysomnography in children.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-C mouse (C-terminal truncation, deletion of exon 21), homozygous and heterozygous, with wild-type siblings
claims.measure: sleep duration and fragmentation, non-invasive home-cage monitoring

claims.text: Early life sleep disruption before weaning interacted with Shank3 heterozygous genotype to produce lasting sex-specific behavioural changes, with males showing changes in sociability, sensory processing and locomotion and females a significant reduction in risk aversion.
claims.eff: reported as significant; no effect sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limA: Single ASD mouse model; the authors call for replication in models with distinct genetic vulnerabilities.
claims.limO: A sex-split battery of this size invites multiple comparisons, and no correction is mentioned. The abstract does not state whether the sex difference was itself tested as an interaction or inferred from separate within-sex tests, which are not the same thing.
claims.model: Shank3 heterozygous (WT/delta-C) mice and wild-type littermates
claims.measure: standard adult behavioural battery (sociability, sensory processing, locomotion, risk aversion)

claims.text: Undisturbed control Shank3 heterozygous mice, mice given post-adolescent sleep disruption and all wild-type mice showed typical behavioural responses in most tests.
claims.limO: This null arrives WITHOUT test statistics, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and 'in most tests' is not quantified: neither the number of tests nor which ones departed from typical can be recovered from the abstract. It is therefore not evidence that the undisturbed heterozygote is behaviourally normal, nor that maturity confers resilience; it is evidence that this study did not detect departures in an unspecified majority of an unspecified battery. The resilience conclusion in particular is an inference from a failure to reject the null in the post-adolescent arm.
claims.model: Shank3 heterozygous (WT/delta-C) mice and wild-type littermates; undisturbed control and post-adolescent sleep disruption arms
claims.measure: standard adult behavioural battery

claims.text: Chronic social isolation restored social novelty preference, olfactory function and self-grooming in Shank3 knockout mice and enhanced social interaction and olfactory neuron responses in wild-type mice, whereas an enriched social environment increased social interest in wild-type mice but had the opposite effect in Shank3 knockout mice.
claims.limO: No group sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals. The allele is not named, so the manipulation cannot be placed precisely on axis P. 'Restored' is a strong word for an abstract that reports no formal test of equivalence to wild-type.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse; allele not named in the abstract; wild-type comparators
claims.measure: social interaction and social novelty preference assays; olfactory neuron responses; self-grooming

claims.text: The striatal metabolome of Shank3 exon 11-21 knockout rats differed from wild-type littermates in 17 metabolites, 14 of them down-regulated, and eight weeks of early swimming from postnatal day 8 shifted the knockout metabolome by 19 metabolites, 18 of them up-regulated, while leaving 22 metabolites different from wild-type.
claims.eff: counts of differential metabolites only; no fold changes, no q-values and no confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limO: No group sizes. Untargeted LC-MS with no stated multiple-testing correction and no stated significance threshold, so the metabolite counts cannot be interpreted. Most importantly, the swimming group still differs from wild-type on 22 metabolites, more than the 17 that separated untreated knockouts from wild-type, so the data as reported do not show normalisation towards the wild-type profile; the conclusion that swimming 'regulated' the metabolome is compatible with a shift in an orthogonal direction. The abstract reports no behavioural outcome, so the metabolite shift is not tied to anything the animal does.
claims.model: Shank3 exon 11-21 knockout Sprague-Dawley rat; wild-type littermate controls
claims.measure: striatal metabolite profile, LC-MS

claims.text: Levels and activity of thioredoxin redox proteins were significantly changed in Shank3 knockout mice, and inhibition of Trx1 with PX-12 in wild-type mice decreased Trx1 and Nrf2 expression, altered synaptic protein and neurotransmission marker levels, raised nitrosative stress and produced an autism-like behavioural phenotype resembling that of Shank3 knockout mice.
claims.eff: reported as significant; no effect sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limO: No sample sizes or statistics. The pharmacological arm shows that Trx1 inhibition can produce an ASD-like phenotype in wild-type animals, which is a phenocopy argument and does not establish that the thioredoxin change is on the causal path from SHANK3 loss to the phenotype; the converse experiment, restoring Trx function in the knockout, is not reported in the abstract. The allele is not named.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse (allele not named in the abstract); primary cortical neurons from the same line; human SH-SY5Y cells carrying a SHANK3 mutation
claims.measure: thioredoxin system protein levels and activity; Nrf2 expression; synaptic protein and neurotransmission markers; nitrosative stress markers; behavioural assays

claims.text: Children aged 0-3 with at least one exposure to general anaesthesia had an autism incidence of 11.26 per 100,000 person-years against 6.05 in propensity-matched unexposed children, an incidence ratio of 1.86 (95% CI 1.34-2.59).
claims.limO: This is the one record in the batch that reports a confidence interval, and it is an association in administrative claims data. Propensity matching on recorded baseline characteristics cannot remove confounding by indication: the children who need surgery before age three differ from those who do not, and the conditions that bring them to theatre are themselves associated with neurodevelopmental outcomes. The absolute incidences are very low, so the relative measure rests on small numbers of events. Nothing in this record is about SHANK3.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: recorded autism diagnosis, Taiwan Maternal and Child Health Database

claims.text: Repeated sevoflurane exposure on postnatal days 5-7 induced autism-like behaviours in mice and down-regulated high-risk autism genes including SHANK3.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals. Six genes are named as down-regulated with no statement of how many were tested or whether any correction was applied. The behavioural assays are not named. Nothing links the expression change to the behavioural change beyond their co-occurrence.
claims.model: wild-type mouse; no SHANK3 manipulation; strain not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: expression of autism risk genes including SHANK3, assay not stated; autism-like behavioural assays, not named

claims.text: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy improved social behaviour and reduced cortical neuroinflammation in InsG3680 homozygous mice compared with placebo, with upregulated Igf1 expression and fewer Iba1-positive cells.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no effect sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals. The pressure and duration of the hyperbaric protocol are not stated, so the result cannot be related to any clinical protocol. Blinding and randomisation are not mentioned, and a placebo condition for a chamber-based intervention is difficult to construct; how it was done is not described in the abstract.
claims.model: InsG3680(+/+) knock-in mouse carrying the human SHANK3 InsG3680 mutation
claims.measure: social behaviour assays, not named; Igf1 expression; Iba1-positive cell counts

claims.text: Shank3b mutant mice of both sexes reproduced core and accompanying autism-like behaviours with significant sex differences, and heterozygous knockouts showed behavioural patterns distinct from both wild-type and homozygous knockout groups.
claims.eff: reported as significant; no effect sizes, no test statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limO: No group sizes and no statistics. Linear discriminant analysis is a supervised method that will separate groups to some degree on noise alone unless validated on held-out data, and the abstract does not say whether cross-validation was used. 'Distinct' for the heterozygotes is a direction-free statement: the abstract does not say which behaviours differed or in which direction.
claims.model: Shank3b mutant mouse, heterozygous and homozygous, with wild-type controls
claims.measure: whole-body behaviour, 3D motion capture with linear discriminant analysis

claims.text: Drosophila Shank null mutants of both sexes were fully viable and fertile with no apparent morphological or developmental defects.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT any test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval; 'no apparent defects' describes an inspection, not a measurement, and the abstract does not say what was inspected or how many animals. It is not evidence that loss of Shank has no developmental consequence in the fly, only that none was apparent on gross examination. The mutants in fact show an abnormal calyx and reduced olfactory acuity, so the absence is specific to gross morphology.
claims.model: Drosophila melanogaster Shank null mutants; Shank is the only SHANK family member in this species
claims.measure: viability, fertility and gross morphological and developmental inspection

claims.text: The abnormal mushroom body calyx structure and reduced olfactory acuity of Drosophila Shank mutants were fully rescued by pan-neuronal re-expression of Shank and only partially rescued by presynaptic re-expression, with no rescue by postsynaptic re-expression.
claims.limO: The postsynaptic result is a null and it arrives WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval. Crucially, the abstract reports no expression control: a failed rescue is uninterpretable unless the transgene is shown to be expressed at a comparable level in the postsynaptic compartment, and nothing in the abstract establishes that. GAL4 driver specificity and leak are likewise not characterised here. The claim that Shank acts presynaptically therefore rests on an uncontrolled negative plus a partial positive.
claims.model: Drosophila melanogaster Shank null mutants with cell-compartment-restricted Shank re-expression
claims.measure: calyx structure; olfactory acuity

claims.text: In vivo two-photon imaging in the developing mouse brain revealed shared and distinct dendritic spine morphogenesis and plasticity phenotypes between the autism-associated SHANK3 InsG3680 mutant and the schizophrenia-associated SHANK3 R1117X mutant.
claims.limO: No animal or spine counts, no effect sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Which phenotypes are shared and which are distinct is not specified, so the claim cannot be used quantitatively; it records that a comparison was made and that it separated the two alleles.
claims.model: InsG3680 knock-in mouse and R1117X knock-in mouse, both carrying human SHANK3 patient mutations
claims.measure: dendritic spine morphogenesis and structural plasticity, live two-photon in vivo imaging

claims.text: No significant changes in dendritic arborization were observed in either the InsG3680 or the R1117X SHANK3 mutant mouse.
claims.limO: This null arrives WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval. It is therefore not evidence that SHANK3 mutation leaves dendritic arborization intact, only that this study did not detect a difference at an unreported sample size. The authors then reason from it that synaptic rather than architectural dysregulation drives the behavioural deficits, which is an inference from failure to reject a null and is weaker than the sentence it supports. Arborization measured by in vivo two-photon imaging samples a limited depth and field, which further limits sensitivity.
claims.model: InsG3680 knock-in mouse and R1117X knock-in mouse
claims.measure: dendritic arborization, in vivo imaging

claims.text: CaMKII phosphorylates Shank3 at serine 782 in vitro and in heterologous cells co-transfected with CaMKII, and the nearby autism-associated variant Shank3 S685I increased S782 phosphorylation.
claims.limO: No replicate counts, no effect sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Phosphorylation demonstrated in vitro and in transfected heterologous cells need not occur at endogenous stoichiometry in neurons, and the abstract does not report an endogenous measurement.
claims.model: in vitro phosphorylation assays, heterologous cells co-transfected with CaMKII, and cultured hippocampal neurons; species of the cultures not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: Shank3 phosphorylation by mass spectrometry and a phospho-state-specific antibody

claims.text: The phospho-null Shank3 S782A mutation increased Shank3 and PSD-95 synaptic puncta size in cultured hippocampal neurons without affecting the colocalisation of Shank3 with PSD-95.
claims.limO: The colocalisation null comes WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT a confidence interval, so it is not evidence that colocalisation is preserved, only that no difference was detected. Colocalisation coefficients are in any case insensitive to the kind of change that alters puncta size, and the abstract does not say which coefficient was used. No culture or neuron counts are given.
claims.model: cultured hippocampal neurons expressing Shank3 S782A; species not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: Shank3 and PSD-95 synaptic puncta size and colocalisation, immunofluorescence

claims.text: Miniscope imaging in Shank3 knockout mice showed a reduced frequency of calcium transients in superior colliculus neurons projecting to the ventral tegmental area, with altered neuronal correlation and intrinsic cellular properties, and the interneural correlation correlated with the severity of social deficits.
claims.limO: No animal or cell counts, no effect sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals. A brain-behaviour correlation reported without the sample size cannot be judged at all. The allele is not named. Not peer reviewed.
claims.model: Shank3 homozygous knockout mouse; allele not named in the preprint abstract
claims.measure: calcium transient frequency and neuronal correlation by miniscope imaging; intrinsic cellular properties

claims.text: In young children with autism spectrum disorder, functional MRI showed a significant decrease in connectivity between the superior colliculus and the ventral tegmental area, and that connectivity correlated with the severity of social deficits.
claims.limO: No cohort size, no effect sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals. The correlation with symptom severity is reported without an n, so it cannot be evaluated. Subcortical fMRI connectivity in young children is technically demanding and motion-sensitive, and no quality control is described. Not peer reviewed.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: functional connectivity, fMRI; social deficit severity, instrument not named

claims.text: Shank3 deficiency promoted oligodendrocyte precursor cell proliferation while impairing oligodendrocyte maturation and myelination through hyperactivation of Erk signalling, and pharmacological Erk inhibition restored maturation in vitro, rescued myelination deficits in vivo and partially improved autism-related behaviours and motor function.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, no effect sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals. The inhibitor is not named and no dose or schedule is given, so neither selectivity nor exposure can be judged. 'Partially improved' behaviour is not quantified; the gap between a full myelination rescue and a partial behavioural rescue is exactly the kind of gap that matters for a trial endpoint and the abstract does not characterise it.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient mouse and primary oligodendrocyte cultures; allele not named in the abstract
claims.measure: OPC proliferation and oligodendrocyte maturation markers; myelination; Erk pathway activation; transcriptomics; behavioural and motor assays

claims.text: In an exome-wide association analysis of 310 Emirati individuals with type 2 diabetes, a SHANK3 variant at 22q13.33 (rs9616915) was associated with diabetic retinopathy at p = 5.18 x 10^-4.
claims.eff: p = 5.18 x 10^-4; no odds ratio, no allele frequencies and no confidence interval reported in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors state that only 16% of the markers from the exome chip passed quality control, that many variants were monomorphic in the Arab population or absent from a Euro-centric array, and that under-representation in reference panels may inhibit discovery.
claims.limO: No effect size and no confidence interval for the association, only a p-value. With 39,840 SNPs tested and four complication categories, a Bonferroni threshold would be of the order of 1 x 10^-6; p = 5.18 x 10^-4 is some two to three orders of magnitude short of it, so this does not survive correction for multiple testing and is reported as a top-ranked signal rather than a significant one. No replication cohort. 310 individuals split across four complication categories gives very small subgroups, none of which is sized in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: exome array genotyping, Illumina Infinium Exome-24; medically diagnosed diabetic retinopathy

claims.text: RNAi knockdown of Shank3 in neuronal cultures reduced the synaptic expression of metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 and impaired mGluR5 signalling, DHPG-induced long-term depression, mGluR5-dependent modulation of network activity, spine morphology and the frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents.
claims.limO: No culture or cell counts, no effect sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Acute RNAi knockdown in culture is not the same perturbation as lifelong heterozygous loss in a patient, and off-target effects of the RNAi are not addressed in the abstract.
claims.model: primary neuronal cultures with RNAi knockdown of Shank3; species not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: synaptic mGluR5 expression; ERK1/2 and CREB phosphorylation after DHPG; DHPG-induced long-term depression; multielectrode network activity; spine number, width and length; mEPSC frequency

claims.text: Shank3 RNAi knockdown did not affect the expression of other major synaptic proteins besides metabotropic glutamate receptor 5.
claims.limO: This null arrives WITHOUT test statistics, WITHOUT any power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and the proteins tested are not even named, so the size of the panel cannot be established. It is not evidence that SHANK3 knockdown leaves the rest of the synaptic proteome intact; it is evidence that this study detected no change in an unnamed set of proteins by an unstated method at an unreported sample size. The claim of specificity that the paper rests on is therefore carried entirely by an unquantified negative.
claims.model: primary neuronal cultures with RNAi knockdown of Shank3; species not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: expression of other major synaptic proteins; the proteins are not named in the abstract

claims.text: A positive allosteric modulator of mGluR5 restored DHPG-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation and normalised miniature excitatory postsynaptic current frequency in Shank3 knockdown neurons.
claims.limO: No replicate counts, no effect sizes, no statistics and no confidence intervals. 'Normalised' is asserted without an equivalence test against control. The rescue is of two readouts in culture; no behavioural or whole-animal outcome is reported, so the therapeutic inference the authors draw at the end of the abstract runs well ahead of the data.
claims.model: primary neuronal cultures with RNAi knockdown of Shank3; species not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: DHPG-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation; mEPSC frequency

claims.text: Cage, genotype and zinc diet each contributed significantly to gut bacterial community variation in Shank3B knockout and wild-type mice, accounting for 12.8%, 3.9% and 2.3% of the variation respectively, and fungal diversity was significantly lower in Shank3B knockout than in wild-type mice on the control zinc diet.
claims.n: four gastrointestinal sample types (ileum, caecum, colon, faecal); number of animals not reported
claims.eff: variance explained: cage 12.8%, genotype 3.9%, zinc diet 2.3%; no confidence intervals reported
claims.limO: This record is kept mainly for the proportions. Cage explains more than three times as much community variation as genotype and more than five times as much as diet, and the three together account for under a fifth of the variation, so the great majority is unexplained. Any proposal to use a microbiome signature as a PMS marker has to clear that noise floor. Number of animals and cages is not reported, and with cage as the dominant factor the effective sample size is cages rather than mice. The abstract states that a supplementary zinc diet reverses autism-like behaviours in this model as established background; no behavioural outcome is measured here, so that statement is not tested by this study and must not be extracted from it.
claims.model: Shank3B homozygous knockout mouse and wild-type comparators
claims.measure: bacterial and fungal community composition and diversity by sequencing; host gene expression; metagenomic functional profiles

claims.text: Shank3B-/- mice are more sensitive than wild-type controls to weak tactile stimulation in a vibrissa motion detection task, and their vibrissa primary somatosensory cortex shows increased pyramidal neuron firing together with reduced interneuron activity.
claims.limO: No sample sizes, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals appear in the abstract. Homozygous null allele, whereas PMS is a haploinsufficiency; the abstract reports no heterozygous data.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mouse (deletion of the PDZ domain-encoding exons); homozygous
claims.measure: tactile detection threshold in a vibrissa motion detection task; in vivo population calcium imaging of spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity

claims.text: Deleting Shank3 preferentially in inhibitory interneurons of vibrissa primary somatosensory cortex is sufficient to produce pyramidal neuron hyperactivity and increased tactile stimulus sensitivity.
claims.limO: Sufficiency is shown; necessity is not addressed in the abstract (no interneuron-sparing deletion is reported). No n, statistics or confidence intervals. The driver line and its specificity are not named, so off-target deletion cannot be assessed from the abstract.
claims.model: conditional Shank3 deletion restricted to vS1 inhibitory interneurons; floxed allele and driver not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: pyramidal neuron activity and tactile detection threshold

claims.text: A truncating SHANK3 mutation (STOP) found in a patient with ASD strongly impairs dendritic spine development and morphology, reduces synaptic transmission in mature neurons and blocks the effect of Shank3 on growth cone motility.
claims.limO: Overexpression of constructs in a culture system, not endogenous patient genotype; the abstract does not state the host neuron species, n, test statistics or confidence intervals. The paper's own framing is risk-factor biology in ASD, not PMS.
claims.model: cultured neurons expressing human SHANK3 constructs carrying patient variants STOP, Q321R, R12C and R300C; host species and culture type not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: spine density and morphology (imaging), synaptic transmission (electrophysiology), growth cone motility, actin accumulation

claims.text: Two SHANK3 variants inherited from healthy parents (R12C and R300C) produce intermediate effects on spine density and synaptic transmission rather than no effect.
claims.limO: 'Intermediate' is not quantified in the abstract: no effect sizes, no test statistics, no confidence intervals and no n. An intermediate effect that is statistically indistinguishable from either wild-type or the STOP mutant cannot be ruled out from the abstract alone.
claims.model: cultured neurons expressing human SHANK3 R12C and R300C constructs; host species not stated
claims.measure: spine density and synaptic transmission

claims.text: In valproate-exposed zebrafish larvae, oxytocin treatment at 50 micromolar for 48 hours increased shank3a, shank3b and oxytocin receptor expression and improved social and exploratory behaviours.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. The abstract reports that 25 and 100 microM were less effective than 50 microM but gives no comparison statistics, so the dose-response shape cannot be assessed. Crucially, shank3 here is a correlated transcript in a toxicant model, not a manipulated gene: no causal claim about SHANK3 follows.
claims.model: valproate-exposed zebrafish larvae (Danio rerio); no shank3 manipulation
claims.measure: shank3a, shank3b and oxytocin receptor expression by qPCR; light-dark preference, shoaling, mirror and social preference tests

ref.venue: Iranian Journal of Basic Medical Sciences

claims.text: Dogs carrying Shank3 mutations show behavioural and attentional avoidance of faces, in contrast to wild-type controls.
claims.limO: No n, no statistics, no confidence intervals in the abstract. Neither the allele nor the breed is named, which blocks any comparison with other Shank3 dog work.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant dogs; allele and exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: face versus object looking behaviour and attention (eye tracking / behavioural preference)

claims.text: Face-specific neural responses recorded over the temporal cortex are reduced in amplitude and delayed in latency in Shank3 mutant dogs compared with wild-type controls, and frontal/parietal responses underlying face categorisation are also reduced.
claims.limO: The word 'significantly' appears without any test statistic, p value, effect size, n or confidence interval in the abstract. Latency delay is asserted without a value.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant dogs; allele not stated
claims.measure: face-versus-object event-related responses from scalp/skull electrodes (amplitude and latency)

claims.text: Copy number analysis of SHANK3, SHANK2, NLGN3 and NLGN4 in 285 Chinese ASD cases detected no deletion or duplication in any of the four genes.
claims.n: 285 ASD cases (copy number); 285 cases and 384 controls (NLGN4 sequencing)
claims.limA: The authors conclude only that these genes 'may not be major disease genes in Chinese ASD cases'.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and it is therefore not evidence of absence. It is also underpowered by construction: SHANK3 structural variants are reported in roughly 0.5-1% of ASD, so in 285 cases the expected count is of the order of one to three, and observing zero is statistically compatible with the published frequency. The upper bound of the confidence interval around zero in 285 cases is not stated by the authors and would cover the prevalence the study appears to argue against. Multiplex fluorescence competitive PCR also targets specific amplicons and will not detect a deletion outside them.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: gene copy number by multiplex fluorescence competitive PCR

claims.text: Sequencing of the NLGN4 regulatory, untranslated and coding regions in 285 ASD cases and 384 controls identified no missense mutations, and six common NLGN4 SNPs showed no association with ASD.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT an effect estimate, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals; only 'did not find significant difference' is stated. With 285 cases and 384 controls, an association of the odds-ratio magnitude typical of common variants in ASD would be undetectable, so this is not evidence of absence of association.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Sanger sequencing of NLGN4 promoter, 5'/3' UTR and coding region; association analysis of 6 common SNPs

claims.text: A trace metal profile characteristic of autism patients applied to cultured hippocampal neurons reduces Shank gene expression, GluN1 and GluN2a NMDA receptor subunit expression, synaptic Shank and GluN2a protein levels, and synapse density.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals. The abstract writes 'Shank' without specifying which paralogue, so this cannot be attributed to SHANK3 specifically. The exposure concentrations and durations are not given, so the physiological relevance of the profile cannot be judged from the abstract.
claims.model: primary hippocampal neuron cultures; species not stated in the abstract; no genetic manipulation
claims.measure: Shank and NMDA receptor subunit gene expression, synaptic protein levels, synapse density (imaging)

claims.text: Zinc supplementation rescues the synaptic alterations produced by the autism-characteristic biometal profile, but zinc deficiency alone is not the sole causative factor for those alterations.
claims.limO: The negative half of this claim (zinc deficiency alone does not reproduce the effect) is reported WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, so it is not evidence of absence: a partial contribution of zinc deficiency smaller than the detectable effect is fully compatible with the data as reported. The abstract also does not state which single-ion manipulations were run or how many.
claims.model: primary hippocampal neuron cultures; species not stated
claims.measure: synapse number, NMDA receptor subunit and Shank expression

claims.text: Disruption of Shank3 in adult mice reduces the number of medial prefrontal cortex neurons encoding the experience of other mice and increases the number encoding the animal's own experience, abolishing the encoding of social agency.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals. Males only, so no statement about females is possible from this source. The allele and induction method are not named in the abstract, so the completeness of the disruption cannot be judged.
claims.model: adult-onset Shank3 disruption and subsequent re-expression in mouse; allele and induction system not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: single-neuron encoding of self and other experience during social interaction (chronic electrophysiological recording)

claims.text: Restoring Shank3 expression in the medial prefrontal cortex of adult mice reverses the self/other encoding imbalance and increases sociability over a period of five to eight weeks.
claims.limO: No n, statistics or confidence intervals. The 5-8 week figure is a range with no dispersion measure. Reversal is shown for the mPFC phenotype only; the abstract makes no claim about other phenotypes or regions, and absence of evidence there should not be read as evidence of absence.
claims.model: adult Shank3 re-expression restricted to mPFC; allele and induction system not specified
claims.measure: social agency encoding by mPFC neurons; sociability in behavioural testing

claims.text: Treating iPSC-derived cortical neurons from patients with a SHANK3 mutation with a neuronal nitric oxide synthase inhibitor produced therapeutic effects similar to those seen in Shank3 and Cntnap2 mouse models.
claims.limO: No n (number of patient lines or differentiations), no test statistics, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals. 'Similar therapeutic effects' is not operationalised in the abstract, so the measured variables cannot be listed. No isogenic control is mentioned.
claims.model: patient-derived iPSC cortical neurons carrying a SHANK3 mutation
claims.measure: molecular and synaptic nitrosative-stress-related phenotypes; 'similar therapeutic effects' not further specified in the abstract

claims.text: In two patients with mosaic 22q13.2-qter deletion of similar size (8.8 Mb and 8.9 Mb) and the neurological phenotype of 22q13.3 deletion syndrome, phenotype severity tracked the proportion of deleted cells rather than deletion size or parent of origin.
claims.limA: The authors frame the mosaicism-severity relationship as 'likely', not as demonstrated.
claims.limO: Two cases. No statistical test is possible and none is offered; there is no effect size and no confidence interval. The attribution of severity to mosaic fraction rests on the two deletions being of similar size and is confounded with parent of origin, which also differs between the cases. The phenotype is not quantified with any standardised instrument in the abstract.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: karyotype, FISH, array-CGH, microsatellite marker analysis; clinical neurological phenotype

claims.text: In a patient with a mosaic maternal 22q13.2-qter deletion, microsatellite marker analysis showed no evidence of mosaicism, although karyotype, FISH and array-CGH all detected it.
claims.limO: A single case, so this null carries no test, no power calculation and no confidence interval, and it cannot support any estimate of how often microsatellite analysis misses mosaicism. It is not evidence that the method generally fails: here the failure has a specific and stated cause, the concurrent segmental isodisomy, which masks the allelic imbalance the method relies on.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: detection of mosaicism by microsatellite marker analysis, compared with karyotype, FISH and array-CGH

claims.text: Shank3 exon 11-21 knockout rats show deficits in social memory, object recognition and water maze learning, reduced hippocampal volume and neuron number, and lower levels of related scaffold and receptor proteins.
