claims.limA: The authors state only that early swimming 'has a positive effect'.
claims.limO: The reported Results concern the deficits of the Shank3-deficient rats; the abstract does not state a single outcome for the swimming intervention itself, in any direction, with any statistic. The conclusion that swimming has a positive effect is therefore not supported by anything shown in the abstract, and no exercise effect could be extracted from it. No n, no statistics, no confidence intervals anywhere. The title's claim of a 'promising early intervention' should not be cited from this abstract.
claims.model: Shank3 exon 11-21 knockout rat
claims.measure: social memory, object recognition, Morris water maze; brain volume and H-spectrum by MRI; hippocampal dendritic spines by Golgi staining and confocal microscopy

claims.text: Atypical reciprocal social interaction and indiscriminate repetitive grooming are already present in juvenile Shank3B knockout mice of both sexes, extending findings previously reported in adult male Shank3B knockouts.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals. The abstract does not state which of the assayed behaviours showed no difference, so any null results within this battery are invisible from the abstract and cannot be counted.
claims.model: Shank3B KO mouse (deletion of the PDZ domain); juvenile and developmental time points
claims.measure: reciprocal social interaction, repetitive grooming, ultrasonic communication across developmental days

claims.text: Anterior cingulate cortex neurons of Shank3B knockout mice show normal dendritic morphology and synaptic activity at one week postnatal.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT a reported test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and no equivalence bound is offered. It is therefore not evidence of absence: a real but smaller-than-detectable difference at one week cannot be excluded, and that distinction is exactly what a therapeutic-window argument would turn on. Golgi staining and whole-cell recording in the first postnatal week are also technically demanding, so a floor effect in sensitivity is plausible and unaddressed.
claims.model: Shank3B knockout mouse (PDZ domain deletion)
claims.measure: dendritic morphology by Golgi staining; synaptic function by electrophysiological recording

claims.text: Significant impairments in dendritic growth and synaptic activity in the anterior cingulate cortex of Shank3B knockout mice emerge between two and three weeks postnatal.
claims.limO: 'Significant' is stated with no test, no p value, no effect size, no n and no confidence interval. Longitudinal in design but cross-sectional in the sampling described, so the onset date is bounded only to the interval between the sampled ages.
claims.model: Shank3B knockout mouse (PDZ domain deletion)
claims.measure: dendritic morphology by Golgi staining; synaptic activity by electrophysiology

claims.text: Children with ASD both with and without SHANK3 deficiency show increased cortical thickness and reduced nodal degree relative to typically developing children, mainly in lateral temporal cortex, prefrontal cortex, temporo-parietal junction, superior temporal gyrus and limbic/paralimbic regions.
claims.limO: No group sizes, no test statistics, no effect sizes, no confidence intervals and no statement of correction for multiple comparisons, in a study that tests many regions and several network metrics. Structural covariance networks are built across subjects rather than within them, so group-level network metrics here have no per-participant variance and cannot be used as an individual marker as reported.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: cortical thickness and sulcus depth from structural MRI; nodal degree and topological properties of structural covariance networks (graph theory)

claims.text: A trend towards regular structural covariance network topology was observed in ASD children with SHANK3 defects but not in ASD children without SHANK3 defects.
claims.limO: The absence in the non-SHANK3 group is reported WITHOUT a test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and the word used for the positive side is 'trend', which in context means it was not itself established as significant. A difference between the two groups is implied but no direct group-by-group interaction test is reported, so the standard error of inferring a difference from one significant and one non-significant result applies in full. This is not evidence of absence in the non-SHANK3 group.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: graph-theoretical topology of structural covariance networks (regular versus small-world organisation)

claims.text: Automated analysis of ultrasonic vocalisations with TrackUSF shows that social calls of Shank3-deficient rats span a spectrum shifted from appetitive towards aversive calls, with the tool detecting the majority of calls at under 1% false positives.
claims.eff: false-positive detection rate under 1%; no effect size reported for the Shank3 group comparison
claims.limO: The only quantified figure is the tool's false-positive rate; the Shank3 group comparison is reported with no n, no test statistic, no effect size and no confidence interval. 'The majority of USVs' detected is not given as a number, so sensitivity cannot be read off. Rat ultrasonic vocalisation has no direct human homologue, so the translational step to human communication outcomes is an analogy, not a measurement.
claims.model: Shank3-deficient rat; allele not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: ultrasonic vocalisations during social interaction, analysed by TrackUSF and compared with manual scoring by a trained observer

claims.text: Shank3 mutant mice display repetitive grooming, social deficits, anxiety and motor abnormalities, reproducing the behavioural profile the same laboratory had reported previously.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals. 'Many of these behaviors' implies that some previously reported behaviours were not reproduced, but the abstract does not say which, so the internal non-reproductions are invisible and uncountable from this source.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant mouse with a genetically reversible mutation permitting restoration of wild-type Shank3; exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: repetitive grooming, social interaction, anxiety, locomotor and rearing behaviour

claims.text: Early genetic restoration of wild-type Shank3 rescues repetitive grooming and social, locomotor and rearing deficits in Shank3 mutant mice.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals. The abstract does not state whether anxiety and motor abnormalities, both listed in the baseline phenotype, were rescued; their omission from the rescue list may indicate a null that is not reported, and this cannot be resolved from the abstract. The restoration age is not given, so no therapeutic window can be derived from this record.
claims.model: genetically reversible Shank3 mutant mouse with early restoration of wild-type Shank3
claims.measure: repetitive grooming, social interaction, locomotor and rearing behaviour

claims.text: In Shank3 knockout mice the ratio of D1 to D2 spiny projection neuron innervation in the prelimbic-to-dorsomedial striatum pathway is reversed, producing impaired action switching and repetitive behaviour, and genetic restoration of Shank3 in the dorsomedial striatum rescues both the physiological and the behavioural deficits.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals. The allele is not named, which blocks comparison with other Shank3 restoration studies. 'Rescued' is not quantified, so partial rescue cannot be distinguished from full rescue.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mouse; allele not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: D1/D2 innervation ratio (circuit mapping); action repetition and switching in a heterogeneous action sequence task

claims.text: Mice overexpressing Shank3 show reduced heart weight, increased cardiac fibrosis, arrhythmia, sudden cardiac death and impaired contractility, with prolonged action potential duration, increased L-type calcium channel current density, larger and slower-decaying cytosolic calcium transients and reduced troponin I.
claims.eff: cardiac Shank3 interactome comprised 78 proteins; no other effect size, test statistic or confidence interval reported
claims.limO: No n, test statistics or confidence intervals for any physiological comparison. The level of overexpression is not stated, so it cannot be judged against the roughly twofold increase expected in a 22q13 duplication. Transgenic overexpression is not equivalent to duplication of the endogenous locus.
claims.model: Shank3-overexpressing transgenic mouse; construct, promoter and copy number not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: cardiac histology, electrocardiogram and echocardiogram; action potentials and L-type calcium currents in isolated cardiomyocytes; cytosolic calcium transients; cell shortening; immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry of the cardiac Shank3 interactome; western blot

claims.text: Sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium content is unchanged in cardiomyocytes of Shank3-overexpressing transgenic mice despite increased cytosolic calcium transients.
claims.limO: This null comes WITHOUT a reported test statistic, WITHOUT a power calculation and WITHOUT confidence intervals, and no equivalence bound is given. 'Remained normal' is an unquantified comparison with non-transgenic cardiomyocytes and is not evidence of absence: a moderate change in store content cannot be excluded, and if present it would change the mechanistic interpretation of the increased transients.
claims.model: Shank3-overexpressing transgenic mouse; isolated cardiomyocytes
claims.measure: sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium content in isolated cardiomyocytes

claims.text: Shank3-InsG3680(+/+) mice show a strong behavioural preference for silent regions of an arena offering a choice between soundscapes, compared with wild-type mice.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals. The test is novel and not independently validated, so avoidance of sound is an interpretation rather than a measured hypersensitivity threshold; the authors themselves write only that the mice 'might express an auditory hypersensitivity phenotype'. Homozygous, whereas PMS is a haploinsufficiency.
claims.model: Shank3-InsG3680(+/+) mouse carrying a guanine insertion modelled on a human ASD mutation; homozygous
claims.measure: choice between soundscapes in a novel arena-based behavioural test

claims.text: Intermittent hypobaric hypoxia training at a simulated altitude of 5000 m, 4 h per day for 14 consecutive days, ameliorated autistic-like behaviours in male Shank3B-/- mice and acted by upregulating HIF1-alpha in dorsal raphe serotonergic neurons.
claims.limO: No n, test statistics, effect sizes or confidence intervals for any comparison. Males only. The behavioural assays that improved are not named in the abstract, so it is not possible to tell which domains responded and which, if any, did not; an unreported null within the behavioural battery cannot be excluded. The effect is downstream compensation, not restoration of SHANK3, so it does not bear on the dosage question.
claims.model: Shank3B-/- mouse (PDZ domain deletion), homozygous; Fmr1-/y mice used as a second model
claims.measure: autistic-like behaviours; HIF1-alpha expression; firing rate of dorsal raphe serotonergic neurons

claims.text: Oral venlafaxine throughout pregnancy significantly downregulated SHANK3 and TUBB5 mRNA in the brain tissue of BALB/c pups at postnatal day 21 compared with untreated controls.
claims.n: 14 dams in two groups of 7; number of pups analysed not reported
claims.eff: not_reported (stated as significant; no test statistic, effect size or confidence interval in the abstract)
claims.limO: No test statistic, no effect size and no confidence interval are given for any comparison. Group sizes are given at the level of dams, not pups, so the analysis may be pseudoreplicated across littermates; the abstract does not say how this was handled.
claims.model: wild-type BALB/c mice; no Shank3 manipulation; prenatal venlafaxine exposure
claims.measure: SHANK3 and TUBB5 mRNA, quantitative real-time PCR; brain size quantified from images with ImageJ

claims.text: DDC mRNA expression did not differ significantly between venlafaxine-exposed and control BALB/c pups, while SHANK3 and TUBB5 in the same samples did.
claims.n: 14 dams in two groups of 7; number of pups analysed not reported
claims.limO: The null carries no reported test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval. With at most seven litters per arm this is not evidence that venlafaxine leaves DDC unchanged; it is only a failure to detect a change. Its value here is comparative - it shows the assay did not move every gene in the panel - and it should be used for nothing more.
claims.model: wild-type BALB/c mice; no Shank3 manipulation; prenatal venlafaxine exposure
claims.measure: DDC mRNA, quantitative real-time PCR

claims.text: Four weeks of daily intranasal oxytocin doubled the time adult Shank3-/- mice spent interacting with a social partner, with the effect detectable after two weeks and persisting for four weeks after treatment ended.
claims.eff: approximately twofold increase in social interaction time; 50% reduction in exploratory behaviour; 30% reduction in repetitive behaviour. No confidence intervals or test statistics in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors call for further work on the benefits and risks of long-term administration, applicability to other ASD models, and effects on social communication, which was not measured.
claims.limO: No animal numbers and no sex information in the abstract, in a literature where oxytocin effects are known to be sex-dependent. Percentage changes are given without dispersion, so the precision of each estimate is unknown. A homozygous null is a more severe lesion than the heterozygous state of most people with PMS.
claims.model: Shank3-/- mice; the specific allele and exons targeted are not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: time in social interaction, exploratory behaviour, repetitive behaviour

claims.text: In the same oxytocin-treated Shank3-/- mice, social disinterest was also raised by roughly 10%, which the authors interpret as a form of social ambivalence accompanying the increase in sociability.
claims.eff: approximately 10% increase; no test statistic or confidence interval reported
claims.limO: A 10% change reported without dispersion or a test is close to uninterpretable on its own. It is charted because it is an unfavourable effect of the treatment, and unfavourable effects are the ones that disappear from abstracts first.
claims.model: Shank3-/- mice; allele not stated
claims.measure: social disinterest, scored within the social interaction assay

claims.text: Tmem169 promotes neuronal process and synapse development through its interaction with Shank3, and its deletion in the mouse dorsal forebrain produces neuronal morphological abnormalities and synaptic dysfunction.
claims.limO: No numbers, statistics or confidence intervals in the abstract. The Shank3 link is an interaction result; nothing in the abstract shows that Shank3 levels or Shank3-dependent function mediate the Tmem169 phenotype, so the causal ordering stated in the conclusion is stronger than the abstract evidences.
claims.model: conditional Tmem169 deletion in the dorsal forebrain; Shank3 not manipulated
claims.measure: neuronal morphology, synaptic function, autism-like behaviours, protein interaction with Shank3

claims.text: Chronic social isolation restored social novelty responses and olfactory deficits and normalised self-grooming in Shank3 knockout mice.
claims.limA: not_reported in the abstract
claims.limO: Preprint, not peer reviewed. No group sizes, no statistics, no confidence intervals and no sex information. The direction of the chronic isolation result is counterintuitive and is the kind of finding that most needs the full analysis before it is cited.
claims.model: Shank3 knockout mice; allele and exons not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: social interaction and social novelty tests, olfactory neuron responses, self-grooming

ref.venue: Research Square (preprint server; venue not stated in the source listing, inferred from the DOI registrant prefix)

claims.text: In wild-type mice, two hours of social isolation induced social deficits whereas chronic social isolation enhanced social interaction and olfactory neuron responses.
claims.limO: Preprint. No numbers or statistics in the abstract. Acute and chronic isolation move the same measure in opposite directions, which makes the interpretation of the knockout rescue dependent on isolation duration in a way the abstract does not quantify.
claims.model: wild-type mice, social environment manipulation
claims.measure: social interaction across repeated trials, olfactory neuron responses

ref.venue: Research Square (preprint server; venue not stated in the source listing, inferred from the DOI registrant prefix)

claims.text: Shank3B+/- mice performed as well as wild-type mice at detecting target odours against known background odours, and learned the task at a similar rate.
claims.n: 8 Shank3B+/- mice (five males, three females) and 6 WT mice (three males, three females)
claims.eff: not_reported (no test statistic, effect size or confidence interval in the abstract)
claims.limO: This null has no reported test, no power calculation and no confidence interval, in 8 against 6 animals. At that size only a large deficit would be detectable, so it is not evidence that known-background olfaction is intact in these mice. Its evidential role is narrower and sound: it shows the animals could perform the task at all, which is what makes the novel-background deficit in the same animals interpretable as specific rather than as a general inability.
claims.model: Shank3B+/- mice (exon 13-16 deletion line originally reported by Peca and colleagues)
claims.measure: target odour detection against known background odours, head-fixed operant task; learning rate

claims.text: Average glomerular odour responses in the olfactory bulb of Shank3B+/- mice were correlated with those of wild-type mice, but trial-to-trial variability of the responses was increased.
claims.eff: not_reported; the comparison is described as a correlation, with no coefficient, test or confidence interval given
claims.limO: The null on mean responses is reported without animal numbers, without a test statistic and without a confidence interval, and the comparison is stated as a correlation rather than an equivalence test. A correlation between genotype means cannot establish that the means are the same. The informative part of the record is the variance result, not the mean null: the same data show increased trial-to-trial variability, so a report of normal mean responses taken alone would be misleading.
claims.model: Shank3B+/- mice (exon 13-16 deletion line)
claims.measure: glomerular odour responses, imaging in awake mice

claims.text: When known background odours were replaced by novel ones in catch trials, the odour detection performance of Shank3B+/- mice fell to almost chance level while wild-type performance did not.
claims.n: 8 Shank3B+/- mice (five males, three females) and 6 WT mice (three males, three females)
claims.eff: performance described as dropping to almost chance; no effect size or confidence interval in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors note that the same deficit has been reported in the Cntnap2 model and suggest it may be general across autism mouse models rather than specific to Shank3.
claims.limO: 8 against 6 animals, no statistics in the abstract. The authors' own generality caveat is the important one for this corpus: a deficit shared with an unrelated autism model is not a SHANK3-specific readout and should not be proposed as one.
claims.model: Shank3B+/- mice (exon 13-16 deletion line)
claims.measure: target odour detection in catch trials with novel background odours

claims.text: Allele frequencies of SHANK2 and SHANK3 single-nucleotide polymorphisms did not differ significantly between the ADHD, ASD and combined ADHD+ASD clinical groups, nor between community controls and pseudo-controls.
claims.n: 298 boys with ADHD (including 256 family trios), 134 boys with ASD, 109 boys with both, 232 typically developing community controls
claims.eff: not_reported for the between-group homogeneity comparisons
claims.limO: No test statistics, no power calculation and no confidence intervals are given for the homogeneity nulls. They are heterogeneity checks used to justify pooling the groups, not substantive findings, and they are the weakest kind of null: a non-significant difference taken as grounds for treating groups as identical. The subgroups are small enough (109 to 298) that real differences between clinical categories could easily have been missed.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: allele frequencies of SHANK2 and SHANK3 single-nucleotide polymorphisms

claims.text: In the pooled comparison, significant disease associations after multiple-testing correction were found for three SHANK2 polymorphisms only, and the authors name SHANK2 alone, not SHANK3, as the candidate pleiotropic gene for ADHD and ASD.
claims.n: 541 boys across three clinical groups and 232 community controls plus 256 pseudo-controls from trios
claims.eff: For SHANK2, odds ratios 0.762 (permuted p = 0.0376), 0.720 (permuted p = 0.0034) and 0.770 (permuted p = 0.0407). No corresponding figures for SHANK3
claims.limO: The SHANK3 null is reported by omission: the abstract gives statistics for the three significant SHANK2 polymorphisms and says nothing about the SHANK3 results in the pooled test. No test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval is available for SHANK3, and the number of SHANK3 polymorphisms examined is not stated. This cannot support a claim that common SHANK3 variation is unrelated to ADHD or ASD; it supports only the narrower statement that this study did not report one. Full text is needed before the record is used at all.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: case-control and pseudo-control association testing of SHANK gene polymorphisms, with permutation-based multiple-testing correction

claims.text: Shank3 immunoreactivity in the normal human brain shows a largely neuropil pattern with differential laminar and regional distribution, strongest in forebrain subregions and light in brainstem neurons and cerebellar granule cells.
claims.n: not_reported (post-mortem cases grouped as youth, adult, aged and Alzheimer's disease; group sizes not given in the abstract)
claims.limO: No case numbers, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Post-mortem interval and antibody validation are not described, both of which govern how much a Shank3 immunoreactivity map can be trusted.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Shank3 immunoreactivity by immunohistochemistry and double immunofluorescence; Shank3, PSD95 and synaptophysin by immunoblot

claims.text: Shank3, PSD95 and synaptophysin protein levels in prefrontal, precentral and cerebellar cortex were reduced in aged and Alzheimer's disease cases relative to youth and adult cases, with disrupted neuropil labelling in the dentate gyrus molecular layer in Alzheimer's disease.
claims.limO: No group sizes, no statistics, no confidence intervals. Shank3 and PSD95 levels are stated to correlate across regions, so the decline may reflect general synaptic loss rather than anything specific to Shank3; the abstract does not separate the two.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: Shank3, PSD95 and synaptophysin by immunoblot; Shank3 immunoreactivity by immunohistochemistry

claims.text: Dietary zinc supplementation prevented impairments in auditory fear memory and social interaction in Tbr1+/- mice but did not restore social novelty preference.
claims.eff: not_reported. Statistical approach is stated (two-way ANOVA with Sidak post hoc, one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc) but no test statistic, effect size or confidence interval is given
claims.limA: The authors state that effects in rodent models may not reproduce in human patients, and that other affected structures, including olfactory bulb and anterior commissure, remain to be examined.
claims.limO: The social novelty failure is reported as a bare negative within a factorial design. The analysis plan is named but no power calculation is reported and no confidence interval is given, so a partial rescue of social novelty cannot be excluded. This is a selective rescue claim, which is the kind most vulnerable to being underpowered on the one component that did not move.
claims.model: Tbr1+/- mice; Shank3 not manipulated, SHANK3 expression measured as an outcome
claims.measure: auditory fear conditioning, three-chamber social interaction and social novelty, amygdala slice whole-cell patch clamp, immunohistochemistry for GluN1 and SHANK3 puncta

claims.text: Tbr1 haploinsufficiency did not produce excessive grooming or elevated anxiety in mice, unlike the phenotypes previously described in the Shank3 model.
claims.limO: A null with no reported test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval. It establishes only that these assays did not detect a phenotype in this line at this sample size; it is not evidence that Tbr1 haploinsufficiency leaves grooming and anxiety intact.
claims.model: Tbr1+/- mice
claims.measure: self-grooming and anxiety assays

claims.text: Dietary zinc supplementation restored SHANK3 expression and GluN1 synaptic puncta density in the basal and lateral amygdala of Tbr1+/- mice and reversed AMPA and NMDA receptor hypofunction at thalamic to lateral amygdala synapses.
claims.limO: No cell or animal numbers, no effect sizes, no confidence intervals. That a dietary manipulation raises SHANK3 immunoreactivity in a mouse with two intact Shank3 alleles says nothing about whether it would do so where one allele is absent, which is the PMS case.
claims.model: Tbr1+/- mice
claims.measure: whole-cell patch clamp AMPA and NMDA receptor currents, presynaptic function, GluN1 and SHANK3 immunohistochemical puncta density

claims.text: Knockdown of Shank3/ProSAP2 by RNA interference reduced dendritic spine density in cultured hippocampal neurons.
claims.limO: No neuron or culture counts, no effect sizes, no confidence intervals in the abstract. The species of the cultured neurons is not stated in the abstract, which is why species is recorded as other rather than guessed at. Acute knockdown in culture is not equivalent to lifelong heterozygous loss in a brain.
claims.model: RNA interference knockdown of Shank3/ProSAP2 in cultured hippocampal neurons; not a patient variant
claims.measure: dendritic spine density

claims.text: Transgenic expression of Shank3 was sufficient to induce functional dendritic spines in aspiny cerebellar neurons, recruiting glutamate receptors and increasing the amplitude, frequency and AMPA component of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents, and these effects required Shank3 interaction with the glutamate receptor complex.
claims.limO: No numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract, and the species is not stated. Overexpression in a cell type that is normally aspiny shows what Shank3 can do in a permissive context; it does not establish that restoring Shank3 in a haploinsufficient neuron would rebuild spines.
claims.model: Shank3 transgene expression in aspiny cerebellar neurons; mutation and deletion constructs used to test the glutamate receptor interaction
claims.measure: spine formation, synaptic contact number and size, miniature EPSC amplitude, frequency and AMPA component

claims.text: ZnT3 knockout mice, which lack synaptic zinc, had smaller dendritic spines and smaller miniature excitatory postsynaptic current amplitudes than wild-type mice in the auditory cortex.
claims.limO: No animal, cell or spine counts, no effect sizes, no confidence intervals in the abstract.
claims.model: ZnT3 knockout mice; Shank3 not manipulated
claims.measure: dendritic spine size, miniature excitatory postsynaptic current amplitude

claims.text: The spine size deficit in ZnT3 knockout mice was restricted to synapses expressing Shank3, and in wild-type mice synapses expressing both Shank3 and ZnT3 had larger spines than synapses expressing Shank3 without ZnT3.
claims.limO: The synapse-specificity claim rests on a contrast between two subpopulations of synapses with no counts, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals given. The absence of a deficit at Shank3-negative synapses is itself an unquantified null; without a power statement it cannot carry the specificity argument as firmly as the conclusion implies.
claims.model: ZnT3 knockout and wild-type mice, synapses classified by Shank3 and ZnT3 expression
claims.measure: dendritic spine size at synapses classified by Shank3 and ZnT3 expression

claims.text: In Alzheimer's disease post-mortem brain, Shank3 protein was decreased and ubiquitin-modified while Shank2 was increased, alongside substantial loss of NMDA receptor 1 and up to 40% loss of the AMPA receptor subunit GluR2 at the postsynaptic density.
claims.eff: GluR2 loss up to 40% at the postsynaptic density; no figures given for Shank3, and no test statistics or confidence intervals anywhere in the abstract
claims.limO: No case numbers, no statistics, no confidence intervals. Post-mortem interval is not stated, and Shank3 is a protein whose detection is sensitive to it. The opposite directions for Shank2 and Shank3 are interesting but rest on immunoblot in an unstated number of cases.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: quantitative proteomic profiling with immunoblot confirmation of NMDA receptor 1, GluR2, Shank2 and Shank3; ubiquitin modification of Shank3

claims.text: ProSAP2/Shank3 is continuously lost from, redistributed among and reincorporated into synaptic structures on timescales of minutes to hours, at rates far exceeding replenishment from somatic sources.
claims.limO: No synapse or culture counts, no effect sizes, no confidence intervals. Species not stated in the abstract, hence recorded as other. Overexpressed tagged protein may not behave as endogenous Shank3.
claims.model: fluorescently tagged ProSAP2/Shank3 and Synapsin I in cultured neurons; no patient variant
claims.measure: loss, redistribution, reincorporation and replenishment kinetics of tagged ProSAP2/Shank3

claims.text: Exchange rates of ProSAP2/Shank3 and Synapsin I at synapses were not affected by inhibiting protein synthesis or proteasome-mediated protein degradation, although they were accelerated by stimulation.
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistic, effect size or confidence interval in the abstract
claims.limO: A null without a reported test, without a power calculation and without a confidence interval. It is better supported than most nulls in this batch because the same preparation and the same measure did detect a change under stimulation, which demonstrates assay sensitivity; but assay sensitivity is not power, and the abstract gives no bound on the size of an effect that could have been missed. It should be cited as a failure to detect an effect of synthesis or degradation inhibition, not as evidence that these processes do not contribute.
claims.model: tagged ProSAP2/Shank3 in cultured neurons
claims.measure: fluorescence recovery after photobleaching exchange rates

claims.text: Shank3 was identified as one of seven hub proteins in whole-brain proteomic network analysis of chronic intermittent ethanol exposure and diazepam treatment, within a glutamatergic synapse signalling module.
claims.limO: Hub identification by network topology is a ranking of a computational graph, not a measured effect on Shank3. No animal numbers, no statistics and no confidence intervals in the abstract, and the species is not stated. The direction of any Shank3 change is not given.
claims.model: two-bottle choice and chronic intermittent ethanol exposure animal model; Shank3 not manipulated
claims.measure: label-free LC-MS/MS whole-brain proteomics with weighted gene correlation network analysis and protein-protein interaction hub identification

claims.text: Hippocampal neurons of young and adult IRSp53 knockout mice showed no morphological abnormalities in vivo, although cultured neurons from the same mice showed retarded dendritic development in vitro.
claims.limO: The in vivo null carries no test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval, and no animal numbers are given. It cannot establish that IRSp53 loss leaves hippocampal morphology intact. It is more useful as a dissociation: the same animals yielded a positive in vitro result, so the contrast between preparations is the finding, and the in vivo arm on its own would be uninformative.
claims.model: IRSp53-deficient mice; Shank3 not manipulated
claims.measure: neuronal morphology in vivo and dendritic development in primary culture

claims.text: Removal of IRSp53 increased hippocampal synaptic plasticity, with augmented long-term potentiation and paired-pulse facilitation, smaller postsynaptic densities and increased NMDA receptor subunit levels, while postsynaptic Shank proteins competed with Eps8 to block IRSp53-dependent actin bundling.
claims.limO: No numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. The Shank competition result is biochemical and is not shown in the abstract to operate in the knockout animals, so the link between the two halves of the study is proposed rather than demonstrated there.
claims.model: IRSp53-deficient mice
claims.measure: long-term potentiation, paired-pulse facilitation, postsynaptic density size, NMDA receptor subunit levels, contextual fear conditioning, actin bundling assays

claims.text: In a social operant conditioning task measuring effort to access a social partner, Shank3B mutant mice showed reduced social orienting and failed to show social reward seeking.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals in the abstract. Failure to show social reward seeking is stated as an absence, and an absence of an operant effect in an unstated number of animals is a null in disguise unless the full text gives the comparison. The zygosity of the Shank3B line used is not stated, which matters: homozygotes and heterozygotes differ substantially in this model.
claims.model: Shank3B mutant mice (exon 13-16 deletion line); zygosity not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: social operant conditioning: effort to access a social partner, concurrent social orienting; test-retest reliability reported as high

claims.text: Oxytocin receptor antagonism decreased social motivation in the same social operant task, and the task itself showed sex differences and high test-retest reliability in mice.
claims.eff: not_reported; test-retest reliability described as high, with no coefficient given
claims.limO: Reliability is asserted without a coefficient or confidence interval, which is the one statistic a methods paper proposing an outcome measure most needs to report in its abstract.
claims.model: wild-type and Shank3B mutant mice; oxytocin receptor antagonist manipulation
claims.measure: social operant conditioning: effort to access a social partner; test-retest reliability

claims.text: SHANK3a protein was 30 to 50% lower in the parietal cortex of people who died with Alzheimer's disease, and the loss was associated with cognitive decline.
claims.n: not_reported (post-mortem human cohort; size not given in the abstract)
claims.eff: 30 to 50% loss; no confidence interval, no correlation coefficient and no test statistic in the abstract
claims.limO: Cohort size, sex distribution and the cognitive instrument are not stated in the abstract. The association with cognitive decline is cross-sectional against post-mortem tissue and cannot establish direction.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: SHANK3a protein level, related to ante-mortem cognitive decline

claims.text: Hemizygous Shank3 exon 4-9 deletion and Alzheimer's-type neuropathology acted synergistically to impair object recognition memory at 9, 12 and 18 months and anxious behaviour at 9 and 12 months in 3xTg-AD mice, and Shank3a deficiency raised soluble beta-amyloid 42 and human tau at 18 months.
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistics or confidence intervals in the abstract
claims.limO: No animal numbers for any age group, in a design with repeated testing at three ages and a four-genotype structure. Synergy is an interaction claim and interactions need substantially more animals than main effects; without numbers or an interaction statistic the claim cannot be assessed from the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3 exon 4-9 deletion mice, hemizygous, crossed with 3xTg-AD mice modelling amyloid and tau pathology
claims.measure: object recognition memory, anxiety behaviour, Shank3a, PSD-95, drebrin and homer1 levels, soluble beta-amyloid 42 and human tau

claims.text: In the parietotemporal cortex of hemizygous Shank3 exon 4-9 deletion mice, Shank3a was reduced by the expected 50% while PSD-95, drebrin and homer1 levels remained unchanged.
claims.eff: Shank3a reduced by approximately 50% as expected for the hemizygous state; no figures, test statistics or confidence intervals for the unchanged proteins
claims.limO: The null has no reported test, no power calculation and no confidence interval, and no animal numbers. Immunoblot comparisons of this kind are typically run in small groups where only large changes are detectable, so this is not evidence that PSD-95, drebrin and homer1 are unaffected by SHANK3 loss; it is a failure to detect a change. It is nonetheless one of the more useful nulls in the batch, because the 50% Shank3a reduction in the same lysates shows the assay could resolve a change of that magnitude.
claims.model: hemizygous Shank3 exon 4-9 deletion mice
claims.measure: Shank3a, PSD-95, drebrin and homer1 protein levels

claims.text: Lipopolysaccharide treatment did not rescue social behaviour deficits in Shank3, Cntnap2 or Fmr1 mutant mice, although it temporarily rescued them in offspring exposed to maternal immune activation.
claims.eff: not_reported; no test statistic, effect size or confidence interval in the abstract
claims.limO: The null is reported without animal numbers, without a power calculation and without a confidence interval. It is unusually well supported for a null of this kind, because the same treatment in the same hands produced a rescue in the maternal immune activation model, and because the authors go on to identify a specific reason for the difference - the monogenic mutants did not produce comparable IL-17a - and then show that supplying IL-17a directly does produce the rescue. That mechanistic completion is what raises this above an unexplained failure; it is still not a powered test of equivalence.
claims.model: Shank3 mutant mice, alongside Cntnap2 and Fmr1 mutants and a maternal immune activation model; Shank3 allele not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: social behaviour; cortical neuronal activity; cytokine levels including IL-17a

claims.text: Delivering IL-17a directly into the primary somatosensory cortex dysgranular zone promoted sociability in Shank3, Cntnap2 and Fmr1 mutant mice as well as in maternal immune activation offspring.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals in the abstract. The delivery route is direct intracortical administration of a cytokine, which is not a route available in people; nothing in the abstract tests a systemically deliverable equivalent.
claims.model: Shank3, Cntnap2 and Fmr1 mutant mice and maternal immune activation offspring; Shank3 allele not stated
claims.measure: social behaviour; neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex dysgranular zone

claims.text: Across longitudinal EEG recording from weaning to young adulthood, Shank3 C-terminal truncation male mice slept less overall, had increased REM sleep early in life despite significantly reduced NREM sleep, and failed to develop the normal ability to shorten sleep latency after prolonged waking.
claims.eff: not_reported; NREM reduction described as significant, with no test statistic, effect size or confidence interval given
claims.limA: The authors present the developmental trajectory of sleep in this model as previously unknown and position the study as the first longitudinal description.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, no effect sizes, no confidence intervals, and males only. A longitudinal design with repeated measures needs its analysis model stated and the abstract does not give one.
claims.model: Shank3 C-terminal truncation mice (Shank3 delta-C)
claims.measure: longitudinal EEG: total sleep time, REM and NREM amounts, sleep latency after sleep loss, NREM slow-wave activity

claims.text: The abnormal response to sleep pressure in Shank3 C-terminal truncation mice appeared to be independent of homeostatic NREM slow-wave dynamics.
claims.eff: not_reported; the authors' own hedge, that the phenomenon seems independent, is the strongest statement available
claims.limO: A null with no test statistic, no power calculation and no confidence interval, in an unstated number of male animals. The authors themselves hedge it. It cannot support a claim that slow-wave homeostasis is intact in this model, and it matters for the corpus because a candidate EEG endpoint is being set aside on the strength of a negative that is not powered to set it aside.
claims.model: Shank3 C-terminal truncation mice (Shank3 delta-C)
claims.measure: NREM slow-wave activity as the homeostatic index, against sleep latency after sleep loss

claims.text: Long-term oral treatment with CBD-enriched medical cannabis oil reduced anxiety and decreased repetitive grooming by over 70% in a human mutation-based Shank3 mouse model, with CB1 receptor signalling implicated and cerebrospinal fluid glutamate concentrations lowered.
claims.eff: over 70% reduction in repetitive grooming; no test statistic or confidence interval in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors note the near absence of basic preclinical research on medical cannabis in this field.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, no sex information, no dose and no duration. A 70% behavioural reduction reported without dispersion in an unstated number of animals. Grooming is also reduced by general sedation, and the abstract does not report a locomotor control.
claims.model: human mutation-based Shank3 mouse model; the specific mutation is not named in the abstract
claims.measure: anxiety and repetitive grooming behaviour, CB1 receptor signalling, cerebrospinal fluid glutamate, cerebellar RNA sequencing

claims.text: The authors conclude that their results question the relevance of CBD enrichment of medical cannabis for treating core autism symptoms and emphasise the THC component as the one alleviating repetitive and social behaviour deficits.
claims.eff: not_reported; no comparison statistics between preparations are given in the abstract
claims.limO: This is the weakest kind of negative to cite: the abstract states a conclusion about CBD enrichment without reporting the comparison it rests on. No test, no power, no confidence interval, and the preparations compared are not described. The claim that THC rather than CBD carries the effect requires the full text before it is used in any ASPM communication, because families make real decisions on exactly this point.
claims.model: human mutation-based Shank3 mouse model; mutation not named
claims.measure: repetitive and social behaviours

claims.text: Cortical pyramidal neurons differentiated from iPSCs of four patients with autism carrying de novo SHANK3 truncating mutations show SHANK3 mRNA levels below 50% of control levels.
claims.eff: less than 50% of controls; no test statistic or confidence interval reported in the abstract
claims.limA: The authors present the result as further support for synaptic abnormalities in a subset of patients with ASD, not as a general ASD mechanism.
claims.limO: Four patient lines against three control lines is a small, unmatched comparison; the abstract gives a percentage but no test statistic, no effect size with dispersion and no confidence interval. Controls are not stated to be isogenic or family-matched, so donor genomic background is a plausible alternative explanation.
claims.model: iPSC-derived cortical pyramidal neurons from patients carrying de novo SHANK3 truncating mutations; neural stem cell differentiation, 40-45 days
claims.measure: SHANK3 mRNA level relative to controls

claims.text: Dendritic spine density, whole spine volume and spine head volume are reduced in iPSC-derived cortical pyramidal neurons from patients with autism carrying de novo SHANK3 truncating mutations, in correlation with reduced SHANK3 mRNA.
claims.n: 4 patient lines; 3 control lines; number of neurons and spines not reported
claims.limA: The authors describe spine morphology as variable across filopodia, thin, stubby and mushroom categories.
claims.limO: The correlation between SHANK3 mRNA and spine measures is asserted without a coefficient, a test statistic or a confidence interval in the abstract, and with four patient lines any correlation across lines rests on very few independent units. Number of neurons and spines measured is not reported, so it cannot be judged whether the analysis treats spines or lines as the unit of replication.
claims.model: iPSC-derived cortical pyramidal neurons from patients carrying de novo SHANK3 truncating mutations
claims.measure: dendritic spine density and spine/spine-head volume, 3D measurement with GFP labelling and immunofluorescence

claims.text: Circuit-selective Shank3 mutation restricted to the unidirectional prefrontal cortex to basolateral amygdala projection alters spine morphology and excitation-inhibition balance of that circuit and reduces sociability in mice.
claims.limA: The authors note that pathogenic neural-network mechanisms underlying social dysfunction are largely unknown and present the circuit as one level of explanation.
claims.limO: No n, no sex, no genetic background, no effect size and no confidence interval are available from the abstract. The comparison with human ASD neuroimaging is stated as consistency, not as a formal test.
claims.model: circuit-selective Shank3 mutation (ctMUT) in the prefrontal cortex to basolateral amygdala projection; allele and exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: spine morphology, excitatory-inhibitory balance, neural activity amplitude and variability, social interaction behaviour

claims.text: Optogenetic activation of the prefrontal-to-amygdala circuit in wild-type mice only partially recapitulates the reduced sociability of Shank3 circuit-mutant mice, and circuit inhibition in the mutants only partially rescues social behaviour.
claims.limA: The authors themselves describe both effects as partial.
claims.limO: A partial recapitulation and a partial rescue together mean the circuit is neither necessary nor sufficient for the whole social phenotype, but the residual is not quantified: no effect size, no test statistic, no confidence interval and no power analysis are reported in the abstract. The unexplained remainder therefore cannot be sized, and this record must not be cited as showing that the circuit accounts for sociability.
claims.model: circuit-selective Shank3 mutation (ctMUT) in the prefrontal cortex to basolateral amygdala projection
claims.measure: sociability in social interaction testing after optogenetic manipulation

claims.text: Simultaneous local deletion of Shank2 and Shank3 in the retrosplenial area of mice severely impairs social memory, and the impairment is rescued by DREADD-mediated neuronal activation.
claims.n: 10 cortical subregions screened; animal numbers not reported
claims.limA: The authors position the retrosplenial area as an addition to a list of contributing regions, not as the sole locus.
claims.limO: Shank2 is deleted alongside Shank3 throughout, so no part of this result isolates Shank3. The abstract gives no animal numbers, no effect size and no confidence interval, and no correction for the 10 regions screened is mentioned.
claims.model: Shank2-Shank3 double knockout mouse, plus local simultaneous deletion of Shank2 and Shank3 in each of 10 cortical subregions; exons targeted not stated in the abstract
claims.measure: social memory testing after regional Shank2/3 deletion

claims.text: In a screen of 10 cortical subregions, the retrosplenial area is the only subregion reported in which local Shank2/3 deletion severely impairs social memory.
claims.n: 10 cortical subregions; animal numbers per region not reported
claims.limA: The authors report only the positive hit and frame the screen as a means of linking cortical areas to specific autistic traits.
claims.limO: The nine subregions that did not yield a social-memory impairment are not individually reported, and no test, no effect size, no confidence interval and no power calculation is given for any of them. This null is therefore not evidence that Shank2/3 deletion in those regions leaves social memory intact; it is an unreported remainder of a screen, and must not be cited as regional specificity.
claims.model: local simultaneous Shank2 and Shank3 deletion in each of 10 cortical subregions
claims.measure: social memory and other autistic-trait assays across cortical subregions

claims.text: In a Chinese autism cohort of 539 cases and 512 controls screened with a 358-gene panel, SHANK3 and SHANK2 variants were the most frequent findings and occurred in 1.2% of cases.
claims.eff: SHANK3 and SHANK2 variants in 1.2% of cases; pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 9.5% of cases; no confidence intervals reported
claims.limA: The authors note that panel diagnostic potential had previously been evaluated only in small cohorts and is understudied in the Chinese population.
claims.limO: SHANK3 and SHANK2 are reported together, so the SHANK3-only rate cannot be recovered from the abstract. No confidence interval accompanies the 1.2%, which rests on roughly six or seven individuals, and the female excess is stated without a count or a test.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: targeted capture resequencing of 358 candidate genes; ADI-R and ADOS phenotyping

claims.text: Of 358 candidate autism genes sequenced, a subset of 78 syndromic and 54 nonsyndromic genes was the most significantly associated with case status, implying the remaining genes on the panel were not.
claims.limA: The authors frame the subset as a prioritisation for future screening rather than as a negative verdict on the remaining genes.
claims.limO: The genes outside the associated subset are not listed and no per-gene statistic, confidence interval or power calculation is given. With 539 cases spread over 358 genes, most genes are certain to be underpowered individually, so absence of association here is uninformative about absence of effect and must not be cited as exclusion of any gene.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: burden of ultra-rare functional variants per gene, cases versus controls

claims.text: Increased Ube3a dosage in mice is associated with transcriptional dysregulation of autism-associated genes including Shank3.
claims.limA: The authors present the result as suggesting a contribution to sex bias, phrased as a suggestion rather than a demonstration.
claims.limO: Shank3 appears only inside an example list of dysregulated genes; the direction, magnitude, dispersion and significance of the Shank3 change are not given, nor is the brain region. Nothing in this record supports a specific statement about Shank3.
claims.model: mice carrying extra copies of Ube3a; Shank3 genotype not manipulated
claims.measure: transcriptomic profiling, differential expression of autism-associated genes including Shank3

claims.text: Mice carrying the ASD-linked Shank3 InsG3680 mutation show striatal synaptic transmission defects before weaning age together with impaired juvenile social interaction.
claims.limA: The authors note it is unclear how different mutations of the same gene contribute to different disorders and present the mouse comparison as a route to that question.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, no sex, no genetic background, no effect size and no confidence interval are obtainable from the abstract. The temporal coincidence with the early onset of ASD symptoms in humans is an interpretive parallel, not a measured relationship.
claims.model: Shank3 InsG3680 knock-in mouse, modelling a human ASD-linked SHANK3 variant
claims.measure: striatal synaptic transmission; juvenile social interaction

claims.text: Adult mice carrying the schizophrenia-linked Shank3 R1117X mutation show synaptic defects in prefrontal cortex and altered social dominance behaviour, a profile distinct from that of InsG3680 mice.
claims.limA: The authors present the allele comparison as informing, not settling, the corresponding question in human patients.
claims.limO: The two lines are compared qualitatively; no statistical test of a genotype-by-phenotype interaction between the two alleles is reported in the abstract, which is what a claim of distinct profiles requires. No n, effect size or confidence interval is available.
claims.model: Shank3 R1117X knock-in mouse, modelling a human schizophrenia-linked SHANK3 variant
claims.measure: prefrontal synaptic function; social dominance behaviour

claims.text: Shank3 InsG3680 and R1117X mouse lines differ in Shank3 mRNA stability and in SHANK1 and SHANK2 upregulation.
claims.limA: The authors present the molecular difference as part of a demonstration that different alleles of one gene diverge at molecular, synaptic and circuit levels.
claims.limO: Neither the direction nor the magnitude of the SHANK1/2 change per line is given in the abstract, and no brain region is specified. No statistics or confidence intervals are reported.
claims.model: Shank3 InsG3680 and Shank3 R1117X knock-in mouse lines
claims.measure: Shank3 mRNA stability; SHANK1 and SHANK2 protein or transcript levels

claims.text: Children with SHANK3 defects show decreased grey matter volume in dorsal striatum, amygdala, hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus compared with idiopathic ASD and typically developing controls.
claims.n: 14 with SHANK3 defects; 26 idiopathic ASD controls; 32 typically developing controls
claims.limA: The authors present the work as offering specific insights from a monogenic cause and as a basis for future functional connectivity studies.
claims.limO: Fourteen children in the index group is small for voxel-wise morphometry; the abstract reports no effect size, no confidence interval and no statement of multiple-comparison correction, and does not say which of the two control groups each contrast is against.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: grey matter volume, voxel-based morphometry on structural MRI

claims.text: Children with SHANK3 defects show decreased fractional anisotropy across projection, association and commissural white matter tracts, including middle cerebral peduncle, corpus callosum, superior longitudinal fasciculus, corona radiata and internal and external capsule.
claims.n: 14 with SHANK3 defects; 26 idiopathic ASD controls; 32 typically developing controls
claims.limA: The authors describe the finding as supporting a striatum-centred disruption and as motivating functional connectivity work.
claims.limO: The change is reported as widespread rather than localised, which is also the pattern expected from head motion in a young, more impaired group; the abstract reports no motion control, no effect size and no confidence interval, and n = 14 is small for TBSS.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: fractional anisotropy, tract-based spatial statistics on diffusion MRI

claims.text: L-serine administration to growth hormone-releasing hormone knockout and wild-type mice alters histone marks in hippocampus and cortex and changes mRNA expression of a set of genes that includes shank3.
claims.limA: The authors present the work as a novel insight into beneficial effects of L-serine, without claiming a mechanism specific to any one gene.
claims.limO: The causal wording, that epigenetic marks regulate the listed transcripts, is not supported by any manipulation described in the abstract; it is a correlation between two sets of measurements. The direction and magnitude of the shank3 change are not given, no dose is stated, and no statistics or confidence intervals are reported.
claims.model: growth hormone-releasing hormone knockout (GHRH-KO) mice and wild-type controls; Shank3 not manipulated
claims.measure: histone marks H3K4me, H3K9ac, H3K14ac, H3K18ac; mRNA expression of BDNF, grm3, foxp1, shank3, auts2, marcksl1; anxiety, object recognition and autism-like behaviours

claims.text: Early environmental enrichment produced no benefit on ASD-like phenotypes in Shank3 complete knockout mice, including no change in repetitive self-grooming or hole-board exploration, contrary to previous reports of enrichment benefit in rodent models.
claims.limA: The authors state explicitly that a different enrichment protocol might have rescued the phenotypes in their model, and that the translational value of enrichment experiments is unknown.
claims.limO: No test statistic, no effect size, no confidence interval and no power analysis are reported for any of the null comparisons, and no animal numbers are given. This null therefore does not establish that enrichment is without effect in Shank3 knockouts; it establishes only that no effect was detected here, and the study cannot exclude an effect it was too small to see. The authors' own caveat about protocol choice compounds this.
claims.model: Shank3 complete knockout, Shank3 delta-exon-4-22 mice generated and characterised by the same laboratory
claims.measure: repetitive self-grooming; hole-board exploration; anxiety-like behaviour; motor performance

claims.text: Early environmental enrichment increased anxiety-like behaviour in all mice regardless of Shank3 genotype.
claims.limA: The authors use this result to argue against a one-size-fits-all approach to behavioural intervention in ASD.
claims.limO: The genotype-independence is the null part of this record and it is unsupported by any reported interaction test, effect size, confidence interval or power calculation. An undetected genotype-by-enrichment interaction in an unpowered design is the expected result whether or not one exists.
claims.model: Shank3 complete knockout (delta-exon-4-22) mice and wild-type littermates
claims.measure: anxiety-like behaviour

claims.text: Early environmental enrichment decreased motor performance specifically in wild-type mice and not in Shank3 knockout mice.
claims.limA: The authors draw a general conclusion that enrichment protocols are not universally beneficial.
claims.limO: A genotype-specific effect requires a significant interaction, and none is reported; an effect present in one group and absent in the other is not the same thing. No effect size, confidence interval or power analysis accompanies the knockout null, so the absence in knockouts may simply be a floor effect in an already impaired group.
claims.model: Shank3 complete knockout (delta-exon-4-22) mice and wild-type littermates
claims.measure: motor performance

claims.text: Cortical neurons derived from iPSCs of patients with mutations in GRIN2B, SHANK3 or UBTF, or with 7q11.23 duplication, show hyperexcitability and early maturation compared with neurons from unaffected first-degree relatives.
claims.limA: The authors frame convergence as an indication, read together with previously reported data, rather than as a demonstration.
claims.limO: The claim is a convergence across four different genetic causes, only one of which is SHANK3, and the abstract does not report the SHANK3 line separately; nothing here supports a SHANK3-specific statement. No cell or line numbers, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals are given.
claims.model: iPSC-derived cortical neurons from patients with GRIN2B, SHANK3 and UBTF mutations and 7q11.23 duplication; controls derived from a first-degree relative without the mutation
claims.measure: whole-cell patch clamp: sodium currents, excitatory postsynaptic current amplitude and rate, evoked action potentials

claims.text: A shared hyperexcitable, early-maturing cortical neuron phenotype across four different ASD-associated genetic causes is not specific to SHANK3 mutation.
claims.limA: The authors present convergence as the finding of interest and do not discuss it as a specificity problem.
claims.limO: No between-genotype test is reported, so similarity across lines is asserted from each line differing from control, not from a demonstrated absence of difference between lines. There is no equivalence test, no confidence interval on the between-genotype difference and no power analysis, so this cannot be cited as evidence that the phenotypes are the same; it is only evidence that no difference was shown.
claims.model: iPSC-derived cortical neurons from patients with four different ASD-associated mutations including SHANK3
claims.measure: comparison of electrophysiological phenotype across genotypes

claims.text: CRISPR-Cas9 mutation of the zebrafish shank3a paralogue markedly reduces social contagion through a deficit in attention that impairs recognition of others' affective states.
claims.limA: The authors state that zebrafish are unlikely to represent the full complexity of socio-cognitive and communication deficits in human ASD, and cannot represent the scaling up to higher-order empathic and prosocial phenotypes.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals are available from the abstract. The attribution to an attention mechanism rests on a clustering analysis, which is a decomposition of observed variance rather than an experimental dissociation.
claims.model: CRISPR-Cas9 mutation of the zebrafish shank3a paralogue, selected by the authors for greater orthology and functional conservation relative to the human gene
claims.measure: two-phase social contagion protocol with distress and neutral demonstrator states, later recall and discrimination

claims.text: Among the neuroplasticity markers whose whole-brain expression changed between shank3a mutant and wild-type zebrafish, only downregulated neuroligins clustered with shank3a expression in a component contributing to attention.
claims.limA: The authors note the limits of the zebrafish model for human socio-cognitive phenotypes but do not discuss the non-clustering markers.
claims.limO: The markers that did not cluster are not named or quantified, and no test, effect size, confidence interval or power calculation is given for them. The negative half of this result is therefore uninterpretable as absence of involvement; it reflects what a clustering procedure retained, not what was shown to be unrelated.
claims.model: CRISPR-Cas9 shank3a mutant zebrafish and wild-type comparison
claims.measure: whole-brain expression of neuroplasticity markers; clustering against phenotypic variation

claims.text: Chronic sodium bromide administration relieved autistic-like behavioural deficits in Shank3 delta-exon-13-16 knockout mice as well as in Oprm1 and Fmr1 knockout mice.
claims.limA: The authors note that no pharmacological treatment has been approved that ameliorates social behaviour in patients with ASD, and present bromide as a therapeutic potential rather than an established effect.
claims.limO: Which behaviours improved in the Shank3 line specifically is not stated; the result is reported for the three models together. No doses, durations, animal numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals are available from the abstract. Bromide has a long human safety history that the abstract does not weigh against efficacy.
claims.model: Shank3 delta-exon-13-16 knockout mice, alongside Oprm1 and Fmr1 knockout mice
claims.measure: autistic-like behaviours: social interaction, communication, repetitive behaviour

claims.text: Bromide ions behave as positive allosteric modulators of the mGlu4 receptor in heterologous cells, and chronic sodium bromide acts synergistically with an mGlu4 positive allosteric modulator on autistic-like behaviour in Oprm1 knockout mice.
claims.limA: The authors offer the mechanism as providing a molecular explanation for the observed synergy.
claims.limO: The synergy and the transcriptional changes are reported in Oprm1 null mice, not in the Shank3 line, so the proposed mechanism is not shown to operate in a SHANK3 context at all. No doses, numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals are given.
claims.model: Oprm1 knockout mice; heterologous cell expression system for mGlu4
claims.measure: mGlu4 receptor pharmacology in heterologous cells; autistic-like behaviour

claims.text: Four hours after loose ligation of the rat sciatic nerve, Shank1 protein increased in the ipsilateral postsynaptic density of spinal dorsal horn neurons, with no change in the contralateral postsynaptic density of ligated animals or in either side of sham-operated animals.
claims.limA: The authors present Shank1 accumulation as possibly a necessary step in injury-associated plasticity, not as established.
claims.limO: The contralateral and sham comparisons are internal controls reported without test statistics, effect sizes, confidence intervals or any power calculation, so they show only that no change was detected. Shank1 message did not change overall, which the abstract also reports without statistics.
claims.model: loose ligation of the sciatic nerve in rats; sham-operated controls
claims.measure: Shank1 protein and mRNA in the postsynaptic density; weight distribution and thermal hyperalgesia

claims.text: Ingenuity pathway analysis of rat hippocampal synaptoneurosome proteomes after anodal transcranial direct-current stimulation identified shank3 among the significant predicted upstream regulators.
claims.n: 184 differentially expressed hippocampal proteins; animal numbers not reported
claims.limA: The authors describe their results as descriptive molecular evidence.
claims.limO: shank3 here is a software-predicted upstream regulator inferred from a protein expression pattern; SHANK3 itself was not measured, manipulated or validated. No confidence interval or enrichment statistic is reported in the abstract. This record supports no statement about SHANK3 protein or function.
claims.model: male Sprague Dawley rats; Shank3 not manipulated
claims.measure: bottom-up liquid chromatography mass spectrometry proteomics; Ingenuity pathway analysis upstream regulator prediction; passive avoidance test

claims.text: Shank3 Venus/+ and Shank3 Venus/Venus knock-in mice, carrying a fluorescent tag on the full-length Shank3a isoform, showed no behavioural deficits.
claims.limA: The authors present the line as a tool for studying endogenous Shank3a expression, and the absence of deficits as supporting its validity.
claims.limO: This null is the result the tool requires in order to be usable, which makes it the case where a power analysis matters most, and none is reported. No behavioural battery is named, no animal numbers, no effect sizes and no confidence intervals or equivalence bounds are given. The record therefore does not establish that the Venus tag is functionally silent; it establishes only that no deficit was detected in unspecified testing.
claims.model: Shank3 Venus/Venus and Shank3 Venus/+ knock-in mice; Venus tag on the full-length Shank3a isoform
claims.measure: behavioural testing of knock-in mice; battery not specified in the abstract

claims.text: Shank3 Venus/delta-C mice show a developmental delay in brain expression of the Venus-tagged Shank3a isoform compared with Shank3 Venus/+ controls.
claims.limA: The authors present the delta-C allele as a model of ASD and the delay as a demonstration of what the tool can detect.
claims.limO: A delay implies a time course, and the ages compared, the magnitude and the statistics are all absent from the abstract. The wild-type copy is tracked in the presence of a mutant copy, so the result concerns the remaining allele rather than total Shank3a.
claims.model: Shank3 Venus/Venus mice crossed with Shank3 delta-C/delta-C mice to give Shank3 Venus/delta-C and Shank3 Venus/+ genotypes
claims.measure: endogenous Venus-Shank3a expression over development

claims.text: Shank3B knockout mice, an acute restraint stress model and a chronic inflammatory pain model all show increased anxiety in the open field test and elevated plus maze, but only the Shank3B knockout and stress models show increased total self-grooming duration.
claims.limA: The authors frame the three models as a comparison designed to separate anxiety from stereotypy.
claims.limO: The pain model is described as showing only an increasing trend in mean self-grooming duration, which is a non-significant result reported without the test, the effect size, a confidence interval or any power calculation; with no power analysis the pain model cannot be said to differ from the other two. Animal numbers are not reported for any arm.
claims.model: Shank3B knockout mice; acute restraint stress model; chronic inflammatory pain model
claims.measure: open field test; elevated plus maze; total self-grooming duration

claims.text: Diazepam reduced anxiety and total grooming duration in Shank3B knockout mice but did not restore the grooming microstructure, which was partially relieved in the acute stress model.
claims.limA: The authors conclude that anxiety aggravated stereotyped self-grooming duration but not the grooming microstructure in the ASD model, and that stereotypy and anxiety may involve separate but interacting circuits.
claims.limO: The conclusion that the circuits are separate rests on this null, and it carries no test statistic, no effect size, no confidence interval and no power analysis; a drug effect on microstructure smaller than the study could detect would produce the same result. No dose or duration for diazepam is given in the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3B knockout mice; acute restraint stress model
claims.measure: self-grooming microstructure by grooming analysis algorithm, cephalo-caudal progression; total grooming duration; anxiety measures

claims.text: Shank3B knockout mice, acute stress mice and chronic pain mice show distinct self-grooming microstructures despite all three showing elevated anxiety.
claims.limA: The authors propose that stereotypy and anxiety are supported by separate but interacting circuits.
claims.limO: No effect sizes, confidence intervals or animal numbers are reported, and the three models are not stated to have been run contemporaneously or counterbalanced.
claims.model: Shank3B knockout mice; acute restraint stress model; chronic inflammatory pain model
claims.measure: self-grooming microstructure, cephalo-caudal progression, by grooming analysis algorithm

claims.text: Mice lacking RICH2, a Rho-GAP identified as a SHANK3 interaction partner at the postsynaptic density, show fear of novel objects, increased stereotypic behaviour, impaired motor learning, increased multiple spine synapses in hippocampus and cerebellum, and disinhibition of synaptic RAC1 in vivo.
claims.limA: The authors propose that a disintegrated SHANK3/RICH2 complex might at least in part be responsible for abnormal spine formation in ASD, phrasing the link to SHANK3 as a possibility.
claims.limO: SHANK3 itself is not measured or manipulated in this study; the connection is the previously reported protein interaction. The enlarged-spine phenotype runs opposite in direction to the reduced spine density reported in SHANK3 patient-derived neurons, so the record should not be read as a model of SHANK3 loss. No animal numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals are reported.
claims.model: RICH2 knockout mouse; Shank3 not manipulated
claims.measure: novel object fear; stereotypic behaviour; motor learning; spine synapse number; receptor composition; actin polymerisation; synaptic RAC1 activity

claims.text: In the striatum of adult BTBR mice, a model of idiopathic autism, expression changed for a set of synaptic and plasticity genes that includes Shank3, alongside raised mGlu5 receptor expression and mGlu5-mediated polyphosphoinositide hydrolysis.
claims.limA: The authors present the findings as supporting a role for mGlu5 abnormalities in adult idiopathic ASD and as unveiling potential targets.
claims.limO: Shank3 appears inside a list of regulated genes with no direction, magnitude, statistic or confidence interval given for it specifically. Doses and durations for MTEP, MK-801 and ketamine are not reported in the abstract.
claims.model: BTBR mice, a model of idiopathic autism; Shank3 not manipulated
claims.measure: qPCR and western blot for mRNA and protein; in vivo polyphosphoinositide hydrolysis; self-grooming and social interaction

claims.text: The statement that clinical trials of mGlu5 receptor antagonists in fragile X syndrome showed no beneficial effects is background cited by this study, not a result it reports.
claims.limA: The authors cite the trial failures as motivation for studying idiopathic rather than monogenic ASD models.
claims.limO: No trial is identified, no effect estimate is given and no primary source is recoverable from the abstract. This record must never be cited as evidence about mGlu5 antagonists; the primary trial reports are the source for that, per the protocol rule that a secondary mention is never the source of a claim.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: none in this study

claims.text: Re-expression of Shank3 in adult conditional knock-in mice improved synaptic protein composition, spine density and neural function in the striatum.
claims.limA: The authors frame the work as showing a certain degree of continued plasticity in the adult diseased brain.
claims.limO: No animal numbers, effect sizes or confidence intervals are available from the abstract, and it is not stated whether the restored measures reached wild-type levels or merely moved towards them. Conditional re-expression restores the gene globally and instantly, which no human intervention would.
claims.model: novel Shank3 conditional knock-in mouse allowing adult re-expression of Shank3
claims.measure: synaptic protein composition; spine density; striatal neural function

claims.text: Adult re-expression of Shank3 rescued social interaction deficits and repetitive grooming behaviour in Shank3 conditional knock-in mice.
claims.limA: The authors describe the rescue as applying to certain behavioural abnormalities, explicitly not to all.
claims.limO: Whether rescue was complete or partial is not stated, and no effect sizes or confidence intervals are given. Grooming and social interaction in mice are not the endpoints a human trial would use, so the translational step is not supplied by this record.
claims.model: Shank3 conditional knock-in mouse with adult re-expression
claims.measure: social interaction; repetitive grooming

claims.text: Anxiety and motor coordination deficits were not recovered by adult re-expression of Shank3 in Shank3 conditional knock-in mice.
claims.limA: The authors contrast the rescued and unrescued domains and conclude that plasticity in the adult diseased brain is partial.
claims.limO: No test statistic, no effect size, no confidence interval and no power analysis accompanies either null, and no animal numbers are reported. A rescue smaller than the study could detect would look identical, so this is not evidence that anxiety and motor coordination are irreversible; it is evidence that no recovery was detected in this design. The asymmetry with the rescued behaviours is also untested: no interaction between behavioural domain and rescue is reported.
claims.model: Shank3 conditional knock-in mouse with adult re-expression
claims.measure: anxiety-like behaviour; motor coordination

claims.text: Densities of parvalbumin- and somatostatin-positive interneurons did not differ between adult Shank3-overexpressing transgenic mice and wild-type mice in medial prefrontal cortex, striatum or hippocampus.
claims.limO: No sample size, no statistical test, no power calculation and no confidence interval in the abstract. A null stated as 'no significant difference' without numbers is a failure to detect, not demonstrated equivalence.
claims.model: Shank3-overexpressing transgenic mouse (manic model); construct not specified in the abstract
claims.measure: density of parvalbumin- and somatostatin-positive interneurons, immunohistochemistry

claims.text: GAD65 and GAD67 mRNA levels were decreased in adult Shank3-overexpressing mice, while in juveniles only hippocampal GAD65 was reduced and no behavioural hyperactivity was present.
claims.limO: No n, no test statistics and no effect sizes in the abstract. The age comparison is between separate groups, so the developmental claim rests on a cross-sectional contrast.
claims.model: Shank3-overexpressing transgenic mouse
claims.measure: GAD65 and GAD67 mRNA, and protein levels

claims.text: No significant differences in allele, genotype or haplotype frequencies of ten SHANK3 variants were found between people with bipolar disorder and controls.
claims.n: 1482 individuals with or without bipolar disorder
claims.limO: No power calculation and no confidence interval, but with 1482 individuals this is a better-powered null than almost anything else in the corpus. The abstract gives no group sizes or minor allele frequencies, so the detectable effect cannot be reconstructed.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: genotyping of ten SHANK3 variants

claims.text: Peripheral SHANK3 mRNA expression did not differ between people with bipolar disorder and healthy controls.
claims.limO: The subset size for the expression analysis is not given, so this null is uninterpretable as to power. No test, no interval.
claims.model: not_applicable
claims.measure: peripheral SHANK3 mRNA expression

claims.text: The number of immature neurons and radial glial progenitor cells was substantially decreased in the ventral hippocampus of Shank3+/dC mice.
claims.limO: No n and no statistics in the abstract.
claims.model: Shank3+/dC transgenic (heterozygous, C-terminal deletion)
claims.measure: number of immature neurons and radial glial progenitor cells

claims.text: No consistent differences in the number or size of astrocytes or microglia were detected in hippocampus, medial prefrontal cortex or striatum of Shank3+/dC mice.
claims.limO: No power calculation, no confidence interval, no test statistic. 'No consistent differences' is a particularly weak formulation: it does not say whether any individual comparison reached significance.
claims.model: Shank3+/dC transgenic
claims.measure: number and size of astrocytes and microglia

claims.text: Introducing the human SHANK3 S685 missense variant into mice reproduced only a small subset of the phenotypes seen in constitutive Shank3 knockout mice.
claims.limO: Which knockout phenotypes failed to appear is not enumerated in the abstract, so the size of the 'small subset' cannot be judged. No n, no statistics.
claims.model: knock-in of the human ASD-linked SHANK3 S685 missense variant
